title.zh: 卷三百〇九 列傳第一百九十七 流賊 李自成 張獻忠
title.en: Volume 309 Biographies 197: Traitors: Li Zicheng, Zhang Xianzhong
title.raw: 卷三百〇九 列傳第一百九十七 流賊 李自成 張獻忠 Volume 309 Biographies 197: Traitors: Li Zicheng, Zhang Xianzhong

sentences.zh: 李自成 張獻忠

translations.literal: Li Zicheng, Zhang Xianzhong
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong

sentences.zh: 盜賊之禍，歷代恒有，至明末李自成、張獻忠極矣。

translations.literal: The calamity of banditry has existed in every age; by the late Ming, Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong brought it to its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry has plagued every dynasty, but in the late Ming it reached its zenith with Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 史冊所載，未有若斯之酷者也。

translations.literal: In what the historical records contain, there has never been cruelty such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing recorded in the annals of history approaches their savagery.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，唐賽兒倡亂山東。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign, Tang Sai'er raised rebellion in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, Tang Sai'er led a rebellion in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 厥後乘瑕弄兵，頻見竊發，然皆旋就撲滅。

translations.literal: Afterward, seizing openings to wield arms, raids were frequently seen breaking out, yet all were soon suppressed and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, rebels seized every opening to take up arms, and uprisings broke out again and again, but each was swiftly crushed.

sentences.zh: 惟武宗之世，流寇蔓延，幾危宗社，而卒以掃除。

translations.literal: Only in the age of Emperor Wuzong did roaming bandits spread widely, nearly endangering the imperial altars, yet in the end they were swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Emperor Wuzong did roaming bandits spread so widely that they nearly toppled the dynasty, yet they were ultimately swept away.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝勵精有為，視武宗何啻天壤，而顧失天下，何也？

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanglie exerted himself with vigor and achievement; compared with Wuzong, how could they be less than heaven and earth apart—yet he lost the realm. Why?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chongzhen strove with energy and purpose, worlds apart from the feckless Wuzong—yet he lost the empire. Why?

sentences.zh: 明興百年，朝廷之綱紀既肅，天下之風俗未澆。

translations.literal: A century after the rise of Ming, the court's statutes were already strict, and the customs of the realm were not yet diluted.
translations.idiomatic: A century after the founding of the Ming, court discipline was firm and public morals had not yet decayed.

sentences.zh: 孝宗選舉賢能，布列中外，與斯民休養生息者十餘年，仁澤深而人心固，元氣盛而國脈安。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong selected the worthy and able, deploying them within and without; he rested the people and let them recover for more than ten years. Benevolence ran deep and hearts were firm; vital energy flourished and the nation's pulse was secure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hongzhi appointed worthy men throughout the realm and gave the people more than a decade to recover. His benevolence ran deep, loyalty held firm, and the dynasty's vital energy remained strong.

sentences.zh: 雖以武之童昏，亟行稗政，中官幸夫，濁亂左右，而本根尚未盡拔，宰輔亦多老成。

translations.literal: Although under Wuzong's childish folly wicked policies were urgently pursued, eunuchs and favorites muddied and disturbed those around him, the root was not yet entirely uprooted, and many chief ministers were seasoned men.
translations.idiomatic: Even under the childish Wuzong, who pursued reckless policies while eunuchs and favorites corrupted the court, the dynasty's roots had not yet been torn up, and many senior ministers remained men of experience.

sentences.zh: 迨盜賊四起，王瓊獨典中樞，陸完、彭澤分任閫帥，委寄既專，旁撓絕少，以故危而不亡。

translations.literal: When bandits rose on all sides, Wang Qiong alone held the central pivot; Lu Wan and Peng Ze separately bore frontier command. Entrustment was already concentrated, interference from the side was very little—thus peril without perishing.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose on every side, Wang Qiong held sole authority at court while Lu Wan and Peng Ze commanded the frontiers. Power was concentrated and interference minimal, which is why the dynasty teetered but did not fall.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝承神、熹之後，神宗怠荒棄政，熹宗暱近閹人，元氣盡澌，國脈垂絕。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanglie succeeded after Shenzong and Xizong. Shenzong was idle and abandoned governance; Xizong was intimate with eunuchs close at hand. Vital energy was entirely drained; the nation's pulse hung by a thread.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen inherited the throne after the Wanli and Tianqi emperors. Wanli had neglected government, Tianqi had favored eunuchs, and by then the dynasty's vital energy was spent and its life thread all but severed.

sentences.zh: 向使熹宗禦宇復延數載，則天下之亡不再傳矣。

translations.literal: If Xizong's reign over the realm had extended several more years, then the realm's fall would not have waited another generation.
translations.idiomatic: Had Tianqi's reign lasted only a few years longer, the empire would have fallen before Chongzhen ever took the throne.

sentences.zh: 莊烈之繼統也，臣僚之党局已成，草野之物力已耗，國家之法令已壞，邊疆之搶攘已甚。

translations.literal: When Zhuanglie succeeded to the throne, factional alignments among officials were already formed, material strength in the countryside was already exhausted, the state's laws and orders were already broken, and frontier turmoil was already severe.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Chongzhen ascended the throne, official factions were entrenched, the countryside was exhausted, laws lay in ruins, and the frontiers were in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 莊烈雖銳意更始，治核名實，而人才之賢否，議論之是非，政事之得失，軍機之成敗，未能灼見於中，不搖於外也。

translations.literal: Although Zhuanglie was keen to renew beginnings and govern by verifying names and realities, whether talent was worthy or not, whether discourse was right or wrong, whether administration gained or lost, whether military plans succeeded or failed—he could not see them clearly within and remain unshaken without.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chongzhen was determined to reform and judge men by their deeds, he could not clearly discern who was talented, which policies were sound, which administrations succeeded, or which military plans worked—and he could not hold firm against outside pressures.

sentences.zh: 且性多疑而任察，好剛而尚氣。

translations.literal: Moreover, his nature was much given to suspicion and reliance on scrutiny; he loved hardness and esteemed temper.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he was deeply suspicious and relied on minute scrutiny; he loved to be forceful and prized his own pride.

sentences.zh: 任察則苛刻寡恩，尚氣則急遽失措。

translations.literal: Relying on scrutiny, he was harsh and sparing of grace; esteeming temper, he was hasty and lost composure.
translations.idiomatic: His scrutiny made him harsh and unforgiving; his pride made him rash and prone to misjudgment.

sentences.zh: 當夫群盜滿山，四方鼎沸，而委政柄者非庸即佞，剿撫兩端，茫無成算。

translations.literal: When bandits filled the mountains on every side and the four quarters seethed like a cauldron, those entrusted with power were either mediocre or sycophantic; between suppression and appeasement they wavered, with no settled plan.
translations.idiomatic: While bandits swarmed the hills and the realm seethed on every side, those he entrusted with power were either mediocre or sycophantic, vacillating between suppression and appeasement with no coherent strategy.

sentences.zh: 內外大臣救過不給，人懷規利自全之心。

translations.literal: Ministers within and without could not keep up with remedying faults; each harbored a heart of scheming for profit and self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers at court and in the provinces could barely answer for their own mistakes; everyone schemed for personal gain and self-preservation.

sentences.zh: 言語戇直，切中事弊者，率皆摧折以去。

translations.literal: Those whose words were blunt and straight, striking to the heart of affairs' abuses, were generally broken and driven away.
translations.idiomatic: Those who spoke bluntly and hit the mark on the empire's ills were invariably crushed and driven from office.

sentences.zh: 其所任為閫帥者，事權中制，功過莫償。

translations.literal: Those he appointed as frontier commanders had their authority checked at the center; merit and fault could not be requited.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier generals he appointed had their authority curtailed from the capital, and neither success nor failure could be properly rewarded or punished.

sentences.zh: 敗一方即戮一將，隳一城即殺一吏，賞罰太明而至於不能罰，制馭過嚴而至於不能制。

translations.literal: Lose one region and a general was executed; lose one city and an official was killed. Rewards and punishments were too clear, until punishment could not be applied; control was too strict, until control could not be exercised.
translations.idiomatic: Lose a battle and a general was executed; lose a city and an official was killed. His rewards and punishments were so rigid that in the end he could punish no one, and his control was so severe that in the end he controlled nothing.

sentences.zh: 加以天災流行，饑饉洊臻，政繁賦重，外訌內叛。

translations.literal: Added to this were natural disasters spreading, famine arriving in succession, government affairs numerous and levies heavy, external strife and internal rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On top of all this came natural disasters, repeated famines, burdensome government and crushing taxes, foreign threats and internal rebellion.

sentences.zh: 譬一人之身，元氣羸然，疽毒併發，厥症固已甚危，而醫則良否錯進，劑則寒熱互投，病入膏肓，而無可救，不亡何待哉？

translations.literal: It is like one person's body: vital energy enfeebled, carbuncle poison erupting together—the symptoms are already very dangerous, yet physicians good and bad are admitted in confusion, and prescriptions cold and hot are given in turn. The disease enters the marrow; nothing can save it. If it does not perish, what is there to wait for?
translations.idiomatic: It was like a man whose vital energy was spent, with ulcers erupting everywhere—the illness was already grave, yet good and bad physicians were admitted in turn and hot and cold remedies prescribed at random. The disease reached the marrow with no cure in sight. How could the dynasty not fall?

sentences.zh: 是故明之亡，亡於流賊，而其致亡之本，不在於流賊也。

translations.literal: Therefore Ming's fall was a fall to roaming bandits, yet the root of its bringing-about fall did not lie in roaming bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Ming fell to the bandit armies, but the root cause of its fall lay not in the bandits themselves.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 莊烈非亡國之君，而當亡國之運，又乏救亡之術，徒見其焦勞瞀亂，孑立於上十有七年。

translations.literal: Zhuanglie was not a ruler who should lose a state, yet he met the fate of a state about to fall, and moreover lacked the arts of saving a state about to fall. One only saw him anxious and toiling, confused and disordered, standing alone above for seventeen years.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen was not a ruler destined to lose his kingdom, yet he faced the fate of a dying dynasty without the means to save it. For seventeen years one could only watch him toil in anguish, confused and alone upon the throne.

sentences.zh: 而帷幄不聞良、平之謀，行間未睹李、郭之將，卒致宗社顛覆，徒以身殉，悲夫！

translations.literal: Yet within the curtains one did not hear counsel like Liang and Ping's; in the ranks one did not see generals like Li and Guo. In the end the altars of state were overturned; he could only offer his body in sacrifice. How tragic!
translations.idiomatic: No Zhang Liang or Chen Ping offered counsel from within the tent; no Li Guangbi or Guo Ziyi led armies in the field. In the end the altars of state were overturned, and he could only die with his realm. How tragic!

sentences.zh: 自唐賽兒以下，本末易竟，事具剿賊諸臣傳中。

translations.literal: From Tang Sai'er downward, beginning and end are easy to complete; the affairs are fully set out in the biographies of the various ministers who suppressed bandits.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang Sai'er onward, the full course of events is readily traced in the biographies of the ministers who suppressed the bandits.

sentences.zh: 獨志其亡天下者，立李自成、張獻忠傳。

translations.literal: Only those who recorded the loss of the realm—for them biographies of Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong are established.
translations.idiomatic: For those who brought down the empire, biographies of Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong alone are set forth here.

sentences.zh: 李自成

translations.literal: Li Zicheng
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng

sentences.zh: 李自成，米脂人，世居懷遠堡李繼遷寨。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng was a man of Mizhi, his family dwelling for generations at Li Jiqian's stockade in Huaiyuan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng was a native of Mizhi in Shaanxi, his family having lived for generations at Li Jiqian's stockade in Huaiyuan Fort.

sentences.zh: 父守忠，無子，禱于華山，夢神告曰：「以破軍星為若子。」

translations.literal: His father Shouzhong had no son. He prayed at Mount Hua, and in a dream a god told him: "Take the Broken Army star as your son."
translations.idiomatic: His father Shouzhong, who had no son, prayed at Mount Hua and dreamed that a god told him, "Take the Broken Army star as your son."

sentences.zh: 已，生自成。

translations.literal: Afterward, Zicheng was born.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Zicheng was born.

sentences.zh: 幼牧羊于邑大姓艾氏，及長，充銀川驛卒。

translations.literal: In youth he herded sheep for the Ai clan, a great family of the district. When grown, he served as a courier at Yinchuan post station.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he herded sheep for the Ai clan, a prominent local family. When he came of age, he became a courier at the Yinchuan post station.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，鬥很無賴，數犯法。

translations.literal: He was skilled at riding and archery, fierce and unruly, and repeatedly broke the law.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at riding and archery, fierce and unruly, and repeatedly ran afoul of the law.

sentences.zh: 知縣晏子賓捕之，將置諸死，脫去為屠。

translations.literal: Magistrate Yan Zibin arrested him and was about to put him to death, but he escaped and became a butcher.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Yan Zibin arrested him and was about to execute him, but he escaped and became a butcher.

sentences.zh: 天啟末，魏忠賢党喬應甲為陝西巡撫，硃童蒙為延綏巡撫，貪黷不詰盜，盜由是始。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianqi, Wei Zhongxian's faction member Qiao Yingjia was Shaanxi governor and Zhu Tongmeng was Yan-sui governor. Greedy and corrupt, they did not pursue bandits, and banditry began from this.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianqi reign, Qiao Yingjia of Wei Zhongxian's faction became governor of Shaanxi and Zhu Tongmeng governor of Yan-sui. Corrupt and negligent, they failed to suppress banditry, and from this the troubles began.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，陝西大饑，延綏缺餉，固原兵劫州庫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen, Shaanxi suffered great famine. Yan-sui lacked pay, and the troops at Guyuan raided the prefectural treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen, Shaanxi suffered a great famine. Yan-sui troops went unpaid, and soldiers at Guyuan raided the prefectural treasury.

sentences.zh: 白水賊王二，府谷賊王嘉胤，宜川賊王左掛、飛山虎、大紅狼等，一時並起。

translations.literal: The Baishui bandit Wang Er, the Fugu bandit Wang Jiayin, the Yichuan bandits Wang Zuogua, Feishanhu, Dahonglang, and others—all rose at once.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits Wang Er of Baishui, Wang Jiayin of Fugu, and Wang Zuogua, Feishanhu, and Dahonglang of Yichuan all rose at once.

sentences.zh: 有安塞馬賊高迎祥者，自成舅也，與饑民王大樑聚眾應之。

translations.literal: There was the Ansai horse bandit Gao Yingxiang, Zicheng's maternal uncle, who with the famine refugee Wang Daliang gathered a host and responded.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was the horse bandit Gao Yingxiang of Ansai, Zicheng's uncle, who with the famine refugee Wang Daliang raised a following and joined the uprising.

sentences.zh: 迎祥自稱闖王，大樑自稱大樑王。

translations.literal: Yingxiang styled himself King Who Charges; Daliang styled himself King Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiang styled himself the Dashing King; Daliang styled himself King Daliang.

sentences.zh: 二年春，詔以楊鶴為三邊總督，捕之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, an edict appointed Yang He as Three Frontiers supreme commander to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year, Yang He was appointed supreme commander of the Three Frontiers with orders to capture them.

sentences.zh: 參政劉應遇擊斬王二、王大樑，參政洪承疇擊破王左掛，賊稍稍懼。

translations.literal: Vice commissioner Liu Yingyu attacked and beheaded Wang Er and Wang Daliang; vice commissioner Hong Chengchou defeated Wang Zuogua, and the bandits grew somewhat fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commissioner Liu Yingyu attacked and killed Wang Er and Wang Daliang; vice commissioner Hong Chengchou defeated Wang Zuogua, and the bandits began to grow fearful.

sentences.zh: 會京師戒嚴，山西巡撫耿如𣏌勤王兵嘩而西，延綏總兵吳自勉、甘肅巡撫梅之煥勤王兵亦潰，與群盜合。

translations.literal: When the capital declared martial alert, Shanxi governor Geng Rubian's troops sent to aid the throne mutinied and went west; Yan-sui commander Wu Zimian and Gansu governor Mei Zhihuan's relief troops also broke and joined the mass of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital declared martial law, the relief troops of Shanxi governor Geng Rubian mutinied and marched west; the relief forces of Yan-sui commander Wu Zimian and Gansu governor Mei Zhihuan also broke and joined the bandits.

sentences.zh: 延綏巡撫張夢鯨恚死，承疇代之，召故總兵杜文煥督延綏、固原兵，便宜剿賊。

translations.literal: Yan-sui governor Zhang Mengjing died of rage; Chengchou replaced him. The former commander Du Wenhuan was summoned to direct Yan-sui and Guyuan troops with discretionary authority to suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yan-sui governor Zhang Mengjing died of despair; Chengchou replaced him. Former commander Du Wenhuan was recalled to direct the Yan-sui and Guyuan troops with full authority to suppress the bandits.

sentences.zh: 三年，王左掛、王子順、苗美等戰屢敗，乞降。

translations.literal: In the third year, Wang Zuogua, Wang Zishun, Miao Mei, and others were repeatedly defeated in battle and begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Wang Zuogua, Wang Zishun, Miao Mei, and others were repeatedly defeated and begged to surrender.

sentences.zh: 而王嘉胤掠延安、慶陽間，楊鶴撫之，不聽，從神木渡河犯山西。

translations.literal: But Wang Jiayin raided between Yan'an and Qingyang. Yang He tried to appease him, but he would not listen; crossing the Yellow River at Shenmu, he invaded Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: But Wang Jiayin raided between Yan'an and Qingyang. Yang He tried to appease him, but he refused and crossed the Yellow River at Shenmu to invade Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 是時，秦地所征曰新餉，曰均輸，曰間架，其目日增，吏因緣為奸，民大困。

translations.literal: At this time, what Qin territory levied was called new military provisions, called equalized transport, called tiered housing tax—the categories daily increased, and officials used the opportunity for wickedness. The people were greatly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the levies in Shaanxi multiplied—new military tax, transport equalization, housing surtax—with categories growing daily while officials exploited the system. The people were driven to desperation.

sentences.zh: 以給事中劉懋議，裁驛站，山、陝遊民仰驛糈者，無所得食，俱從賊，賊轉盛。

translations.literal: On the proposal of supervising secretary Liu Mao, post stations were cut. Vagrant people in Shan and Shaan who relied on post-station grain had nothing to eat and all followed the bandits; the bandits grew still stronger.
translations.idiomatic: On the proposal of supervising secretary Liu Mao, post stations were abolished. Vagrants in Shaanxi and Shanxi who had depended on post-station rations lost their livelihood and joined the bandits, who grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 兵部郎中李繼貞奏曰：「延民饑，將盡為盜，請以帑金十萬振之。」

translations.literal: Ministry of War director Li Jizhen memorialized: "The people of Yan are starving and will all become bandits. I request one hundred thousand taels from the treasury to relieve them."
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of War director Li Jizhen memorialized: "The people of Yan-sui are starving and will all become bandits. I request one hundred thousand taels from the treasury for relief."

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 而嘉胤已襲破黃甫川、清水、木瓜三堡，陷府谷、河曲。

translations.literal: But Jiayin had already raided and taken Huangfuchuan, Qingshui, and Mugua forts, and captured Fugu and Hequ.
translations.idiomatic: But Jiayin had already stormed the forts of Huangfuchuan, Qingshui, and Mugua and captured Fugu and Hequ.

sentences.zh: 又有神一元、不沾泥、可天飛、郝臨庵、紅軍友、點燈子、李老柴、混天猴、獨行狼諸賊，所在蜂起，或掠秦，或東入晉，屠陷城堡。

translations.literal: There were also the bandits Shen Yiyuan, Buzhanni, Ketianfei, Hao Lin'an, Hongjunyou, Dian Dengzi, Li Laochai, Huntianhou, Duxinglang, and others—rising like bees everywhere, some raiding Qin, some entering Jin to the east, slaughtering and taking castles.
translations.idiomatic: Other bandits—Shen Yiyuan, Buzhanni, Ketianfei, Hao Lin'an, Hongjunyou, Lamp-Lighter, Li Laochai, Heaven-Stirring Monkey, Lone Wolf, and others—rose everywhere, some raiding Shaanxi, some pushing east into Shanxi, slaughtering and capturing walled towns.

sentences.zh: 官兵東西奔擊，賊或降或死，旋滅旋熾。

translations.literal: Government troops struck east and west in pursuit; bandits either surrendered or died, yet as soon as they were extinguished they flared again.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops struck in every direction; bandits surrendered or were killed, yet as soon as one group was destroyed another rose.

sentences.zh: 延安賊張獻忠亦聚眾據十八寨，稱八大王。

translations.literal: The Yan'an bandit Zhang Xianzhong also gathered a host and held eighteen stockades, styling himself the Eighth Great King.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan'an bandit Zhang Xianzhong also gathered followers, seized eighteen stockades, and styled himself the Eighth Great King.

sentences.zh: 四年，孤山副將曹文詔破賊河曲，王嘉胤遁去。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Gushan vice commander Cao Wenzhao defeated the bandits at Hequ, and Wang Jiayin fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, vice commander Cao Wenzhao of Gushan defeated the bandits at Hequ, and Wang Jiayin fled.

sentences.zh: 已，復自岳陽突犯澤、潞，為左右所殺，其党共推王自用號紫金梁者為魁。

translations.literal: Afterward, he again burst from Yueyang to raid Ze and Lu, and was killed by those at his side. His faction jointly elevated as leader Wang Ziyong, styled Purple-Gold Beam.
translations.idiomatic: He later burst from Yueyang to raid Zezhou and Lu'an, where his own men killed him. His followers elevated Wang Ziyong, styled Purple-Gold Beam, as their leader.

sentences.zh: 自用結群賊老回回、曹操、八金剛、掃地王、射塌天、閻正虎、滿天星、破甲錐、刑紅狼、上天老、蠍子塊、過天星、混世王等及迎祥、獻忠共三十六營，眾二十余萬，聚山西。

translations.literal: Ziyong joined the mass of bandits—Old Huihui, Cao Cao, Eight Vajras, Sweeping-Earth King, Shooting-Sky Collapser, Yan Zhenghu, Full Sky of Stars, Armor-Breaking Awl, Punishment Red Wolf, Heaven-Ascending Elder, Scorpion Lump, Crossing Heaven Star, World-Mixing King, and others—together with Yingxiang and Xianzhong in thirty-six camps, more than two hundred thousand strong, gathering in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong allied with Old Huihui, Cao Cao, Eight Vajras, Sweeping-Earth King, Shooting-Sky Collapser, Yan Zhenghu, Full Sky of Stars, Armor-Breaking Awl, Punishment Red Wolf, Heaven-Ascending Elder, Scorpion Lump, Crossing Heaven Star, World-Mixing King, and others, together with Yingxiang and Xianzhong—thirty-six camps totaling more than two hundred thousand men gathered in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 自成乃與兄子過往從迎祥，與獻忠等合，號闖將，未有名。

translations.literal: Zicheng then followed Yingxiang with his nephew Guo, joined with Xianzhong and the rest, and was styled Dashing General—he had not yet made a name.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng followed Yingxiang with his nephew Guo, joined forces with Xianzhong and the others, and was styled the Dashing General, though he had not yet made a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 楊鶴撫賊不效被逮，洪承疇代鶴，張福臻代承疇，督諸將曹文詔、楊嘉謨剿賊，所向克捷，陝地略定。

translations.literal: Yang He's appeasement of bandits was ineffective and he was arrested. Hong Chengchou replaced He; Zhang Fuzhen replaced Chengchou. They directed the various generals Cao Wenzhao and Yang Jiamo to suppress bandits; wherever they went they prevailed, and Shaanxi territory was largely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yang He's appeasement policy failed and he was arrested. Hong Chengchou replaced him, then Zhang Fuzhen replaced Chengchou. They directed generals Cao Wenzhao and Yang Jiamo against the bandits, who met success wherever they marched, and Shaanxi was largely pacified.

sentences.zh: 而山西賊大盛，剽掠甯鄉、石樓、稷山、聞喜、河津間。

translations.literal: But the Shanxi bandits grew greatly strong, plundering between Ningxiang, Shilou, Jishan, Wenxi, and Hejin.
translations.idiomatic: But the Shanxi bandits grew stronger still, plundering Ningxiang, Shilou, Jishan, Wenxi, Hejin, and the surrounding region.

sentences.zh: 五年，賊分道四出，連陷大寧、隰州、澤州、壽陽諸州縣，全晉震動。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the bandits divided into four routes and went forth, successively taking Daning, Xi Prefecture, Ze Prefecture, Shouyang, and other prefectures and counties. All Jin was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the bandits split into four columns and overran Daning, Xi Prefecture, Zezhou, Shouyang, and other prefectures and counties, throwing all of Shanxi into alarm.

sentences.zh: 乃罷巡撫宋統殷，以許鼎臣代之，與宣大總督張宗衡分督諸將。

translations.literal: Governor Song Tongyin was dismissed and Xu Dingchen replaced him; together with Xuan-Da supreme commander Zhang Zongheng they divided command of the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Song Tongyin was dismissed and replaced by Xu Dingchen, who with Xuan-Da supreme commander Zhang Zongheng divided command of the generals.

sentences.zh: 宗衡督虎在威、駕人龍、左良玉等兵八千人，駐平陽，責以平陽、澤、潞四十一州縣。

translations.literal: Zongheng directed the troops of Hu Zaiwei, Jia Renlong, Zuo Liangyu, and others—eight thousand men—stationed at Pingyang, charged with forty-one prefectures and counties of Pingyang, Ze, and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Zongheng commanded eight thousand troops under Hu Zaiwei, Jia Renlong, Zuo Liangyu, and others, stationed at Pingyang with responsibility for forty-one prefectures and counties in the Pingyang, Zezhou, and Lu'an region.

sentences.zh: 鼎臣督張應昌、頗希牧、艾萬年兵七千人，駐汾州，責以汾、太、沁遼三十八州縣。

translations.literal: Dingchen directed the troops of Zhang Yingchang, Po Ximu, and Ai Wannian—seven thousand men—stationed at Fen Prefecture, charged with thirty-eight prefectures and counties of Fen, Tai, Qin, and Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Dingchen commanded seven thousand troops under Zhang Yingchang, Po Ximu, and Ai Wannian, stationed at Fenzhou with responsibility for thirty-eight prefectures and counties in the Fen, Taiyuan, Qinzhou, and Liaozhou region.

sentences.zh: 賊亦轉入磨盤山，分眾為三：閻正虎據交城、文水，窺太原；

translations.literal: The bandits also shifted to Millstone Mountain and divided their host into three: Yan Zhenghu held Jiaocheng and Wenshui, watching Taiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: The bandits also shifted to Millstone Mountain and divided into three columns: Yan Zhenghu held Jiaocheng and Wenshui, threatening Taiyuan;

sentences.zh: 邢紅狼、上天龍據吳城，窺汾州；

translations.literal: Xing Honglang and Shang Tianlong held Wucheng, watching Fen Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Xing Honglang and Shang Tianlong held Wucheng, threatening Fenzhou;

sentences.zh: 自用、獻忠突沁州、武鄉，陷遼州。

translations.literal: Ziyong and Xianzhong burst into Qin Prefecture and Wuxiang and took Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong and Xianzhong struck Qinzhou and Wuxiang and captured Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 六年春，官兵共進力擊。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, government troops jointly advanced and struck with full force.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year, government troops advanced in concert and struck with full force.

sentences.zh: 自用懼，乞降於故錦衣僉事張道浚。

translations.literal: Ziyong was afraid and begged to surrender to the former Embroidered Uniform Guard assistant commissioner Zhang Daojun.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong grew fearful and offered to surrender to the former Embroidered Uniform Guard commissioner Zhang Daojun.

sentences.zh: 約未定，陽和兵襲之。

translations.literal: The agreement was not yet settled when Yanghe troops raided them.
translations.idiomatic: Before terms were settled, Yanghe troops attacked them.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，敗約去。

translations.literal: The bandits were enraged, broke the agreement, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the bandits broke off negotiations and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會總兵官曹文詔率陝西兵至，偕諸將猛如虎、虎大威、頗希牧、艾萬年、張應昌等合剿，屢戰皆大克，前後殺混世王、滿天星、姬關鎖、翻山動，掌世王、顯道神等，破自用、獻忠、老回回、蠍子塊、掃地王諸賊。

translations.literal: When supreme commander Cao Wenzhao arrived leading Shaanxi troops, together with the generals Meng Ruhu, Hu Dawei, Po Ximu, Ai Wannian, Zhang Yingchang, and others he jointly suppressed them. Battle after battle was greatly won; before and after they killed World-Mixing King, Full Sky of Stars, Ji Guansuo, Overturning Mountain Shake, Palm World King, Manifest Way God, and others, and defeated the bandits Ziyong, Xianzhong, Old Huihui, Scorpion Lump, and Sweeping-Earth King.
translations.idiomatic: When supreme commander Cao Wenzhao arrived with Shaanxi troops and joined generals Meng Ruhu, Hu Dawei, Po Ximu, Ai Wannian, Zhang Yingchang, and others in a joint campaign, victory followed victory. They killed World-Mixing King, Full Sky of Stars, Ji Guansuo, Overturning Mountain Shake, Palm World King, Manifest Way God, and others, and defeated Ziyong, Xianzhong, Old Huihui, Scorpion Lump, and Sweeping-Earth King.

sentences.zh: 其後，自用又為川將鄧玘射殺之。

translations.literal: Afterward, Ziyong was again shot and killed by Sichuan commander Deng Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ziyong was shot and killed by Sichuan commander Deng Qi.

sentences.zh: 山西三大盜俱敗。

translations.literal: The three great bandits of Shanxi were all defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The three great Shanxi bandit leaders were all defeated.

sentences.zh: 初，賊之破澤州也，分其眾，南逾太行，掠濟源、清化、修武，圍懷慶。

translations.literal: At first, when the bandits took Ze Prefecture, they divided their host, crossed the Taihang southward, raided Jiyuan, Qinghua, and Xiuwu, and besieged Huaiqing.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits first took Zezhou, they split their forces, crossed the Taihang Mountains southward, raided Jiyuan, Qinghua, and Xiuwu, and besieged Huaiqing.

sentences.zh: 官軍擊之，賊遁走。

translations.literal: Government troops struck them, and the bandits fled.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops attacked and the bandits fled.

sentences.zh: 別賊復闌入西山，大掠順德、真定間。

translations.literal: Other bandits again forced their way into the Western Hills and greatly plundered between Shunde and Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Other bandits forced their way into the Western Hills and plundered widely between Shunde and Zhending.

sentences.zh: 大名道盧象升力戰劫賊。

translations.literal: Daming circuit intendant Lu Xiangsheng fought fiercely and seized back the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Daming circuit intendant Lu Xiangsheng fought fiercely against the raiding bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊自邢臺摩天嶺西下，抵武安，敗總兵左良玉，河北三府焚劫殆遍。

translations.literal: The bandits came down west from Motian Ridge at Xingtai, reached Wu'an, defeated commander Zuo Liangyu, and the three prefectures of Hebei were burned and plundered nearly throughout.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits descended west from Motian Ridge at Xingtai, reached Wu'an, defeated commander Zuo Liangyu, and burned and plundered nearly all of the three Hebei prefectures.

sentences.zh: 潞王上疏告急，兼請衛鳳、泗陵寢。

translations.literal: Prince of Lu memorialized in urgent alarm, also requesting guards for the Feng and Si imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu memorialized in urgent alarm and also requested guards for the imperial tombs at Feng and Si.

sentences.zh: 詔特遣總兵倪寵、王朴率京營兵六千人，與諸將並進。

translations.literal: An edict specially dispatched commanders Ni Chong and Wang Pu leading six thousand capital camp troops to advance together with the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially dispatched commanders Ni Chong and Wang Pu with six thousand capital camp troops to advance together with the other generals.

sentences.zh: 賊聞之，欲從河內走太行。

translations.literal: The bandits heard this and wished to go from Henei through the Taihang.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the bandits planned to flee from Henei through the Taihang Mountains.

sentences.zh: 文詔邀擊之，不敢進。

translations.literal: Wenzhao intercepted and struck them; they dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao intercepted them and they dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 賊之敗於山西者，亦奔河北合營，迎祥、自成、獻忠、曹操、老回回等俱至。

translations.literal: The bandits defeated in Shanxi also fled to Hebei and joined camps; Yingxiang, Zicheng, Xianzhong, Cao Cao, Old Huihui, and others all arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits defeated in Shanxi also fled to Hebei to join the main force; Yingxiang, Zicheng, Xianzhong, Cao Cao, Old Huihui, and others all arrived.

sentences.zh: 京兵蹙其後，左良玉，湯九州等扼其前，連戰於青店、石岡、石坡、牛尾、柳泉、猛虎村，屢敗之。

translations.literal: Capital troops pressed their rear; Zuo Liangyu, Tang Jiuzhou, and others blocked their front. Battles followed at Qingdian, Shigang, Shipo, Niwei, Liuquan, and Menghu Village, repeatedly defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Capital troops pressed from the rear while Zuo Liangyu, Tang Jiuzhou, and others blocked the front. Battles at Qingdian, Shigang, Shipo, Niwei, Liuquan, and Menghu Village repeatedly defeated them.

sentences.zh: 賊欲逸，阻於河，大困。

translations.literal: The bandits wished to escape but were blocked by the river and were greatly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits tried to escape but were trapped by the river and fell into desperate straits.

sentences.zh: 賊素畏文詔、道浚，道浚先坐事遣戍，文詔轉戰秦、晉、河北，遇賊輒大克，御史復劾其驕倨，調大同總兵去。

translations.literal: The bandits had always feared Wenzhao and Daojun. Daojun had earlier been implicated in an affair and sent to frontier service; Wenzhao fought across Qin, Jin, and Hebei, meeting bandits and always winning greatly. Censors again impeached him for arrogance, and he was transferred away as Datong commander.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits had always feared Wenzhao and Daojun. Daojun had earlier been banished for misconduct; Wenzhao fought across Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Hebei, defeating the bandits wherever he met them. Censors impeached him for arrogance and he was transferred to command at Datong.

sentences.zh: 賊遂詭辭乞降，監軍太監楊進朝信之，為入奏。

translations.literal: The bandits then used deceitful words to beg surrender. Supervising eunuch Yang Jinchao believed them and entered a memorial on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then feigned surrender. Supervising eunuch Yang Jinchao believed them and memorialized the throne on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 會天寒河冰合，賊突從毛家寨策馬徑渡。

translations.literal: When the weather turned cold the river ice joined, and the bandits suddenly spurred their horses straight across from Maojia Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: When cold weather froze the river, the bandits suddenly galloped across from Maojia Stockade.

sentences.zh: 河南諸軍無扼河者，賊遂連陷澠池、伊陽、盧氏三縣。

translations.literal: Henan troops had none to block the river; the bandits then successively took Mianchi, Yiyang, and Lushi counties.
translations.idiomatic: No Henan troops blocked the crossing, and the bandits successively captured Mianchi, Yiyang, and Lushi.

sentences.zh: 河南巡撫玄默率諸將盛兵待之，賊竄入盧氏山中，由間道直走內鄉，掠鄖陽，又分掠南陽、汝寧，入棗陽、當陽，逼湖廣。

translations.literal: Henan governor Xuan Mo led the various generals with a great host waiting for them. The bandits darted into the Lushi mountains, went by hidden paths straight to Neixiang, raided Yunyang, again divided to raid Nanyang and Runing, entered Zaoyang and Dangyang, and pressed upon Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Henan governor Xuan Mo gathered a large force to await them. The bandits slipped into the Lushi mountains, took hidden paths to Neixiang, raided Yunyang, split to raid Nanyang and Runing, entered Zaoyang and Dangyang, and pressed toward Huguang.

sentences.zh: 巡撫唐暉斂兵守境。

translations.literal: Governor Tang Hui gathered troops and guarded the border.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Tang Hui gathered his troops to guard the border.

sentences.zh: 犯歸、巴、夷陵等處，破夔州，攻廣元，逼四川，所在告急。

translations.literal: They violated Gui, Ba, Yiling, and other places, took Kuizhou, attacked Guangyuan, pressed upon Sichuan—everywhere sent urgent alarms.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Gui, Ba, Yiling, and other places, captured Kuizhou, attacked Guangyuan, and pressed into Sichuan, with urgent alarms arriving from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 七年春，特設山、陝、河南、湖廣、四川總督，專辦賊，以延綏巡撫陳奇瑜為之，以盧象升撫治鄖陽，為奇瑜破賊延水關有威名，而象升曆戰陣知兵也。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, a special post of governor for Shan, Shaan, Henan, Huguang, and Sichuan was established, devoted solely to bandit affairs, with Yan-sui governor Chen Qiyu appointed to it; Lu Xiangsheng was made pacification commissioner of Yunyang. Qiyu had won fame breaking bandits at Yanshui Pass; Xiangsheng had passed through battle lines and knew warfare.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year a special governor was created for Shaanxi, Shanxi, Henan, Huguang, and Sichuan, devoted solely to suppressing the bandits, with Yan-sui governor Chen Qiyu appointed to the post and Lu Xiangsheng made pacification commissioner of Yunyang. Qiyu had won fame defeating bandits at Yanshui Pass, and Xiangsheng was a seasoned commander who knew warfare.

sentences.zh: 於是奇瑜自均州入，與象升並進，師次烏林關，斬賊數千級。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qiyu entered from Jun Prefecture and advanced together with Xiangsheng. The army halted at Wulin Pass and beheaded several thousand bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu entered from Junzhou and advanced with Xiangsheng. At Wulin Pass they beheaded several thousand bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊走漢南，奇瑜以湖廣不足憂，引兵西擊。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to southern Han. Qiyu judged Huguang not worth worrying about and led troops west to strike.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits fled to southern Han. Qiyu judged Huguang not worth worrying about and led his troops west to attack.

sentences.zh: 始，賊自澠池渡河，高迎祥最強，自成屬焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when the bandits crossed the river from Mianchi, Gao Yingxiang was strongest and Zicheng was subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits first crossed the river at Mianchi, Gao Yingxiang was the strongest leader and Zicheng served under him.

sentences.zh: 及入河南，自成與兄子過結李牟、俞彬、白廣恩、李雙喜、顧君恩、高傑等自為一軍。

translations.literal: When they entered Henan, Zicheng with his nephew Guo joined Li Mou, Yu Bin, Bai Guang'en, Li Shuangxi, Gu Jun'en, Gao Jie, and others to form an army of their own.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Henan, Zicheng and his nephew Guo allied with Li Mou, Yu Bin, Bai Guang'en, Li Shuangxi, Gu Jun'en, Gao Jie, and others to form their own army.

sentences.zh: 過、傑善戰，君恩善謀。

translations.literal: Guo and Jie were skilled at fighting; Jun'en was skilled at stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Guo and Gao Jie excelled in combat; Jun'en excelled in strategy.

sentences.zh: 及奇瑜兵至，獻忠等奔商、雒，自成等陷於興安之車箱峽。

translations.literal: When Qiyu's troops arrived, Xianzhong and others fled to Shang and Luo; Zicheng and the rest were trapped at Chexiang Gorge in Xing'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Qiyu's army arrived, Zhang Xianzhong and others fled toward Shang and Luo, while Li Zicheng and his followers were trapped at Chexiang Gorge in Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 會大雨兩月，馬乏芻多死，弓矢皆脫，自成用君恩計，賄奇瑜左右，詐降。

translations.literal: It happened that heavy rain fell for two months; horses lacked fodder and many died; bows and arrows all came unstrung. Zicheng used Jun'en's plan to bribe those around Qiyu and feign surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains fell for two months. Horses went without fodder and many died; bowstrings rotted and fell slack. Li Zicheng followed Jun'en's counsel, bribing Chen Qiyu's staff and feigning surrender.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜意輕賊，許之，檄諸將按兵毋殺，所過州縣為具糗傳送。

translations.literal: Qiyu took the bandits lightly, assented, and issued orders to the generals to hold their troops and not kill; the prefectures and counties they passed were to prepare dry rations and convey them forward.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qiyu underestimated the rebels, granted their plea, and ordered generals to hold their men back from killing. Every prefecture and county along the route was commanded to supply rations and escort the column forward.

sentences.zh: 賊甫渡棧，即大噪，盡屠所過七州縣。

translations.literal: The bandits had barely crossed the plank road when they raised a great clamor and slaughtered their way through seven prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the rebels crossed the plank roads when they raised a great uproar and massacred every county they passed through—seven in all.

sentences.zh: 而略陽賊數萬亦來會，賊勢愈張。

translations.literal: Moreover tens of thousands of bandits from Lüeyang also came to join them, and the bandit strength grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands more from Lüeyang joined them, and rebel strength swelled further.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜坐削籍，而自成名始著矣。

translations.literal: Qiyu was punished by removal from the register, and from then on Zicheng's fame began to grow.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qiyu was stripped of his official rank; from this point Li Zicheng's reputation began to rise.

sentences.zh: 已，洪承疇代奇瑜，李喬巡撫陝西，吳甡巡撫山西。

translations.literal: Before long Hong Chengchou replaced Qiyu; Li Qiao became grand coordinator of Shaanxi and Wu Shen grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hong Chengchou replaced Chen Qiyu; Li Qiao was appointed grand coordinator of Shaanxi and Wu Shen of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 大學士溫體仁謂甡曰：「流賊癬疥疾，勿憂也。」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wen Tiren said to Shen: "Roaming bandits are like ringworm—do not worry about them."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wen Tiren told Wu Shen, "These roaming rebels are a mere itch—nothing to fret over."

sentences.zh: 未幾，西寧兵變，承疇甫受命而東，聞變遽返。

translations.literal: Not long after, the Xining troops mutinied; Chengchou had just received his commission and was heading east when he heard of the revolt and hurried back.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Xining garrison mutinied. Hong Chengchou had barely taken office and was marching east when word of the uprising sent him racing back.

sentences.zh: 迎祥、自成遂入鞏昌、平涼、臨洮、鳳翔諸府數十州縣。

translations.literal: Yingxiang and Zicheng then entered dozens of prefectures and counties including Gongchang, Pingliang, Lintao, and Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yingxiang and Li Zicheng overran dozens of prefectures and counties including Gongchang, Pingliang, Lintao, and Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 敗賀人龍、張天禮軍，殺固原道陸夢龍。

translations.literal: They defeated the armies of He Renlong and Zhang Tianli, and killed Circuit Intendant of Guyuan Lu Menglong.
translations.idiomatic: They routed the armies of He Renlong and Zhang Tianli and killed Lu Menglong, circuit intendant of Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 圍隴州四十餘日，承疇檄總兵左光先與人龍合擊，大破之。

translations.literal: They besieged Long Prefecture for more than forty days; Chengchou ordered Commander Zuo Guangxian to join He Renlong in a combined attack and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: They besieged Longzhou for more than forty days. Hong Chengchou ordered Commander Zuo Guangxian to join He Renlong in a pincer attack and broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷亦命豫、楚、晉、蜀兵四道入陝，迎祥、自成遂竄入終南山。

translations.literal: At the same time the court also ordered armies from Henan, Huguang, Shanxi, and Sichuan in four columns into Shaanxi; Yingxiang and Zicheng then fled into the Zhongnan Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the court ordered four columns—from Henan, Huguang, Shanxi, and Sichuan—into Shaanxi. Yingxiang and Li Zicheng drove into the Zhongnan Mountains.

sentences.zh: 已而東出，陷陳州、靈寶、汜水、滎陽。

translations.literal: Before long they came out eastward and took Chen Prefecture, Lingbao, Sishui, and Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they burst eastward and seized Chenzhou, Lingbao, Sishui, and Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 聞左良玉將至，移壁梅山、溱水間。

translations.literal: Hearing that Zuo Liangyu was about to arrive, they shifted their camp between Meishan and the Qin River.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zuo Liangyu was closing in, they moved their camp between Meishan and the Qin River.

sentences.zh: 部賊拔上蔡，燒汝寧郛。

translations.literal: A detachment of bandits took Shangcai and burned the outer walls of Runing.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel detachment seized Shangcai and set fire to the suburbs of Runing.

sentences.zh: 乃命承疇出關追賊，與山東巡撫硃大典並力擊，賊偵知之。

translations.literal: Then Chengchou was ordered out of the passes to pursue the bandits; he and Shandong grand coordinator Zhu Dadian struck together with combined force, and the bandits learned of it by espionage.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Hong Chengchou out of the passes to hunt the rebels, joining Shandong grand coordinator Zhu Dadian in a combined pursuit—and the rebels learned of it through their spies.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，大會于滎陽。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year they held a great assembly at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year (1635) they convened a great council at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 老回回、曹操、革裏眼、左金王、改世王、射塌天、橫天王、混十萬、過天星、九條龍、順天王及迎祥、獻忠共十三家七十二營，議拒敵，未決。

translations.literal: Old Huihui, Cao Cao, Leather-Eye, Left Gold King, Alter-World King, Shooting-Sky Collapser, Crossing Heaven King, World-Mixing Myriad, Crossing Heaven Star, Nine Dragons, Compliance Heaven King, and with Yingxiang and Xianzhong—all thirteen houses and seventy-two camps—deliberated on resisting the enemy, without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Old Huihui, Cao Cao, Leather-Eye, Left Gold King, Alter-World King, Shooting-Sky Collapser, Crossing Heaven King, World-Mixing Myriad, Crossing Heaven Star, Nine Dragons, Compliance Heaven King—together with Yingxiang and Zhang Xianzhong—thirteen houses in seventy-two camps debated how to resist government forces and reached no decision.

sentences.zh: 自成進曰：「一夫猶奮，況十萬眾乎！

translations.literal: Zicheng advanced and said: "If a single man will fight desperately, how much more a host of a hundred thousand!
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng spoke up: "If one man will fight to the death, what of a hundred thousand?

sentences.zh: 官兵無能為也。

translations.literal: The government troops can do nothing against us.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops cannot touch us.

sentences.zh: 宜分兵定所向，利鈍聽之天。」

translations.literal: We should divide our forces and fix where each is to go; whether we gain or lose, let Heaven decide."
translations.idiomatic: We should divide the army and set each column's destination—gain or loss, leave it to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「善。」

translations.literal: All said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: All agreed: "Well said."

sentences.zh: 乃議革裏眼、左金王當川、湖兵，橫天王、混十萬當陝兵，曹操、過天星扼河上，迎祥、獻忠及自成等略東方，老回回、九條龍往來策應。

translations.literal: They then resolved that Leather-Eye and Left Gold King should take Sichuan and Huguang troops; Crossing Heaven King and World-Mixing Myriad should take Shaanxi troops; Cao Cao and Crossing Heaven Star should hold the river line; Yingxiang, Xianzhong, and Zicheng with the rest should raid the east; Old Huihui and Nine Dragons would shuttle back and forth in support.
translations.idiomatic: They apportioned the fight: Leather-Eye and Left Gold King against Sichuan and Huguang armies; Crossing Heaven King and World-Mixing Myriad against Shaanxi forces; Cao Cao and Crossing Heaven Star to choke the Yellow River; Yingxiang, Zhang Xianzhong, and Li Zicheng to ravage the east; Old Huihui and Nine Dragons to coordinate between them.

sentences.zh: 陝兵銳，益以謝塌天、改世王。

translations.literal: Shaanxi troops were sharp, so Collapsing Heaven and Alter-World King were added.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shaanxi troops were the toughest foe, Collapsing Heaven and Alter-World King were added to that front.

sentences.zh: 所破城邑，子女玉帛惟均。

translations.literal: In cities they captured, women, jade, and silk were to be divided equally.
translations.idiomatic: In every captured city, booty—women, jade, silks—was to be shared equally.

sentences.zh: 眾如自成言。

translations.literal: The multitude followed Zicheng's words.
translations.idiomatic: The host did as Li Zicheng proposed.

sentences.zh: 先是，南京兵部尚書呂維祺懼賊南犯，請加防鳳陽陵寢，不報。

translations.literal: Earlier, Minister of War at Nanjing Lü Weiqi, fearing the bandits would invade south, requested strengthened defenses for the Fengyang imperial tombs, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Nanjing Minister of War Lü Weiqi, fearing a southern thrust, had begged stronger protection for the Fengyang imperial tombs—but the court never answered.

sentences.zh: 及迎祥、獻忠東下，江北兵單。

translations.literal: When Yingxiang and Xianzhong marched east, troops north of the Yangtze were few.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingxiang and Zhang Xianzhong drove east, defenses north of the Yangtze were thin.

sentences.zh: 固始、霍丘俱失守。

translations.literal: Gushi and Huoqiu both fell.
translations.idiomatic: Gushi and Huoqiu both fell.

sentences.zh: 賊燔壽州，陷潁州，知州尹夢鰲、州判趙士寬戰死，殺故尚書張鶴鳴。

translations.literal: The bandits burned Shou Prefecture, took Ying Prefecture; Prefect Yin Meng'ao and Assistant Prefect Zhao Shikuan died in battle; they killed the former Minister Zhang Heming.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels torched Shouzhou and seized Yingzhou. Prefect Yin Meng'ao and assistant prefect Zhao Shikuan were killed in battle, along with the retired minister Zhang Heming.

sentences.zh: 乘勝陷鳳陽，焚皇陵，留守署正硃國相等皆戰死。

translations.literal: Pressing their victory they took Fengyang, burned the imperial tombs, and the acting custodian Zhu Guoxiang and others all died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Riding momentum they stormed Fengyang and burned the imperial mausoleum. Custodian Zhu Guoxiang and the garrison died to a man.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝素服哭，遣官告廟。

translations.literal: When word arrived, the Emperor put on plain dress and wept, and dispatched officials to announce at the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: When news reached the capital, Chongzhen donned mourning garb and wept, then sent officers to announce the calamity at the ancestral shrines.

sentences.zh: 逮漕運都御史楊一鵬棄市，以硃大典代之，大徵兵討賊。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport Yang Yipeng was arrested and executed in the market; Zhu Dadian replaced him, and troops were greatly levied to attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Grain Transport grand coordinator Yang Yipeng was executed in the marketplace. Zhu Dadian took his post and the court mobilized a massive expedition against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊乃大書幟曰古元真龍皇帝，合樂大飲。

translations.literal: The bandits then wrote large on their banners: "Ancient Primeval True Dragon Emperor," and joined music in great feasting.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels raised banners proclaiming an "Ancient Primeval True Dragon Emperor" and feasted to music.

sentences.zh: 自成從獻忠求皇陵監小閹善鼓吹者，獻忠不與。

translations.literal: Zicheng asked Xianzhong for eunuchs from the imperial tomb who were skilled at music; Xianzhong would not give them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng asked Zhang Xianzhong for eunuchs from the burned tomb who could play court music; Zhang Xianzhong refused.

sentences.zh: 自成怒，偕迎祥西趨歸德，與曹操、過天星合，復入陝西。

translations.literal: Zicheng was angered; with Yingxiang he hurried west toward Guide and joined Cao Cao and Crossing Heaven Star, re-entering Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng flew into a rage. He and Yingxiang sped west to Guide, united with Cao Cao and Crossing Heaven Star, and plunged back into Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 獻忠獨東下廬州。

translations.literal: Xianzhong alone marched east down to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong alone drove east into Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 承疇方馳至汝州，命諸將左良玉、湯九州、尤世威、徐來朝、陳永福、鄧玘、張應昌分扼湖廣、河南、鄖陽諸關隘，召曹文詔為中軍。

translations.literal: Chengchou had just raced to Ruzhou and ordered the generals Zuo Liangyu, Tang Jiuzhou, You Shiwei, Xu Laichao, Chen Yongfu, Deng Qi, and Zhang Yingchang to guard in division the passes of Huguang, Henan, and Yunyang; he summoned Cao Wenzhao as central army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou had just reached Ruzhou and ordered Zuo Liangyu, Tang Jiuzhou, You Shiwei, Xu Laichao, Chen Yongfu, Deng Qi, and Zhang Yingchang to hold the passes of Huguang, Henan, and Yunyang. He summoned Cao Wenzhao to command the center.

sentences.zh: 文詔未至，玘以兵亂死。

translations.literal: Wenzhao had not yet arrived when Deng died in a mutiny of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Before Cao Wenzhao could arrive, Deng Qi was killed when his own soldiers mutinied.

sentences.zh: 迎祥、自成從終南山出，大掠富平、寧州。

translations.literal: Yingxiang and Zicheng came out from the Zhongnan Mountains and plundered greatly in Fuping and Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiang and Li Zicheng emerged from the Zhongnan Mountains and ravaged Fuping and Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 老回回、獻忠、曹操、蠍子塊、過天星諸賊，聞承疇出關，先後皆走陝西，焚掠西安、平涼、鳳翔諸郡。

translations.literal: Old Huihui, Xianzhong, Cao Cao, Scorpion Lump, Crossing Heaven Star, and other bandits, hearing Chengchou had left the passes, one after another all fled into Shaanxi, burning and plundering the prefectures of Xi'an, Pingliang, and Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Old Huihui, Zhang Xianzhong, Cao Cao, Scorpion Lump, Crossing Heaven Star, and other chiefs—hearing Hong Chengchou had marched out—poured into Shaanxi one after another, burning Xi'an, Pingliang, Fengxiang, and the surrounding country.

sentences.zh: 承疇亟還救，分遣諸將擊老回回等，令副總兵劉成功、艾萬年擊迎祥、自成于寧州。

translations.literal: Chengchou hurried back to relieve them, sent the generals in division to strike Old Huihui and the rest, and ordered Vice Commanders Liu Chenggong and Ai Wannian to strike Yingxiang and Zicheng at Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou wheeled back to save the provinces, detached columns against Old Huihui and the others, and sent vice-commanders Liu Chenggong and Ai Wannian after Yingxiang and Li Zicheng at Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬年中伏戰死，文詔怒，復擊之，亦中伏戰死。

translations.literal: Wannian fell in an ambush and died in battle; Wenzhao in anger struck again and also fell in an ambush and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ai Wannian was ambushed and killed. Cao Wenzhao, enraged, pressed the attack and was ambushed and slain in turn.

sentences.zh: 群賊乘勝掠地，火照西安城中。

translations.literal: The mass of bandits took advantage of victory to plunder the land; firelight illuminated the city of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Victorious rebels swept the countryside; the glow of burning villages lit Xi'an from afar.

sentences.zh: 承疇力禦之涇陽、三原間，決死戰，賊不得過。

translations.literal: Chengchou with all his strength held them between Jingyang and Sanyuan, fighting a decisive battle; the bandits could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou held the line between Jingyang and Sanyuan in a death struggle and checked their advance.

sentences.zh: 獻忠、老回回等由他道轉突硃陽關，守關將徐來臣軍潰死，尤世威中箭遁。

translations.literal: Xianzhong, Old Huihui, and the rest by another route suddenly attacked Zhuyang Pass; pass defender Xu Laichen's army collapsed and he died; You Shiwei was struck by an arrow and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong and Old Huihui swung through another gap and stormed Zhuyang Pass. Defender Xu Laichen's force broke and he was killed; You Shiwei took an arrow and fled.

sentences.zh: 於是群賊皆出關，分十三營東犯，而迎祥、自成獨留陝西。

translations.literal: Then the mass of bandits all came out of the passes, divided into thirteen camps to invade east, while Yingxiang and Zicheng alone remained in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel hosts then poured out of the passes in thirteen columns to ravage the east, while only Yingxiang and Li Zicheng stayed behind in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 時盧象升已改湖廣巡撫，總理直隸、河南、山東、四川、湖廣諸軍務。

translations.literal: At this time Lu Xiangsheng had already been transferred to grand coordinator of Huguang, with overall command of military affairs in Zhili, Henan, Shandong, Sichuan, and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: By then Lu Xiangsheng had become Huguang grand coordinator with overarching command over Zhili, Henan, Shandong, Sichuan, and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 詔承疇督關中，象升督關外。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chengchou to supervise within the passes and Xiangsheng to supervise outside them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placed Hong Chengchou in charge within the passes and Lu Xiangsheng beyond them.

sentences.zh: 賊亦分兵，迎祥略武功、扶風以西，自成略富平、固州以東。

translations.literal: The bandits also divided their forces: Yingxiang raided west of Wugong and Fufeng; Zicheng raided east of Fuping and Gu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels split likewise: Yingxiang harried west of Wugong and Fufeng; Li Zicheng east of Fuping and Guzhou.

sentences.zh: 承疇遣將追自成，小捷，至醴泉。

translations.literal: Chengchou sent generals in pursuit of Zicheng, achieving a small victory, reaching Liquan.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou's pursuers skirmished successfully with Li Zicheng and pressed as far as Liquan.

sentences.zh: 賊將高傑通于自成妻邢氏，懼誅，挾之來降。

translations.literal: The bandit commander Gao Jie had dealings with Zicheng's wife the Lady Xing; fearing execution, he seized her and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel commander Gao Jie had been carrying on with Li Zicheng's wife Lady Xing; fearing punishment, he seized her and defected.

sentences.zh: 承疇身追自成，大戰渭南、臨潼，自成大敗東走。

translations.literal: Chengchou himself pursued Zicheng; a great battle at Weinan and Lintong; Zicheng was greatly defeated and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou led the pursuit himself. At Weinan and Lintong Li Zicheng was shattered and fled east.

sentences.zh: 迎祥亦屢敗，東逾華陰南原，絕嶺，偕自成出硃陽關，與獻忠合。

translations.literal: Yingxiang also suffered repeated defeats; east past Huayin and Nanyuan, over sheer ridges, he joined Zicheng through Zhuyang Pass and united with Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiang, too, lost battle after battle. He crossed Huayin's southern plateau by treacherous ridges, met Li Zicheng at Zhuyang Pass, and merged with Zhang Xianzhong's force.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，群賊薄閿鄉，左良玉、祖寬禦之不克，遂陷陝州，進攻雒陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter the mass of bandits pressed on Tong Pass; Zuo Liangyu and Zu Kuan defended but could not overcome them; they then took Shan Prefecture and pressed the attack on Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the rebel horde pressed Tong Pass. Zuo Liangyu and Zu Kuan could not hold them; they seized Shanzhou and marched on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 河南巡撫陳必謙督良玉、寬援雒陽，獻忠走嵩、汝。

translations.literal: Henan Grand Coordinator Chen Biqian supervised Liangyu and Kuan to relieve Luoyang; Xianzhong fled to Song and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Henan grand coordinator Chen Biqian rushed Liangyu and Kuan to relieve Luoyang, driving Zhang Xianzhong toward Songshan and Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 迎祥、自成走偃師、鞏縣，略魯山、葉縣，陷光州，象升擊敗之確山。

translations.literal: Yingxiang and Zicheng fled to Yanshi and Gong County, raided Lushan and Ye County, took Guang Prefecture; Xiangsheng defeated them at Queshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiang and Li Zicheng veered through Yanshi and Gongxian, pillaged Lushan and Yexian, and seized Guangzhou before Lu Xiangsheng beat them at Queshan.

sentences.zh: 九年春，迎祥、自成攻廬州，不拔。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year Yingxiang and Zicheng attacked Luzhou but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year (1636) Yingxiang and Li Zicheng besieged Luzhou without success.

sentences.zh: 陷含山、和州，殺知州黎弘業及在籍御史馬如蛟等。

translations.literal: They took Hanshan and He Prefecture, killing Prefect Li Hongye and the retired censor Ma Rujiao and others.
translations.idiomatic: They overran Hanshan and Hezhou, killing prefect Li Hongye and the retired censor Ma Rujiao among others.

sentences.zh: 又攻滁州，知州劉大鞏、太僕卿李覺斯堅守不下。

translations.literal: They again attacked Chuzhou; Prefect Liu Dagong and Grand Secretary of the Imperial Stud Li Juesi held firm and they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed Chuzhou next, but prefect Liu Dagong and Grand Secretary of the Imperial Stud Li Juesi held firm and the city would not fall.

sentences.zh: 象升親督祖寬、羅岱、楊世恩等來援，戰于硃龍橋，賊大敗，屍咽水不流。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng personally supervised Zu Kuan, Luo Dai, Yang Shi'en, and others to come to the relief; battle at Zhulong Bridge; the bandits were greatly defeated, corpses choking the water so it would not flow.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangsheng led Zu Kuan, Luo Dai, Yang Shi'en, and others to the rescue. At Zhulong Bridge the rebels were annihilated—corpses dammed the stream.

sentences.zh: 北攻壽州，故御史方震孺堅守。

translations.literal: They attacked north at Shou Prefecture; the retired censor Fang Zhenru held firm.
translations.idiomatic: They turned north on Shouzhou, where retired censor Fang Zhenru held the walls.

sentences.zh: 折而西，入歸德，邊將祖大樂破之。

translations.literal: They turned west, entered Guide, and frontier commander Zu Dale broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Swinging west into Guide, they were broken by frontier commander Zu Dale.

sentences.zh: 走密、登封，故總兵湯九州戰死。

translations.literal: They fled toward Mi and Dengfeng; the former commander Tang Jiuzhou died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: They fled toward Mi and Dengfeng; former commander Tang Jiuzhou fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 分道犯南陽、裕州，必謙援南陽，象升援裕，令大樂等擊賊，殺迎祥、自成精銳幾盡。

translations.literal: They divided their forces to raid Nanyang and Yu Prefecture; Biqian relieved Nanyang and Xiangsheng relieved Yu; Dale and others were ordered to strike the bandits, killing nearly all of Yingxiang's and Zicheng's elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: Splitting again, they struck Nanyang and Yuzhou. Chen Biqian relieved Nanyang while Lu Xiangsheng relieved Yuzhou; Zu Dale and others were ordered to engage and wiped out nearly all of Yingxiang's and Li Zicheng's veteran corps.

sentences.zh: 賊復分兵再入陝，迎祥由鄖、襄趨興安、漢中，自成由南山逾商、雒，走延綏，犯鞏昌北境。

translations.literal: The bandits again divided their forces and re-entered Shaanxi; Yingxiang by Yunyang and Xiangyang hastened to Xing'an and Hanzhong, Zicheng by the southern mountains crossed Shang and Luo, fled to Yan-sui, and raided the northern border of Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors split once more and re-entered Shaanxi—Yingxiang threading Yunyang and Xiangyang toward Xing'an and Hanzhong, Li Zicheng crossing the southern ranges over Shang and Luo into Yan-sui and raiding northern Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 諸將左光先、曹變蛟破之，自成走環縣。

translations.literal: The generals Zuo Guangxian and Cao Bianjiao defeated them; Zicheng fled to Huan County.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Guangxian and Cao Bianjiao routed Li Zicheng, who fled to Huan County.

sentences.zh: 未幾，官軍敗于羅家山，盡亡士馬器仗，總兵官俞沖霄被執。

translations.literal: Before long government troops were defeated at Mount Luojia; men, horses, and weapons were all lost; Commander Yu Chongxiao was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward government forces lost at Mount Luojia—men, horses, and arms gone to the last item; commander Yu Chongxiao was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 自成執復振，進圍綏德，欲東渡河，山西兵遏之。

translations.literal: Zicheng, having seized the momentum, revived; he advanced to besiege Suide, wishing to cross the Yellow River east; Shanxi troops barred him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng rallied on the victory, besieged Suide, and tried to cross the Yellow River eastward—only to be blocked by Shanxi troops.

sentences.zh: 復西掠米脂，呼知縣邊大綬，曰：「此吾故鄉也，勿虐我父老。」

translations.literal: He again raided west at Mizhi, summoned Magistrate Bian Dakuo, and said: "This is my old home—do not mistreat my elders."
translations.idiomatic: He turned west to plunder Mizhi, summoned Magistrate Bian Dakuo, and said: "This is my homeland—do not harm my people."

sentences.zh: 遺之金，令修文廟。

translations.literal: He gave him gold and ordered him to repair the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: He left gold to repair the county Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 將襲榆林，河水驟長，賊淹死甚眾，乃改道，從韓城而西。

translations.literal: He was about to raid Yulin when the river suddenly rose; many bandits drowned, so he changed route and went west from Hancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Planning a strike on Yulin, he found the river in sudden flood; countless rebels drowned, and he diverted west through Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 時象升及大樂、寬等皆入援京師。

translations.literal: At this time Xiangsheng and Dale, Kuan, and the rest had all entered to relieve the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: By then Lu Xiangsheng, Zu Dale, Zu Kuan, and the main armies had been drawn north to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 孫傳庭新除陝西巡撫，銳意滅賊。

translations.literal: Sun Chuanting was newly appointed grand coordinator of Shaanxi and was keen to exterminate the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuanting had just been named Shaanxi grand coordinator, determined to destroy the rebels.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，擒迎祥於盩啡，獻俘闕下，磔死。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Yingxiang was captured at Zhouzhi; he was presented as a captive below the palace and dismembered to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yingxiang was taken at Zhouzhi, paraded as a captive before the throne, and executed by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 於是賊黨乃共推自成為闖王矣。

translations.literal: Then the bandit factions jointly elevated Zicheng as King Who Charges.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel hosts thereupon acclaimed Li Zicheng King Who Charges.

sentences.zh: 是月，犯階、徽。

translations.literal: That month they raided Jie and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: That same month they raided Jiezhou and Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出秦、隴，犯鳳翔，渡渭河。

translations.literal: Before long they came out of Qin and Long, raided Fengxiang, crossed the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they burst from the Qin-Long region, struck Fengxiang, and forded the Wei.

sentences.zh: 十年，犯涇陽、三原。

translations.literal: In the tenth year they raided Jingyang and Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1637) they ravaged Jingyang and Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 蠍於塊、過天星俱來會。

translations.literal: Scorpion Lump and Crossing Heaven Star both came to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Scorpion Lump and Crossing Heaven Star joined them.

sentences.zh: 傳庭督變蛟連戰七日，皆克，蠍子塊降。

translations.literal: Chuanting supervised Bianjiao in successive battles for seven days, all victorious; Scorpion Lump surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuanting and Cao Bianjiao fought seven days straight, winning every clash; Scorpion Lump surrendered.

sentences.zh: 自成與過天星奔秦州。

translations.literal: Zicheng with Crossing Heaven Star fled to Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng and Crossing Heaven Star fled to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 入蜀，陷寧羌，破七盤關，陷廣元，總兵官侯良柱戰死，遂連陷昭化、劍州、梓潼、江油、黎雅、青川等州縣。

translations.literal: They entered Shu, took Ningqiang, broke Qipan Pass, took Guangyuan; commander Hou Liangzhu died in battle; then in succession they took Zhaohua, Jian Prefecture, Zitong, Jiangyou, Liya, Qingchuan, and other prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: They invaded Sichuan, seized Ningqiang, smashed Qipan Pass, and took Guangyuan—commander Hou Liangzhu died in the fighting—then rolled through Zhaohua, Jianzhou, Zitong, Jiangyou, Liya, Qingchuan, and a string of counties.

sentences.zh: 劍州知州徐尚卿、吏目李英俊、昭化知縣王時化、郫縣主簿張應奇、金堂典史潘夢科皆死。

translations.literal: Jian Prefecture Magistrate Xu Shangqing, Clerk Li Yingjun, Zhaohua Magistrate Wang Shihua, Pixian Registrar Zhang Yingqi, Jintang Clerk Pan Mengke—all died.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhou magistrate Xu Shangqing, clerk Li Yingjun, Zhaohua magistrate Wang Shihua, Pixian registrar Zhang Yingqi, and Jintang clerk Pan Mengke were among those who died defending their posts.

sentences.zh: 進攻成都，七日不克，巡撫王維章坐避賊征。

translations.literal: They attacked Chengdu for seven days without taking it; Grand Coordinator Wang Weizhang was punished for avoiding the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: They besieged Chengdu for seven days without success; grand coordinator Wang Weizhang was recalled and punished for evading the rebels.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，官軍敗賊梓潼，自成奔白水，食盡。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year government troops defeated the bandits at Zitong; Zicheng fled to Baishui, provisions exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year (1638) government forces beat them at Zitong; Li Zicheng fled to Baishui with his men starving.

sentences.zh: 承疇、傳庭合擊于潼關原，大破之。

translations.literal: Chengchou and Chuanting jointly struck at Tong Pass Plain and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou and Sun Chuanting united at Tongguan Plain and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 自成盡亡其卒，獨與劉宗敏、田見秀等十八騎潰圍，竄伏商、洛山中。

translations.literal: Zicheng lost his troops entirely; only with Liu Zongmin, Tian Jianxiu, and eighteen riders did he break the encirclement and hide in the Shang-Luo mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng's army was gone; he escaped the encirclement with Liu Zongmin, Tian Jianxiu, and only eighteen horsemen, hiding in the mountains of Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 其年，獻忠降，自成勢益衰。

translations.literal: That year Xianzhong surrendered; Zicheng's strength grew ever more feeble.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhang Xianzhong surrendered; Li Zicheng's power ebbed further.

sentences.zh: 承疇改薊遼總督，傳庭改保定總督。

translations.literal: Chengchou was transferred to Jizhou-Liaodong supreme commander; Chuanting to Baoding supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou was made Jizhou-Liaodong supreme commander; Sun Chuanting Baoding supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 傳庭以疾辭，逮下獄。

translations.literal: Chuanting pleaded illness and resigned; he was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuanting pleaded illness, resigned, and was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 二人去，自成稍得安。

translations.literal: With the two of them gone, Zicheng gained a little peace.
translations.idiomatic: Once those two were gone, Li Zicheng could breathe a little easier.

sentences.zh: 總理熊文燦方主撫，諜者或報自成死，益寬之。

translations.literal: Overall commander Xiong Wencan was then advocating appeasement; spies sometimes reported Zicheng dead, and restraint toward him grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Overall Pacification Commissioner Xiong Wencan favored negotiation; scouts sometimes reported Li Zicheng dead, and the court relaxed its guard further.

sentences.zh: 十二年夏，獻忠反穀城。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twelfth year Xianzhong rebelled at Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twelfth year (1639) Zhang Xianzhong rose again at Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 自成大喜，出收眾，眾復大集。

translations.literal: Zicheng greatly rejoiced, came forth to gather the host, and the multitude again assembled in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng rejoiced, came out of hiding, and his followers swelled once more.

sentences.zh: 陝西總督鄭崇儉發兵圍之，令曰「圍師必缺。」

translations.literal: Shaanxi Governor Zheng Chongjian sent troops to surround him, with the order: "An encircling army must leave a gap."
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi governor Zheng Chongjian encircled him with orders: "A siege must always leave an opening."

sentences.zh: 自成乃由缺走，突武關，往依獻忠。

translations.literal: Zicheng then fled through the gap, burst through Wuguan, and went to depend on Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng slipped through the deliberate gap, broke past Wuguan, and threw in his lot with Zhang Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 獻忠欲圖之，覺，遁去。

translations.literal: Xianzhong wished to destroy him; Zicheng perceived it and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong meant to eliminate him; Li Zicheng sensed the trap and fled.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌督師夷陵，檄令降，自成出謾語。

translations.literal: Yang Sichang directed the army at Yiling and issued a proclamation ordering surrender; Zicheng replied with insolent words.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang took command at Yiling and ordered the rebels to surrender; Li Zicheng answered with mockery.

sentences.zh: 官軍圍自成于巴西、魚復諸山中，自成大困，欲自經，養子雙喜勸而止。

translations.literal: Government troops surrounded Zicheng in the mountains of Baxi and Yufu; Zicheng was in desperate straits and wished to hang himself, but his adopted son Shuangxi persuaded him to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial forces penned Li Zicheng in the Baxi and Yufu mountains; cornered and ready to take his own life, he was talked down by his adopted son Shuangxi.

sentences.zh: 賊將多出降。

translations.literal: Many of the bandit generals came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: One rebel commander after another surrendered.

sentences.zh: 劉宗敏者，藍田鍛工也，最驍勇，亦欲降。

translations.literal: Liu Zongmin was a blacksmith of Lantian, the fiercest and bravest of them; he too wished to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongmin, a smith from Lantian and their bravest fighter, was also ready to submit.

sentences.zh: 自成與步入叢祠，顧而歎曰：「人言我當為天子，盍卜之，不吉，斷我頭以降。」

translations.literal: Zicheng went in with him to a shrine in the thicket, looked back and sighed, saying: "Men say I am destined to be Son of Heaven—let us divine it; if the omen is ill, cut off my head and surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng led him into a wooded shrine, turned, and sighed: "They say I am fated to rule—let us cast lots; if the sign is bad, take my head and surrender."

sentences.zh: 宗敏諾，三卜三吉。

translations.literal: Zongmin assented; three castings, all auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin agreed; three divinations, all favorable.

sentences.zh: 宗敏還，殺其兩妻，謂自成曰：「吾死從君矣。」

translations.literal: Zongmin returned and killed his two wives, saying to Zicheng: "I shall die following you."
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin went back, slew his two wives, and told Zicheng: "I will follow you to the death."

sentences.zh: 軍中壯士聞之，亦多殺妻子願從者。

translations.literal: When the stalwarts in the army heard this, many also killed wives and children and vowed to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, many bold fighters in the ranks likewise killed their families and pledged to march on.

sentences.zh: 自成乃盡焚輜重，輕騎由鄖、均走河南。

translations.literal: Zicheng then burned all baggage and supplies, and with light cavalry fled by Yun and Jun into Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng burned his entire train, then rode light through Yun and Jun into Henan.

sentences.zh: 河南大旱，斛谷萬錢，饑民從自成者數萬。

translations.literal: Henan suffered great drought; a hu of grain cost ten thousand cash; tens of thousands of starving people followed Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Henan was gripped by drought—grain sold for ten thousand cash a hu—and tens of thousands of the hungry joined Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 遂自南陽出，攻宜陽，殺知縣唐啟泰。

translations.literal: He then marched out from Nanyang, attacked Yiyang, and killed Magistrate Tang Qitai.
translations.idiomatic: He broke out of Nanyang, stormed Yiyang, and killed the magistrate Tang Qitai.

sentences.zh: 攻永甯，殺知縣武大烈，戕萬安王采𨮫。

translations.literal: He attacked Yongning, killed Magistrate Wu Dalie, and slew Prince Wan'an Caiqing.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongning he killed Magistrate Wu Dalie and murdered Prince Wan'an, Caiqing.

sentences.zh: 攻偃師，知縣徐日泰罵賊死。

translations.literal: He attacked Yanshi; Magistrate Xu Ritai cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanshi the magistrate Xu Ritai hurled defiance at the rebels and was killed.

sentences.zh: 時十三年十二月也。

translations.literal: It was the twelfth month of the thirteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the twelfth month of Chongzhen 13.

sentences.zh: 自成為人高顴深，鴟目曷鼻，聲如豺。

translations.literal: Zicheng was tall, with high cheekbones and deep-set eyes, hawk eyes and a hooked nose, and a voice like a jackal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng was tall and gaunt, with prominent cheekbones, deep sockets, predatory eyes, a hooked nose, and a voice like a hunting dog.

sentences.zh: 性猜忍，日殺人斮足剖心為戲。

translations.literal: By nature suspicious and cruel; daily he killed people, chopping off feet and cutting open hearts for sport.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicious and pitiless by nature, he amused himself each day by killing—severing feet and slicing open chests.

sentences.zh: 所過，民皆保塢堡不下。

translations.literal: Wherever he passed, the people all held fast in stockaded villages and would not come down.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere his army went, villagers barricaded themselves in fortified hamlets and refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 杞縣舉人李信者，逆案中尚書李精白子也，嘗出粟振饑民，民德之曰：「李公子活我。」

translations.literal: Li Xin of Qixian, a presented scholar, was the son of Minister Li Jingbai, who had been implicated in the case of treacherous ministers; he had once issued grain to relieve the starving, and the people were grateful, saying: "Master Li has given us life."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin of Qixian, a jinshi and son of the disgraced minister Li Jingbai, had once distributed grain in famine relief; the people blessed him, saying, "Young Master Li has kept us alive."

sentences.zh: 會繩伎紅娘子反，擄信，強委身焉。

translations.literal: It happened that Hong Niangzi, leader of the rope-dancers, rose in rebellion, seized Xin, and forced him to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: Then Hong Niangzi, a rebel leader among the rope-trick performers, captured Xin and compelled him to wed her.

sentences.zh: 信逃歸，官以為賊，囚獄中。

translations.literal: Xin fled home; the officials treated him as a bandit and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Xin escaped home, but officials branded him a rebel and threw him in jail.

sentences.zh: 紅娘子來救，饑民應之，共出信。

translations.literal: Hong Niangzi came to rescue him; starving people responded, and together they freed Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Niangzi marched to free him; the hungry rose with her, and together they broke Xin out.

sentences.zh: 盧氏舉人牛金星磨勘被斥，私入自成軍為主謀，潛歸，事泄坐斬，已，得末減。

translations.literal: Niu Jinxing of Lushi, a presented scholar, had been dismissed in administrative review; he secretly entered Zicheng's army as chief strategist, then secretly returned; the matter leaked and he was sentenced to execution, but later received a reduced sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Jinxing of Lushi, also a jinshi, had been cashiered in a personnel review; he slipped into Zicheng's camp as chief adviser, slipped back out, was caught, condemned to death, and finally spared.

sentences.zh: 二人皆往投自成，自成大喜，改信名曰岩。

translations.literal: Both men went to join Zicheng; Zicheng was greatly pleased and changed Xin's name to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Both men threw in their lot with Li Zicheng, who was delighted and gave Xin the name Yan.

sentences.zh: 金星又薦卜者宋獻策，長三尺餘，上讖記云：「十八子，主神器。」

translations.literal: Jinxing also recommended the diviner Song Xiance, who stood over three feet tall; his prophecy read: "The eighteen-child shall wield the sacred vessel."
translations.idiomatic: Jinxing also brought in the seer Song Xiance, a man barely three feet tall, whose prophecy ran: "The one named Eighteen shall possess the Mandate."

sentences.zh: 自成大悅。

translations.literal: Zicheng was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 岩因說曰：「取天下以人心為本，請勿殺人，收天下心。」

translations.literal: Yan therefore advised, saying: "To take the realm, the hearts of the people are fundamental—please do not kill, and you will win the hearts of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Yan urged him: "Winning the empire depends on winning hearts—stop the killing, and you will win the people."

sentences.zh: 自成從之，屠戮為減。

translations.literal: Zicheng followed this; slaughter was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng heeded him, and the massacres eased.
