sentences.zh: 又散所掠財物振饑民，民受餉者，不辨岩、自成也，雜呼曰：「李公子活我。」

translations.literal: He also distributed plundered goods to relieve the starving; those who received provisions could not tell Yan from Zicheng, and mixed cries went up: "Master Li has given us life."
translations.idiomatic: He also handed out loot to feed the hungry; recipients could not tell Yan from Zicheng and shouted alike, "Young Master Li has kept us alive!"

sentences.zh: 岩復造謠詞曰：「迎闖王，不納糧。」

translations.literal: Yan also composed a ballad: "Welcome Lord Chuang; pay no grain tax."
translations.idiomatic: Yan composed a slogan: "Welcome Lord Chuang—no grain levies."

sentences.zh: 使兒童歌以相煽，從自成者日眾。

translations.literal: He had children sing it to stir people up; those who followed Zicheng grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Children were taught to sing it as propaganda, and Zicheng's following swelled day by day.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月攻河南，有營卒勾賊，城遂陷，福王常洵遇害。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year he attacked Henan; a garrison soldier colluded with the bandits, and the city fell; Prince Fu Changxun met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chongzhen 14 he struck Henan; a camp soldier opened the gates to the rebels, the city fell, and Prince Fu Changxun was killed.

sentences.zh: 自成兵汋王血，雜鹿醢嘗之，名「福祿酒。」

translations.literal: Zicheng's troops scooped the prince's blood, mixed it with venison paste, and tasted it, naming it "Fortune and Emolument Wine."
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng's men caught the prince's blood, blended it with venison stew, drank it, and called the brew "Wine of Fortune and Salary."

sentences.zh: 王世子由崧裸而逃。

translations.literal: The prince's heir Yousong fled naked.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Yousong escaped stripped to the skin.

sentences.zh: 自成發王邸金振饑民，遂移攻開封。

translations.literal: Zicheng distributed gold from the prince's mansion to relieve the starving, then shifted to attack Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng opened the princely vaults to feed the hungry, then marched on Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 時張獻忠亦陷襄陽，戕襄王翊銘。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Xianzhong also took Xiangyang and slew Prince Xiang Yiming.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhang Xianzhong seized Xiangyang and killed Prince Xiang Yiming.

sentences.zh: 王開封者周王恭枵，聞賊至，急發庫金募死士，與巡撫都御史高名衡等固守。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhou at Kaifeng was Gongxiao; hearing the bandits had come, he urgently opened the treasury to recruit death-defying men, and with Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief Gao Mingheng and others held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhou of Kaifeng, Gongxiao, hearing the rebels approach, emptied his treasury to hire desperate fighters and, with Grand Coordinator Gao Mingheng and others, dug in to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 自成攻七晝夜，解去，屠密縣。

translations.literal: Zicheng attacked for seven days and nights, then withdrew and massacred Mi County.
translations.idiomatic: After seven days and nights of assault Zicheng lifted the siege and slaughtered Mi County.

sentences.zh: 賊魁羅汝才、土寇袁時中皆歸自成。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Luo Rucai and the local raider Yuan Shizhong both submitted to Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief Luo Rucai and the local bandit Yuan Shizhong both joined Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 時中眾二十萬，號小袁營。

translations.literal: Shizhong's host numbered two hundred thousand; he was called the Little Yuan Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shizhong commanded two hundred thousand men, known as the Little Yuan Camp.

sentences.zh: 汝才即曹操，與獻忠同降復叛去者也。

translations.literal: Rucai was Cao Cao, who with Xianzhong had once surrendered and rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai was the man called Cao Cao, who had surrendered with Zhang Xianzhong only to rebel once more.

sentences.zh: 自成初為迎祥裨將，至是勢大盛。

translations.literal: Zicheng had first been a lieutenant under Yingxiang; by now his power was greatly ascendant.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng had begun as a lieutenant to Yingxiang; now his strength was supreme.

sentences.zh: 帝以故尚書傅宗龍為陝西總督，使專辦自成，別敕保定總督楊文岳會師。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed the former minister Fu Zonglong Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi to deal exclusively with Zicheng, and separately ordered Grand Coordinator Yang Wenyue of Baoding to join forces.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chongzhen named the former minister Fu Zonglong governor of Shaanxi to focus on Li Zicheng and ordered Yang Wenyue, governor of Baoding, to unite their armies.

sentences.zh: 宗龍馳入關，與巡撫汪喬年調兵，兵已發盡，乃檄河南大將李國奇、賀人龍兵隸部下，亟出關。

translations.literal: Zonglong galloped into the pass and with Grand Coordinator Wang Qiaonian mustered troops; the troops were already all sent out, so he summoned the Henan generals Li Guoqi and He Renlong under his command and hurried out of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zonglong raced through the pass and, with Governor Wang Qiaonian, scraped together every soldier already deployed, then drafted the Henan commanders Li Guoqi and He Renlong and pushed out of the pass at once.

sentences.zh: 文嶽率虎大威軍俱至新蔡，與自成遇。

translations.literal: Wenyue led Hu Dawei's army to Xincai and met Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyue brought Hu Dawei's troops to Xincai and collided with Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 人龍卒先奔，國奇、大威繼之，宗龍、文嶽以親軍築壘自固。

translations.literal: Renlong's troops fled first; Guoqi and Dawei followed; Zonglong and Wenyue with their personal guards built ramparts and held fast.
translations.idiomatic: He Renlong's men broke first; Li Guoqi and Hu Dawei followed; Zonglong and Wenyue entrenched their bodyguards behind earthworks.

sentences.zh: 夜，文嶽兵潰奔陳州，宗龍與賊持數日，食盡，突圍走，被執死。

translations.literal: By night Wenyue's army collapsed and fled to Chenzhou; Zonglong held out against the bandits for several days, food exhausted, broke out and fled, was captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: That night Wenyue's force disintegrated and fled to Chenzhou; Zonglong held for days until provisions ran out, fought his way out, was taken, and executed.

sentences.zh: 自成陷葉縣，殺副將劉國能，遂圍左良玉於郾城。

translations.literal: Zicheng took Ye County, killed Vice Commander Liu Guoneng, then besieged Zuo Liangyu at Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng seized Ye County, slew Vice Commander Liu Guoneng, and besieged Zuo Liangyu at Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 喬年代宗龍總督，出關，次襄城，自成盡銳攻之，喬年與副將李萬慶皆死。

translations.literal: Qiaonian succeeded Zonglong as grand coordinator, went out of the pass, halted at Xiangcheng; Zicheng attacked with all his strength; Qiaonian and Vice Commander Li Wanqing both died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiaonian replaced Zonglong, marched out, and camped at Xiangcheng; Zicheng threw his full strength against him; Qiaonian and Vice Commander Li Wanqing were both killed.

sentences.zh: 自成劓刖諸生百九十人。

translations.literal: Zicheng mutilated one hundred ninety scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng maimed one hundred ninety degree-holders.

sentences.zh: 遂乘勝陷南陽、鄧州十四城，再圍開封。

translations.literal: He then pressed his victory, took Nanyang, Dengzhou, and fourteen other cities, and besieged Kaifeng again.
translations.idiomatic: Riding momentum he captured Nanyang, Dengzhou, and fourteen cities, then laid siege to Kaifeng once more.

sentences.zh: 巡撫名衡、總兵陳永福力拒之，射中自成目，砲殪上天龍等，自成益怒。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Mingheng and Commander Chen Yongfu resisted with all their strength; an arrow struck Zicheng in the eye, cannon fire killed Shang Tianlong and others, and Zicheng grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Mingheng and General Chen Yongfu fought back fiercely; a shot pierced Zicheng's eye, cannon fire killed Shang Tianlong and others, and his rage only deepened.

sentences.zh: 自成每攻城，不用古梯沖法，專取瓴甋，得一磚即歸營臥，後者必斬。

translations.literal: Whenever Zicheng attacked a city he did not use ancient scaling-ladder and ram methods; he specialized in seizing roof tiles—whoever brought back one brick returned to camp to lie down, and whoever came after without one was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In every siege he spurned ladders and rams; each man had to fetch roof tiles—bring one brick back to camp and rest; fail, and be executed.

sentences.zh: 取磚已，即穿穴穴城。

translations.literal: When enough bricks were gathered, they bored holes through the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Once enough bricks were collected, they tunneled into the wall.

sentences.zh: 初僅容一人，漸至百十，次第傅土以出。

translations.literal: At first the opening held only one man; gradually it reached a hundred or ten; they passed earth out in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The breach began wide enough for one man, then dozens, then hundreds, as diggers passed soil out behind them.

sentences.zh: 過三五步，留一土柱，系以巨糸亙。

translations.literal: Every three or five paces they left an earthen pillar and tied it with a great rope stretched across.
translations.idiomatic: Every few paces they left an earthen column and lashed it with heavy ropes.

sentences.zh: 穿畢，萬人曳糸亙一呼，而柱折城崩矣。

translations.literal: When the boring was finished, ten thousand men pulled the ropes with one shout, and the pillars broke and the wall collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: When the tunneling was done, ten thousand men hauled the ropes at once—the columns snapped and the wall came down.

sentences.zh: 名衡於城上鑿橫道，聽其下有聲，用毒穢灌之，多死。

translations.literal: Mingheng on the wall cut horizontal passages; hearing sounds below, he poured in poison and filth, and many died.
translations.idiomatic: Mingheng bored listening galleries along the parapet; hearing digging below, defenders poured poison and filth into the tunnels, killing many.

sentences.zh: 賊乃即城壞處用火攻法，實藥甕中，火燃藥發，當者輒糜碎，名曰放迸。

translations.literal: The bandits then at the broken wall used fire-attack method: they packed gunpowder in jars; when fire ignited the powder it exploded, and those struck were pulverized; they called it "bursting discharge."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels turned to fire assault at the breach—powder packed in jars, ignited to shatter defenders—a tactic they named "bursting advance."

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，城半圮，賊用放迸法攻之，鐵騎數千馳噪，伺城頹即擁入城。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year, half the wall was ruined; the bandits used the bursting method to attack; several thousand iron cavalry galloped shouting, waiting for the wall to fall to swarm into the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chongzhen 15 half the ramparts crumbled; rebels blasted the breach with bursting charges while thousands of armored horsemen waited to pour through the moment the wall gave way.

sentences.zh: 城故宋汴都，金人所重築也。

translations.literal: The city had been the Song capital Bian, and the Jin had heavily rebuilt it.
translations.idiomatic: The city was the old Song capital of Bian, massively refortified by the Jin.

sentences.zh: 厚數丈，土堅，火外擊，賊騎多殲，自成駭而去。

translations.literal: Several zhang thick, the earth was firm; fire struck from outside, and many bandit horsemen were destroyed; Zicheng fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Walls several zhang thick of packed earth withstood external blasts; rebel cavalry were slaughtered in droves, and Zicheng retreated in shock.

sentences.zh: 南陷西華，尋屠陳州，副使關永傑、知州侯君擢皆罵賊死。

translations.literal: He swept south and took Xihua, then soon massacred Chenzhou; Vice Commissioner Guan Yongjie and Magistrate Hou Junzhuo both cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: He drove south through Xihua, then butchered Chenzhou; Vice Commissioner Guan Yongjie and Magistrate Hou Junzhuo cursed the rebels and died.

sentences.zh: 歸德、睢州、寧陵、太康數十郡縣，悉殘毀。

translations.literal: Guide, Suizhou, Ningling, Taikang, and dozens of prefectures and counties were all ravaged.
translations.idiomatic: Guide, Suizhou, Ningling, Taikang, and dozens of other prefectures and counties were laid waste.

sentences.zh: 商丘知縣梁以樟創死復蘇，全家殲焉。

translations.literal: Liang Yizhang, magistrate of Shangqiu, was beaten until he died and revived; his whole family was annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangqiu, Magistrate Liang Yizhang was beaten to death, revived, and then his entire household was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 已，復攻開封，築長圍為持久計。

translations.literal: Later he attacked Kaifeng again and built a long encirclement for a war of attrition.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to Kaifeng, throwing up a continuous siege line meant to starve the city out.

sentences.zh: 詔起孫傳庭為總督，釋故尚書侯恂命督師，召左良玉援開封。

translations.literal: An edict recalled Sun Chuanating as grand coordinator, released the former minister Hou Xun to direct the army, and summoned Zuo Liangyu to relieve Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: The court reappointed Sun Chuanating as grand coordinator, freed the former minister Hou Xun to take command, and called Zuo Liangyu to Kaifeng's aid.

sentences.zh: 良玉至硃仙鎮，大敗，奔襄陽。

translations.literal: Liangyu reached Zhuxian Town and suffered a great defeat, fleeing to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu reached Zhuxian Town, was routed, and fled to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 諸軍皆屯河北，不敢進。

translations.literal: All the armies camped north of the river and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Government armies massed north of the Yellow River and would not move forward.

sentences.zh: 開封食盡。

translations.literal: Kaifeng's food was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng ran out of food.

sentences.zh: 山東總兵劉澤清亦奉詔至。

translations.literal: Liu Zeqing, regional commander of Shandong, also arrived by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zeqing, commander of Shandong, likewise arrived on imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 傳庭知開封急，大會諸將西安，亟出關來救。

translations.literal: Chuanating knew Kaifeng was urgent; he held a great council of generals at Xi'an and hurried out of the pass to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Kaifeng's peril, Sun Chuanating convened his generals at Xi'an and raced through the pass to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 未至，名衡等議決硃家寨口河灌賊，賊亦決馬家口河欲灌城。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Mingheng and others resolved to breach the Yellow River at Zhujiazhai to flood the bandits; the bandits also breached the river at Majiakou intending to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, Mingheng and others decided to cut the Yellow River at Zhujiazhai to drown the rebels; the rebels cut the river at Majiakou to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 秋九月癸未，天大雨，二口並決，聲如雷，潰北門入，穿東南門出，注渦水。

translations.literal: On guimou day in the ninth month of autumn, heaven sent down great rain; both breaches opened together with a sound like thunder; water burst in through the north gate, passed out the southeast gate, and poured into the Wo River.
translations.idiomatic: On guimou day in the ninth month, torrential rain burst both dikes at once with thunderous roar; floodwater crashed through the north gate, exited the southeast gate, and poured into the Wo River.

sentences.zh: 城中百萬戶皆沒，得脫者惟周王、妃、世子及撫按以下不及二萬人。

translations.literal: Within the city a million households were submerged; those who escaped were only the Prince of Zhou, his consort, the heir, and fewer than twenty thousand persons including the grand coordinator and censorate staff.
translations.idiomatic: A million people drowned inside the walls; only the Prince of Zhou, his consort, the heir, and fewer than twenty thousand officials and soldiers escaped.

sentences.zh: 賊亦漂沒萬餘，乃拔營西南去。

translations.literal: The bandits also had more than ten thousand washed away; they then broke camp and went southwest.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels lost more than ten thousand drowned as well, then broke camp and marched southwest.

sentences.zh: 先是，有馬守應稱老回回、賀一龍稱革裏眼、賀錦稱左金王、劉希堯稱爭世王、藺養成稱亂世王者，皆附自成，時號「革左五營。」

translations.literal: Earlier there had been Ma Shouying, called Old Muslim; He Yilong, called Green-Eye; He Jin, called Left Golden King; Liu Xiyao, called Contending-for-the-Age King; and Lin Yangcheng, called Disorderly-Age King—all had attached themselves to Zicheng, and at the time they were called the "Five Camps of Ge and Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ma Shouying ("Old Muslim"), He Yilong ("Green Eye"), He Jin ("Left Golden King"), Liu Xiyao ("Struggle-for-the-Era King"), and Lin Yangcheng ("Chaotic-Era King") had all joined Zicheng—the so-called Five Camps of Ge and Zuo.

sentences.zh: 自成乃西迎傳庭兵，遇於南陽，傳庭軍潰走，豫人所謂柿園之敗也。

translations.literal: Zicheng then marched west to meet Chuanating's army; they met at Nanyang; Chuanating's army collapsed and fled—the defeat the people of Yu called the Persimmon Garden rout.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng turned west to meet Sun Chuanating at Nanyang; the government army broke and fled—the disaster Henan remembered as the rout at Persimmon Garden.

sentences.zh: 是時大清兵南侵，京師方告急，朝廷不暇復討賊。

translations.literal: At that time the Great Qing army invaded south; the capital was in urgent alarm, and the court had no leisure to pursue the bandits further.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Qing armies drove south; Beijing itself was in crisis, and the court could spare no more attention for the rebels.

sentences.zh: 自成乃收群賊，連營五百餘里，再屠南陽，進攻汝寧。

translations.literal: Zicheng then gathered the bandit hosts, camp after camp for more than five hundred li, massacred Nanyang again, and pressed the attack on Runing.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng rallied every rebel band into a camp line five hundred li long, slaughtered Nanyang again, and advanced on Runing.

sentences.zh: 總兵虎大威中砲死，楊文嶽被殺。

translations.literal: Commander Hu Dawei was killed by cannon fire; Yang Wenyue was slain.
translations.idiomatic: General Hu Dawei died under cannon fire; Yang Wenyue was killed.

sentences.zh: 自成乃脅崇王由樻使從軍，遂由確山、信陽、泌陽向襄陽。

translations.literal: Zicheng then compelled Prince Chong Youfu to march with the army, and advanced by Queshan, Xinyang, and Biyang toward Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He forced Prince Chong Youfu to march with him and drove through Queshan, Xinyang, and Biyang toward Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 左良玉望風南走，自成入襄陽。

translations.literal: Zuo Liangyu fled south at the sight of dust; Zicheng entered Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu fled south at the first dust cloud; Li Zicheng entered Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 分徇屬城及德安諸州縣，皆下，再破夷陵、荊門州。

translations.literal: He dispatched columns to subdue dependent cities and the prefectures and counties of De'an, all of which fell; he again took Yiling and Jingmen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Columns fanned out to seize De'an and its counties, then Yiling and Jingmen fell again.

sentences.zh: 自成自攻荊州，湘陰王儼钅尹遇害，燒獻陵木城，穿毀宮殿。

translations.literal: Zicheng himself attacked Jingzhou; Prince Xiangyin of Xiangyin met disaster; he burned the timber stockade of the Xianling Mausoleum and tunneled through to destroy the palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng personally stormed Jingzhou, killing Prince Xiangyin; he burned the timber defenses around the Xianling Mausoleum and dug into the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 十六年春陷承天。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year he took Chengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Chongzhen 16 he captured Chengtian.

sentences.zh: 將發獻陵，有聲震山谷，懼而止。

translations.literal: When he was about to open the Xianling Mausoleum, a sound shook the mountains and valleys, and in fear he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to violate the Xianling tombs, a thunderous sound rolled through the valleys and he desisted in terror.

sentences.zh: 帝掠潛山、京山、雲夢、黃陂、孝感等州縣，皆下。

translations.literal: Zicheng raided Qianshan, Jingshan, Yunmeng, Huangpi, Xiaogan, and other prefectures and counties; all fell.
translations.idiomatic: He swept Qianshan, Jingshan, Yunmeng, Huangpi, Xiaogan, and neighboring districts—all submitted.

sentences.zh: 先驅逼漢陽，良玉走九江。

translations.literal: His vanguard pressed upon Hanyang; Liangyu fled to Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: His van reached Hanyang; Zuo Liangyu fled to Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 攻鄖陽，撫治都御史徐起元及王光恩力守不下。

translations.literal: He attacked Yunyang; Grand Coordinator Xu Qiyuan and Wang Guangen defended with all their strength and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: At Yunyang, Grand Coordinator Xu Qiyuan and Wang Guangen held firm and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 光恩，賊反正者也。

translations.literal: Guangen was one who had turned from the bandits back to loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Guangen was a former rebel who had returned to the government side.

sentences.zh: 自成自號奉天倡義大元帥，號羅汝才代天撫民威德大將軍。

translations.literal: Zicheng styled himself Grand Marshal for Upholding Heaven and Raising the Cause; he styled Luo Rucai Great General of Substituting for Heaven, Pacifying the People, and Majestic Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng took the title Grand Marshal of the Mandate of Heaven Who Raises the Righteous Cause; he gave Luo Rucai the title Great General Substituting for Heaven Who Pacifies the People in Majestic Virtue.

sentences.zh: 分其眾，曰標營，領兵百隊；

translations.literal: He divided his host, calling one division the Standard Camp, commanding a hundred companies of troops;
translations.idiomatic: He organized his forces into the Standard Camp, commanding one hundred companies;

sentences.zh: 曰先、後、左、右營，各領兵三十餘隊。

translations.literal: and the Forward, Rear, Left, and Right Camps, each commanding more than thirty companies.
translations.idiomatic: and the Forward, Rear, Left, and Right Camps, each with more than thirty companies.

sentences.zh: 標營白幟黑纛，自成獨白鬃大纛銀浮屠；

translations.literal: The Standard Camp used white banners and black pennants; Zicheng alone had a white-maned great pennant with a silver stupa;
translations.idiomatic: The Standard Camp flew white flags and black streamers; Zicheng alone carried a great white-maned banner topped with a silver pagoda;

sentences.zh: 左營幟白，右緋，前黑，後黃，纛隨其色。

translations.literal: the Left Camp's banners were white, the Right crimson, the Forward black, the Rear yellow; pennants followed their colors.
translations.idiomatic: the Left white, the Right crimson, the Forward black, the Rear yellow—pennants matched each camp's color.

sentences.zh: 五營以序直晝夜，次第休息，巡徼嚴密。

translations.literal: The five camps rotated day and night in order, resting in succession; patrol and sentry were strict.
translations.idiomatic: The five camps rotated day and night in strict sequence, resting in turns under tight patrol.

sentences.zh: 逃者謂之落草，磔之。

translations.literal: Those who fled were called "fallen into the grass" and were dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Deserters were called "fallen into the grass" and were torn apart alive.

sentences.zh: 收男子十五以上、四十以下者為兵。

translations.literal: They enrolled men fifteen years and above, forty and below, as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Every man from fifteen to forty was pressed into service.

sentences.zh: 精兵一人，主芻、掌械、執爨者十人。

translations.literal: One elite soldier had ten men attending to fodder, weapons, and cooking.
translations.idiomatic: Each front-line fighter was supported by ten men who carried fodder, arms, and cooked.

sentences.zh: 軍令不得藏白金，過城邑不得室處，妻子外不得攜他婦人。

translations.literal: Military law forbade hoarding silver; passing cities and towns one might not lodge indoors; apart from one's wife one might not take other women.
translations.idiomatic: Army law forbade private silver, forbade sleeping indoors when passing towns, and forbade keeping any woman but one's wife.

sentences.zh: 寢興悉用單布幕。

translations.literal: Sleeping and rising all used single cloth curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Sleep and waking were under single cloth awnings only.

sentences.zh: 綿甲厚百層，矢砲不能入。

translations.literal: Padded armor a hundred layers thick—arrows and cannon could not penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: Quilted armor a hundred layers thick turned aside arrows and shot.

sentences.zh: 一兵倅馬三四匹，冬則以茵褥籍其蹄。

translations.literal: One soldier might have three or four horses apiece; in winter they spread mats and bedding under the hooves.
translations.idiomatic: Each fighter kept three or four horses; in winter they padded the hooves with bedding.

sentences.zh: 剖人腹為馬槽以飼馬，馬見人，輒鋸牙思噬若虎豹。

translations.literal: They cut open human bellies for horse troughs to feed horses; when horses saw people they bared teeth and longed to bite like tigers and leopards.
translations.idiomatic: They gutted captives to make feeding troughs; their horses, seeing men, gnashed their teeth to savage them like beasts.

sentences.zh: 軍止，即出較騎射，曰站隊。

translations.literal: When the army halted, they held contests of mounted archery, called "standing formation."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they camped, they held mounted archery contests called "standing formation."

sentences.zh: 夜四鼓，蓐食以聽令。

translations.literal: At the fourth watch of night they took bedding meal to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth night watch they ate a cold meal in bed awaiting orders.

sentences.zh: 所過崇岡峻阪，騰馬直上。

translations.literal: Where they passed, on lofty hills and steep slopes, they spurred horses straight up.
translations.idiomatic: They galloped up the steepest ridges without slackening.

sentences.zh: 水惟憚黃河，若淮、泗、涇、渭，則萬眾翹足馬背，或抱鬣緣尾，呼風而渡，馬蹄所壅閼，水為不流。

translations.literal: Of waters they feared only the Yellow River; for the Huai, Si, Jing, and Wei, tens of thousands would perch on horseback, or clutch the mane and tail, and cross with a shout—the hooves dammed the flow and the water ceased to run.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Yellow River gave them pause; on the Huai, Si, Jing, and Wei they crossed by the ten thousand—clinging to manes and tails, shouting across until hooves choked the current still.

sentences.zh: 臨陣，列馬三萬，名三堵牆。

translations.literal: In battle they arrayed thirty thousand horses, called the Three Rampart Walls.
translations.idiomatic: In battle they formed thirty thousand horsemen into what they called the Three Rampart Walls.

sentences.zh: 前者返顧，後者殺之。

translations.literal: Whoever in the front rank looked back, those in the rear killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Any man in the front rank who looked back was killed by those behind.

sentences.zh: 戰久不勝，馬兵佯則誘官兵，步卒長槍三萬，擊刺如飛，馬兵回擊，無不大勝。

translations.literal: If the fight dragged on without victory, the cavalry feigned defeat to lure government troops; thirty thousand foot soldiers with long spears struck like flying bolts, and when the cavalry wheeled back to strike, they never failed to win greatly.
translations.idiomatic: If a battle stalled, cavalry feigned retreat to draw government troops in; thirty thousand spearmen struck like lightning, then the horsemen wheeled back—no engagement failed to end in rout.

sentences.zh: 攻城，迎降者不殺，守一日殺十之三，二日殺十之七，三日屠之。

translations.literal: When attacking cities, those who welcomed and surrendered were not killed; hold one day and three-tenths were killed; two days and seven-tenths; three days and the city was massacred.
translations.idiomatic: At a siege, those who opened the gates were spared; resist one day and three in ten died; two days, seven in ten; on the third day the city was slaughtered to the last.

sentences.zh: 凡殺人，束屍為燎，謂之打亮。

translations.literal: Whenever they killed people, they bound the corpses into pyres, calling it "making light."
translations.idiomatic: Every killing ended with corpses stacked and burned—a spectacle they called "making light."

sentences.zh: 城將陷，步兵萬人環堞下，馬兵巡徼，無一人得免。

translations.literal: When a city was about to fall, ten thousand foot soldiers ringed below the parapet and cavalry patrolled; not one person could escape.
translations.idiomatic: As a city neared collapse, ten thousand foot soldiers ringed the walls while cavalry patrolled—no one escaped.

sentences.zh: 獻忠雖至殘忍，不逮也。

translations.literal: Although Xianzhong was cruel to the utmost, he did not reach this.
translations.idiomatic: Even Zhang Xianzhong at his cruellest never matched this.

sentences.zh: 諸營較所獲，馬騾者上賞，弓夭鉛銃者次之，幣帛又次之，珠玉為下。

translations.literal: The camps compared their gains: horses and mules received top reward; bows, crossbows, and firearms came next; cloth and silk after that; pearls and jade ranked lowest.
translations.idiomatic: Camps competed for loot: horses and mules won top prize; bows and guns next; cloth and silk after; pearls and jade last.

sentences.zh: 自成不好酒色，脫粟粗糲，與其下共甘苦。

translations.literal: Zicheng did not love wine or women; he ate coarse millet and shared hardship with his men.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng cared nothing for wine or women, ate coarse grain, and shared every hardship with his troops.

sentences.zh: 汝才妻妾數十，被服紈綺，帳下女樂數部，厚自奉養，自成嘗嗤鄙之。

translations.literal: Rucai had dozens of wives and concubines, wore silk gauze, kept several troupes of female musicians under his tent, and indulged himself richly; Zicheng often sneered at and despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai kept dozens of concubines, dressed in silk, maintained female musicians, and lived in luxury—which Zicheng openly scorned.

sentences.zh: 汝才眾數十萬，用山西舉人吉珪為謀主。

translations.literal: Rucai's host numbered several hundred thousand; he employed the Shanxi presented scholar Ji Gui as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai commanded hundreds of thousands and relied on the Shanxi jinshi Ji Gui as his adviser.

sentences.zh: 自成善攻，汝才善戰，兩人相須若左右手。

translations.literal: Zicheng was skilled at siege, Rucai at field battle; the two relied on each other like left and right hands.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng excelled at sieges, Rucai at open battle—they depended on each other like two hands.

sentences.zh: 自成下宛、葉，克梁、宋，兵強士附，有專制心，顧獨忌汝才。

translations.literal: Zicheng had taken Wan, Ye, Liang, and Song; his soldiers were strong and the people attached to him; he had a mind to monopolize power, yet he alone feared Rucai.
translations.idiomatic: Having seized Wan, Ye, Liang, and Song, with a mighty army and growing ambition to rule alone, he still feared only Rucai.

sentences.zh: 乃召汝才所善賀一龍宴，縛之，晨以二十騎斬汝才於帳中，悉兼其眾。

translations.literal: He then summoned He Yilong, whom Rucai favored, to a feast, bound him, and at dawn sent twenty horsemen to behead Rucai in his tent and wholly absorbed his host.
translations.idiomatic: He invited Rucai's ally He Yilong to a banquet, seized him, and at dawn sent twenty riders to cut Rucai down in his tent and absorb his entire force.

sentences.zh: 自成在中州，所略城輒焚毀之。

translations.literal: Zicheng in the Central Plain burned every city he took.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Central Plain, every city Zicheng captured was burned.

sentences.zh: 及渡漢江，謀以荊、襄為根本，改襄陽曰襄京，修襄王宮殿居之。

translations.literal: After crossing the Han River he planned to make Jing and Xiang his base, changed Xiangyang to Xiangjing, repaired the Prince of Xiang's palace, and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Han he made Jing and Xiang his base, renamed Xiangyang Xiangjing, restored the Prince of Xiang's palace, and made it his seat.

sentences.zh: 改禹州曰均平府，承天府曰揚武州，他府縣多所更易。

translations.literal: He changed Yuzhou to Junping Prefecture, Chengtian to Yangwu Prefecture, and changed many other prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou became Junping Prefecture, Chengtian Yangwu Prefecture, and he renamed cities across the region.

sentences.zh: 牛金星教以創官爵名號，大行署置。

translations.literal: Niu Jinxing taught him to create titles and ranks; he appointed officials on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Jinxing devised offices and ranks; Zicheng filled posts on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 自成無子，兄子過及妻弟高一功，迭居左右，親信用事。

translations.literal: Zicheng had no son; his elder brother's son Guo and his wife's younger brother Gao Yigong alternately attended at his side and were trusted with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he relied on his nephew Guo and his brother-in-law Gao Yigong, who attended him in turn and held real power.

sentences.zh: 田見秀、劉宗敏為權將軍，李岩、賀錦、劉希堯等為制將軍，張鼐、黨守素等為威武將軍，谷可成、任維榮等為果毅將軍，凡五營二十二將。

translations.literal: Tian Jianxiu and Liu Zongmin were made Quan generals; Li Yan, He Jin, Liu Xiyao, and others were made Zhi generals; Zhang Nai, Dang Shousu, and others were made Wei generals; Gu Kecheng, Ren Weirong, and others were made Guo generals—in all twenty-two generals of the five camps.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jianxiu and Liu Zongmin became Quan generals; Li Yan, He Jin, and Liu Xiyao became Zhi generals; Zhang Nai and Dang Shousu became Wei generals; Gu Kecheng and Ren Weirong became Guo generals—twenty-two commanders in all.

sentences.zh: 又置上相、左輔、右弼、六政府侍郎、郎中、從事等官。

translations.literal: He also set up Chief Minister, Left Assistant, Right Assistant, Vice Ministers and Directors of the Six Governments, Attendants, and other offices.
translations.idiomatic: He also created Chief Minister, Left and Right Assistants, vice ministers, directors, and attendants for his six ministries.

sentences.zh: 要地設防禦使，府曰尹，州曰牧，縣曰令。

translations.literal: At strategic points he set defense commissioners; prefectures had Yin, departments Mu, counties Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Key posts received defense commissioners; prefectures had governors called Yin, departments Mu, counties Ling.

sentences.zh: 封崇王由樻襄陽伯、邵陵王在城棗陽伯、保甯王紹圮宣城伯、肅甯王術授順義伯。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Prince Chong Yougui as Marquis of Xiangyang, Prince Shaoling Zaicheng as Marquis of Zaoyang, Prince Baoning Shaoqi as Marquis of Xuancheng, and Prince Sunning Shushou as Marquis of Shunyi.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled Prince Chong Yougui as Marquis of Xiangyang, Prince Shaoling Zaicheng as Marquis of Zaoyang, Prince Baoning Shaoqi as Marquis of Xuancheng, and Prince Sunning Shushou as Marquis of Shunyi.

sentences.zh: 以張國紳為上相，牛金星為左輔，來儀為右弼。

translations.literal: He appointed Zhang Guoshen Chief Minister, Niu Jinxing Left Assistant, and Lai Yi Right Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoshen became Chief Minister, Niu Jinxing Left Assistant, Lai Yi Right Assistant.

sentences.zh: 國紳，安定人，嘗官參政。

translations.literal: Guoshen was a man of Anding who had once served as Administrative Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Guoshen, from Anding, had once been an administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既降，獻文翔鳳妻鄧氏以媚自成。

translations.literal: After he surrendered, he presented Minister Wen Xiangfeng's wife Lady Deng to please Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: After surrendering he offered Minister Wen Xiangfeng's wife Lady Deng to curry favor.

sentences.zh: 自成惡其傷同類，殺之，而歸鄧氏於其家。

translations.literal: Zicheng detested this injury to his own kind and killed him, returning Lady Deng to her family.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng, loathing the betrayal of his own kind, executed him and sent Lady Deng home.

sentences.zh: 六政府侍郎則石首喻上猷、江陵蕭應坤、招遠楊永裕、米脂李振聲、江陵鄧岩忠、西安姚錫胤，尋以宣城丘之陶代振聲為兵政府侍郎。

translations.literal: Vice Ministers of the Six Governments were Yu Shangyou of Shishou, Xiao Yingkun of Jiangling, Yang Yongyu of Zhaoyuan, Li Zhensheng of Mizhi, Deng Yanzhong of Jiangling, and Yao Xiyin of Xi'an; soon Qiu Zhitao of Xuancheng replaced Zhensheng as Vice Minister of the Military Government.
translations.idiomatic: Vice ministers included Yu Shangyou, Xiao Yingkun, Yang Yongyu, Li Zhensheng, Deng Yanzhong, and Yao Xiyin; later Qiu Zhitao replaced Zhensheng at the Military Ministry.

sentences.zh: 其餘受偽職者甚眾，不具載。

translations.literal: The rest who received false offices were very numerous and are not all recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Countless others took false titles; they are not all listed here.

sentences.zh: 使高一功、馮雄守襄陽，任繼光守荊州，藺養成、牛萬才守夷陵，王文曜守澧州，白旺守安陸，蕭雲林守荊門，謝應龍守漢川，周鳳梧守萬禹州。

translations.literal: He sent Gao Yigong and Feng Xiong to guard Xiangyang, Ren Jiguang Jingzhou, Lin Yangcheng and Niu Wancai Yiling, Wang Wenyao Lizhou, Bai Wang Anlu, Xiao Yunlin Jingmen, Xie Yinglong Hanchuan, and Zhou Fengwu Wanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yigong and Feng Xiong held Xiangyang; Ren Jiguang Jingzhou; Lin Yangcheng and Niu Wancai Yiling; Wang Wenyao Lizhou; Bai Wang Anlu; Xiao Yunlin Jingmen; Xie Yinglong Hanchuan; Zhou Fengwu Wanzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是河南、湖廣、江北諸賊莫不聽命。

translations.literal: Thereupon the bandits of Henan, Huguang, and Jiangbei all obeyed his orders.
translations.idiomatic: From Henan to Huguang and Jiangbei, every major rebel band answered to him.

sentences.zh: 自成既殺汝才、一龍，又襲殺養成，奪守應兵，擊殺袁時中於杞縣。

translations.literal: After Zicheng had killed Rucai and Yilong, he also launched a surprise attack and killed Yangcheng, seized Shouying's troops, and in battle killed Yuan Shizhong at Qixian.
translations.idiomatic: Having killed Rucai and Yilong, he ambushed and killed Lin Yangcheng, absorbed Ma Shouying's army, and slew Yuan Shizhong at Qixian.

sentences.zh: 獻忠方據武昌，自成遣使賀，且脅之曰：「老回回已降，曹操輩誅死，行及汝矣。」

translations.literal: Xianzhong was then holding Wuchang; Zicheng sent envoys to congratulate him and also threatened, saying: "Old Muslim has surrendered; Cao Cao and his ilk are executed and dead—the turn will soon come to you."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong held Wuchang; Zicheng sent messengers with congratulations and a threat: "Old Muslim has submitted; Cao Cao and the rest are dead—you are next."

sentences.zh: 獻忠大懼，南入長沙。

translations.literal: Xianzhong was greatly afraid and marched south into Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zhang Xianzhong fled south into Changsha.

sentences.zh: 當是時，十三家七十二營諸大賊，降死殆盡，惟自成、獻忠存，而自成獨勁，遂自稱曰新順王。

translations.literal: At that time of the thirteen great bandits and seventy-two camps, nearly all had surrendered or died; only Zicheng and Xianzhong remained, and Zicheng alone was formidable; he then styled himself the New Shun King.
translations.idiomatic: Of the thirteen great chieftains and seventy-two camps, nearly all were dead or surrendered; only Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong endured, and Zicheng alone stood supreme—he styled himself the New Shun King.

sentences.zh: 集牛金星等議兵所向。

translations.literal: He gathered Niu Jinxing and others to deliberate where the army should go.
translations.idiomatic: He convened Niu Jinxing and his advisers to decide their next march.

sentences.zh: 金星請先取河北，直走京師。

translations.literal: Jinxing requested first taking Hebei and marching straight on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jinxing urged seizing Hebei and marching directly on Beijing.

sentences.zh: 楊永裕請下金陵，斷燕都糧道。

translations.literal: Yang Yongyu requested descending on Jinling and cutting the grain route of the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yongyu proposed taking Nanjing and severing the capital's grain supply.

sentences.zh: 從事顧君恩曰：「金陵居下流，事雖濟，失之緩。

translations.literal: Attendant Gu Jun'en said: "Jinling lies downriver; though the affair might succeed, it would be faulted as too slow.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gu Jun'en argued: "Nanjing lies downstream; even if we took it, the campaign would be faulted as too slow.

sentences.zh: 直走京師，不勝，退安所歸，失之急。

translations.literal: March straight on the capital; if we do not win, where shall we retreat? It would be faulted as too hasty.
translations.idiomatic: A direct strike on Beijing risks defeat with nowhere to retreat—faulted as too rash.

sentences.zh: 關中，大王桑梓邦也，百二山河，得天下三分之二，宜先取之，建立基業。

translations.literal: Guanzhong is the Great King's native country; with its hundred fortified rivers and mountains, one obtains two-thirds of the realm—it should be taken first to establish a foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong is your homeland, defended by a hundred rivers and mountains—you would hold two-thirds of the empire. Take it first and build your base.

sentences.zh: 然後旁略三邊，資其兵力，攻取山西，後向京師，庶幾進戰退守，萬全無失。」

translations.literal: Then overrun the three frontiers, draw on their military strength, seize Shanxi, and afterward advance on the capital—then advance in battle and retreat in defense, with nothing lost."
translations.idiomatic: Then overrun the frontier garrisons, enlist their soldiers, seize Shanxi, and only then march on Beijing—advance when you can, retreat when you must, with every advantage."

sentences.zh: 自成從之。

translations.literal: Zicheng followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng adopted the plan.

sentences.zh: 傳庭之敗於柿園而歸陝也，大治兵，制火車二萬輛，募壯士，使白廣恩、高傑將，欲俟賊饑而擊之。

translations.literal: When Chuanating returned to Shaanxi after defeat at Persimmon Garden, he greatly trained troops, made twenty thousand fire-wagons, recruited stalwarts, and had Bai Guangen and Gao Jie lead them, intending to wait until the bandits were hungry and strike.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated at Persimmon Garden, Sun Chuanating returned to Shaanxi, drilled his army, built twenty thousand fire-carts, recruited tough fighters under Bai Guangen and Gao Jie, and planned to strike when the rebels ran short of food.

sentences.zh: 朝議日督戰，不得已出關。

translations.literal: Court discussion daily pressed for battle; he had no choice but to go out of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: The court daily demanded action; he had no choice but to march out.

sentences.zh: 以牛成虎、盧光祖為前鋒，由靈寶入洛。

translations.literal: He made Niu Chenghu and Lu Guangzu the vanguard and entered Luoyang by Lingbao.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Chenghu and Lu Guangzu led the van through Lingbao into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 高傑為是中軍，檄廣恩從新安來會。

translations.literal: Gao Jie was the central army; he summoned Guangen from Xin'an to join.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jie commanded the center and ordered Guangen to rendezvous from Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 河南將陳永福守新灘，四川將秦翼明出商、洛，為掎角。

translations.literal: Henan commander Chen Yongfu held Xintan; Sichuan commander Qin Yiming came out from Shang and Luo as pincers.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yongfu held Xintan on the Henan front; Qin Yiming marched from Shang and Luo on the Sichuan wing to pinch the enemy.

sentences.zh: 前鋒敗賊澠池，至寶豐，再拔其城。

translations.literal: The vanguard defeated the bandits at Mianchi, reached Baofeng, and again took its city.
translations.idiomatic: The van beat the rebels at Mianchi, reached Baofeng, and retook the city.

sentences.zh: 次郟。

translations.literal: They halted at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: They camped at Ye.

sentences.zh: 自成率萬騎還戰，復大敗，幾被擒。

translations.literal: Zicheng led ten thousand horsemen to give battle and again suffered a great defeat, nearly being captured.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng rode out with ten thousand horses, was routed again, and nearly captured.

sentences.zh: 會天大雨，道濘，糧車不進。

translations.literal: It happened that heaven sent down great rain; the roads were mire; grain wagons could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Then the skies opened; roads turned to mud and supply wagons stalled.

sentences.zh: 自成遣輕騎出汝州，要截糧道。

translations.literal: Zicheng sent light cavalry out from Ruzhou to intercept the grain route.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng dispatched light cavalry from Ruzhou to cut the supply line.

sentences.zh: 傳庭乃分軍三，令廣恩從大道，令高傑親隨從間道，迎糧，令永福守營。

translations.literal: Chuanating then divided the army in three, ordering Guangen by the main road, Gao Jie with his personal guard by the bypath to meet the grain, and Yongfu to hold the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanating split his force: Guangen on the main road, Gao Jie with his guard by a side path to escort supplies, Yongfu to hold camp.

sentences.zh: 傳庭既行，永福兵亦爭發，不可禁，遂為賊所躡。

translations.literal: After Chuanating had marched, Yongfu's troops also vied to set out and could not be restrained; they were then trailed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chuanating left, Yongfu's men rushed out unrestrained and were shadowed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 至南陽，傳庭還戰，賊陣五重，官軍克其三。

translations.literal: Reaching Nanyang, Chuanating turned to fight; the bandit formation was five ranks deep; government troops broke through three.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanyang, Chuanating turned to fight through five rebel lines and broke three.

sentences.zh: 已而稍卻，火車奔，騎兵亦大奔。

translations.literal: Presently they fell back slightly; the fire-wagons fled, and the cavalry also fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Then the line buckled; fire-carts bolted, and the cavalry stampeded.

sentences.zh: 賊縱鐵騎踐之，傳庭大敗。

translations.literal: The bandits unleashed iron cavalry to trample them; Chuanating suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel iron cavalry rode them down; Chuanating's army was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 自成空壁追，一日夜逾四百里，官軍死者四萬余人，失兵器輜重數十萬。

translations.literal: Zicheng pursued with empty camps for a day and night, covering more than four hundred li in one day; government troops dead numbered more than forty thousand; weapons and baggage lost numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng pursued with stripped camps for a day and night, covering four hundred li; more than forty thousand government troops died; arms and baggage losses ran into the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 傳庭奔河北，轉趨潼關，氣敗沮不復振。

translations.literal: Chuanating fled to Hebei, then turned toward Tong Pass; his spirit was broken and he could not rally.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanating fled toward Hebei, then turned for Tong Pass, broken in spirit and beyond recovery.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，自成陷潼關，傳庭死，遂連破華陰、渭南、華、商、臨潼。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, Zicheng took Tong Pass; Chuanating died; he then took in succession Huayin, Weinan, Hua, Shang, and Lintong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zicheng stormed Tong Pass; Chuanating fell; then Huayin, Weinan, Hua, Shang, and Lintong fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 進攻西安，守將王根子開東門納賊。

translations.literal: He pressed the attack on Xi'an; defending general Wang Genzi opened the east gate to admit the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Xi'an; the defender Wang Genzi opened the east gate to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 自成執秦王存樞以為權將軍，永壽王誼曈為制將軍。

translations.literal: Zicheng seized Prince Qin Cunshu to make him a Quan general, and Prince Yongshou Yitang a Zhi general.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Prince Qin Cunshu as a Quan general and Prince Yongshou Yitang as a Zhi general.

sentences.zh: 巡撫馮師孔以下死者十余人，布政使陸之祺等俱降。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Feng Shikong and more than ten others below him died; Administrative Commissioner Lu Zhiqi and others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Feng Shikong and more than ten officials died; Administrative Commissioner Lu Zhiqi and others surrendered.

sentences.zh: 自成大掠三日，下令禁止。

translations.literal: Zicheng plundered greatly for three days, then issued orders forbidding it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng looted freely for three days, then forbade further pillage.

sentences.zh: 改西安曰長安，稱西京。

translations.literal: He changed Xi'an to Chang'an and called it the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed Xi'an Chang'an and proclaimed it the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 賜顧君恩女樂一部，賞入關策也。

translations.literal: He bestowed on Gu Jun'en a troupe of female musicians as reward for the strategy of entering the pass.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded Gu Jun'en with a troupe of female musicians for the plan to take Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 大發民，修長安城，開馳道。

translations.literal: He conscripted the people on a grand scale to repair the walls of Chang'an and open imperial highways.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted the populace en masse to rebuild Chang'an's walls and open imperial roads.

sentences.zh: 自成每三日親赴教場校射，百姓望見黃龍纛，咸伏地呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Every three days Zicheng personally went to the drill ground to inspect archery; the people, seeing the yellow dragon pennant, all prostrated themselves calling "ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Every three days Zicheng inspected archery at the drill ground; commoners who saw his yellow dragon banner kowtowed and shouted "Long live ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 諸將白廣恩、高汝利、左光先、梁甫先行後皆降。

translations.literal: The generals Bai Guangen, Gao Ruli, Zuo Guangxian, and Liang Fu, who had gone ahead, all afterward surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Bai Guangen, Gao Ruli, Zuo Guangxian, and Liang Fu, who had marched ahead, all surrendered in turn.

sentences.zh: 陳永福以先射中自成目，保山巔不敢下，自成折箭為誓，招之，亦降。

translations.literal: Chen Yongfu, because he had earlier shot Zicheng in the eye, held a mountain fastness and dared not come down; Zicheng broke an arrow as oath and summoned him, and he too surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yongfu, who had put out Zicheng's eye, held the mountains and would not descend until Zicheng snapped an arrow in pledge and called him down—then he too submitted.

sentences.zh: 惟高傑以竊自成妻走延安，為李過所追，折而東，渡宜川，絕蒲津以守。

translations.literal: Only Gao Jie, because he had stolen Zicheng's wife and fled to Yan'an, was pursued by Li Guo, turned east, crossed Yichuan, and blocked the Pu ford to hold his ground.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gao Jie, who had run off with Zicheng's wife to Yan'an, was chased by Li Guo, veered east, crossed Yichuan, seized the Pu crossing, and held firm.

sentences.zh: 自成兵所至風靡，乃詣米脂祭墓。

translations.literal: Wherever Zicheng's troops went, resistance crumbled; he then went to Mizhi to sacrifice at his ancestors' tombs.
translations.idiomatic: His armies swept all before them; he returned to Mizhi to worship at his family graves.

sentences.zh: 向為軍所發，焚棄遺骴，築土封之。

translations.literal: They had earlier been dug up by government troops, burned and abandoned as exposed bones; he heaped earth and sealed them anew.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops had once desecrated the graves, leaving bare bones; he piled earth and resealed the mounds.

sentences.zh: 求其宗人，贈金封爵以去。

translations.literal: He sought out his clansmen, bestowed gold, enfeoffed them, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He found his kinsmen, gave them gold and titles, and sent them on their way.

sentences.zh: 改延安府曰天保府，米脂曰天保縣，清澗曰天波府。

translations.literal: He changed Yan'an Prefecture to Tianbao Prefecture, Mizhi to Tianbao County, and Qingjian to Tianbo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan'an became Tianbao Prefecture, Mizhi Tianbao County, Qingjian Tianbo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔不下，屠之。

translations.literal: Fengxiang would not submit; he massacred it.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang resisted; he slaughtered the city.

sentences.zh: 始，自成入陝西，自謂故鄉，毋有侵暴，未一月抄掠如故。

translations.literal: At first, when Zicheng entered Shaanxi, he said it was his homeland and there would be no pillaging; within a month plunder resumed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Shaanxi he had promised no looting in his homeland; within a month the pillaging resumed.

sentences.zh: 又以士大夫必不附己，悉索諸薦紳，搒掠征其金，死者瘞一穴。

translations.literal: He also believed that gentry and officials would surely not attach themselves to him; he searched out all recommended scholars and gentry, flogged and extorted gold from them, and those who died were buried in one pit.
translations.idiomatic: Believing scholars would never join him willingly, he hunted down every local notable, tortured them for gold, and threw the dead into a common pit.

sentences.zh: 榆林故死守，李過等不能克，自成大發兵攻陷之。

translations.literal: Yulin had long defended stubbornly; Li Guo and others could not take it; Zicheng sent a great army and stormed it to capture.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin had held out fiercely; Li Guo could not crack it until Zicheng threw his main army against the walls.

sentences.zh: 副使都任，總兵王世國、尤世威等，俱不屈死。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Du Ren, Commanders Wang Shiguo, You Shiwei, and others all died refusing to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Du Ren and generals Wang Shiguo and You Shiwei died defiant rather than yield.

sentences.zh: 乘勝取寧夏，屠慶陽，執韓王亶脊。

translations.literal: Pressing his victory he took Ningxia, massacred Qingyang, and seized Prince Han Danji.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Ningxia, massacred Qingyang, and captured Prince Han Danji.

sentences.zh: 移攻蘭州，甘肅巡撫林日端等亦死。

translations.literal: He shifted to attack Lanzhou; Grand Coordinator of Gansu Lin Riduan and others also died.
translations.idiomatic: He turned on Lanzhou; Gansu Grand Coordinator Lin Riduan and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 進陷西寧，於是肅州、山丹、永昌、鎮番、莊浪皆降，陝西地悉歸自成。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Xining; thereupon Suzhou, Shandan, Yongchang, Zhenfan, and Zhuanglang all surrendered, and Shaanxi territory wholly returned to Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xining fell, then Suzhou, Shandan, Yongchang, Zhenfan, and Zhuanglang submitted—Shaanxi was entirely his.

sentences.zh: 又遣賊渡河，陷平陽，殺宗室三百餘人。

translations.literal: He also sent bandits across the river to take Pingyang and kill more than three hundred members of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent columns across the Yellow River to seize Pingyang and slaughter more than three hundred imperial clansmen.

sentences.zh: 高傑奔澤州。

translations.literal: Gao Jie fled to Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jie fled to Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 詔以余應桂總督三邊，收邊兵剿賊，然全陝已沒，應桂不能進。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yu Yinggui grand coordinator of the three frontiers to gather frontier troops and suppress the bandits; but all Shaanxi was already lost, and Yinggui could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Yu Yinggui to command the three frontiers and gather border troops, but Shaanxi was already gone and he could not march.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月庚寅朔，自成稱王于西安，僭國號曰大順，改元永昌，改名自晟。

translations.literal: On gengyin, New Year's day of the first month of the seventeenth year, Zicheng declared himself king at Xi'an, usurped the state name Great Shun, changed the era to Yongchang, and changed his name to Zisheng.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of Chongzhen 17, Li Zicheng declared himself king at Xi'an, proclaimed the Great Shun dynasty, adopted the era Yongchang, and took the name Zisheng.

sentences.zh: 追尊其曾祖以下，加諡號，以李繼遷為太祖。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his great-grandfather and below with posthumous titles, taking Li Jiqian as Imperial Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled his ancestors with posthumous titles and named the Tangut prince Li Jiqian as dynastic founder.

sentences.zh: 設天佑殿大學士，以牛金星為之。

translations.literal: He set up the Hall of Heavenly Blessings Grand Academician, appointing Niu Jinxing to it.
translations.idiomatic: He created the Hall of Heavenly Blessings Grand Academician and appointed Niu Jinxing.

sentences.zh: 增置六政府尚書，設弘文館、文諭院、諫議、直指使、從政、統會、尚契司、驗馬寺、知政使、書寫房等官。

translations.literal: He added Ministers of the Six Governments, set up the Hongwen Hall, Wenyuan Academy, Remonstrance Office, Direct-Pointing Commissioners, Administration, General Assembly, Seal-Keeping Office, Horse-Inspection Temple, Policy Commissioners, Writing Office, and other posts.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded the six ministries, founded the Hongwen Hall, Wenyuan Academy, remonstrance office, censors, policy boards, seal office, horse inspection bureau, and secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以乾州宋企郊為吏政尚書、平湖陸之祺為戶政尚書、真甯鞏焴為禮政尚書、歸安張嶙然為兵政尚書。

translations.literal: He appointed Song Qijiao of Qianzhou Minister of Civil Government, Lu Zhiqi of Pinghu Minister of Revenue, Gong Huang of Zhenning Minister of Rites, and Zhang Linran of Gui'an Minister of Military Government.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qijiao of Qianzhou became Minister of Personnel, Lu Zhiqi of Pinghu Minister of Revenue, Gong Huang of Zhenning Minister of Rites, and Zhang Linran of Gui'an Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 復五等爵，大封功臣，侯劉宗敏以下九人，伯劉體純以下七十二人，子三十人，男五十五人。

translations.literal: He restored the five ranks of nobility and enfeoffed his meritorious followers on a grand scale: nine marquises from Liu Zongmin downward, seventy-two earls from Liu Tichun downward, thirty viscounts, and fifty-five barons.
translations.idiomatic: The five noble ranks were restored and the great captains rewarded: nine marquises beginning with Liu Zongmin, seventy-two earls from Liu Tichun, thirty viscounts, and fifty-five barons.

sentences.zh: 定軍制。

translations.literal: He fixed the military regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Military discipline was codified.

sentences.zh: 有一馬儳行列者斬之，馬騰入田苗者斬之。

translations.literal: Whoever had a horse but fell out of rank was beheaded; whoever let his horse trample fields or crops was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Any rider whose mount broke formation was executed; any whose horse ran into grain or seedlings was executed.

sentences.zh: 籍步兵四十萬、馬兵六十萬。

translations.literal: He registered four hundred thousand foot soldiers and six hundred thousand cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The rolls listed four hundred thousand infantry and six hundred thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 兵政侍郎楊王休為都肄，出橫門，至渭橋，金鼓動地。

translations.literal: Yang Wangxiu, Vice Minister of Military Affairs, served as commander of the muster; they marched out through Heng Gate to Wei Bridge with drums and gongs shaking the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Yang Wangxiu directed the grand review; the host filed out Heng Gate to Wei Bridge amid thundering drums.

sentences.zh: 令弘文館學士李化鱗等草檄馳諭遠近，指斥乘輿。

translations.literal: He ordered Hongwen Hall academicians Li Hualin and others to draft proclamations and dispatch them far and near, denouncing the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians of the Hongwen Hall, led by Li Hualin, drafted manifestos sent across the realm condemning the emperor.

sentences.zh: 是日，大風霾，黃霧四塞。

translations.literal: That day a great wind blew; yellow dust filled the sky on every side.
translations.idiomatic: That day a gale rose and yellow dust blotted out the horizon.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝大驚，召廷臣議。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, the emperor was greatly alarmed and summoned his ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: News of the march threw the emperor into alarm; he called the court into council.

sentences.zh: 大學士李建泰請督師，帝許之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Jiantai asked to take command in person; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Jiantai volunteered to lead the armies; the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 時山西自平陽陷，河津、稷山、滎河皆陷，他府縣多望風送款。

translations.literal: By then Pingyang in Shanxi had fallen, along with Hejin, Jishan, and Ronghe; other prefectures and counties mostly surrendered at the first approach.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang was lost, then Hejin, Jishan, and Ronghe; across Shanxi, city after city opened its gates without a fight.

sentences.zh: 二月，自成渡河，破汾州，徇河曲、靜樂，攻太原，執晉王求桂，巡撫蔡懋德死之。

translations.literal: In the second month Zicheng crossed the Yellow River, stormed Fenzhou, swept Hequ and Jingle, and attacked Taiyuan; he seized Prince Jin Guiqiu, and Grand Coordinator Cai Maode died defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Li Zicheng crossed the river, took Fenzhou, overran Hequ and Jingle, and besieged Taiyuan; Prince Jin was captured, Grand Coordinator Cai Maode killed.

sentences.zh: 北徇忻、代，甯武總兵周遇吉戰死。

translations.literal: He drove north through Xin and Dai; Regional Commander Zhou Yuji of Ningwu died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed north into Xin and Dai; Zhou Yuji, commander at Ningwu, fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 自成先遣遊兵入故關，掠大名、真定而北。

translations.literal: Zicheng first sent raiding parties through the old pass to plunder Daming and Zhending and swing north.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng sent scouts through the old frontier pass to ravage Daming and Zhending before turning north.

sentences.zh: 身率眾賊並邊東犯，陷大同，巡撫衛景瑗、總兵硃三樂死。

translations.literal: He himself led the main rebel host east along the border, took Datong, and Grand Coordinator Wei Jingyuan and Regional Commander Zhu Sanle died.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of the main army he struck along the frontier, seized Datong, and killed Wei Jingyuan and Zhu Sanle.

sentences.zh: 自成殺代王傳齊，代籓宗室殆盡。

translations.literal: Zicheng killed Prince Dai Chuanqi; the princely house of Dai was nearly exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng killed Prince Dai Chuanqi and nearly wiped out the entire princely clan.

sentences.zh: 犯宣府，總兵姜環迎降，巡撫硃之馮死。

translations.literal: He attacked Xuanfu; Regional Commander Jiang Huan welcomed him in, and Grand Coordinator Zhu Zhifeng died.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanfu, Jiang Huan surrendered; Zhu Zhifeng died resisting.

sentences.zh: 遂犯陽和，由柳溝逼居庸，總兵官唐通、太監杜之秩迎降。

translations.literal: He then struck Yanghe, pressed Juyong through Liugou, and Regional Commander Tang Tong and Eunuch Du Zhijie surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He drove on Yanghe, forced Juyong via Liugou, and Tang Tong and the eunuch Du Zhijie submitted.

sentences.zh: 三月十三日，焚昌平，總兵官李守鑅死。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the third month he burned Changping; Regional Commander Li Shouzhen died.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth of the third month Changping burned; Li Shouzhen was killed.

sentences.zh: 始，賊欲偵京師虛實，往往陰遣人輦重貨，賈販都市，又令充部院諸掾吏，探刺機密。

translations.literal: At first the rebels wished to spy out the capital's strength; they often secretly sent men bearing heavy goods to trade in the markets, and also planted agents among the clerks of ministries and boards to probe state secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Li Zicheng probed Beijing: agents posing as merchants flooded the markets with goods, while others infiltrated the ministries as clerks to steal secrets.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有謀議，數千里立馳報。

translations.literal: When the court debated policy, reports raced a thousand li to reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Court deliberations were relayed to the rebel camp within days.

sentences.zh: 及抵昌平，兵部發騎探賊，賊輒勾之降，無一還者。

translations.literal: When they reached Changping, the Ministry of War sent cavalry to scout the rebels; the rebels always induced them to defect, and not one returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Changping the Ministry of War sent scouts; every man was turned or killed—none came back.

sentences.zh: 賊游騎至平則門，京師猶不知也。

translations.literal: Rebel patrols reached Pingze Gate while the capital still did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel horsemen were at Pingze Gate before Beijing knew war had come.

sentences.zh: 十七日，帝召問群臣，莫對，有泣者。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth the emperor summoned the ministers for counsel; none could answer, and some wept.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth he called his ministers; none had a plan, and many wept.

sentences.zh: 俄頃賊環攻九門，門外先設三大營，悉降賊。

translations.literal: Presently the rebels ringed and assaulted the Nine Gates; three great camps had been set outside the walls and all surrendered to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Nine Gates were besieged; the three camps outside had already gone over to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 京師久乏餉，乘陴者少，益以內侍。

translations.literal: The capital had long lacked pay; few manned the battlements, and eunuchs were added to the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Pay was exhausted, defenders scarce on the walls, and eunuchs pressed into service.

sentences.zh: 內侍專守城事，百司不敢問。

translations.literal: Eunuchs monopolized the defense; the hundred offices dared not question them.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs controlled the walls; no civil official dared interfere.

sentences.zh: 十八日，賊攻益急，自成駐彰義門外，遣降賊太監杜勳縋入見帝，求禪位。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth the assault grew fiercer; Zicheng halted outside Zhangyi Gate and sent the surrendered eunuch Du Xun down on a rope to see the emperor and demand abdication.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth the attack intensified; Li Zicheng waited at Zhangyi Gate and sent the turncoat eunuch Du Xun to demand the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，叱之下，詔親征。

translations.literal: The emperor in rage drove him away and issued an edict for a personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged, dismissed him, and proclaimed he would lead the army himself.

sentences.zh: 日暝，太監曹化淳啟彰義門，賊盡入。

translations.literal: At dusk Eunuch Cao Huachun opened Zhangyi Gate and the rebels poured in.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Cao Huachun opened Zhangyi Gate; the rebels flooded the city.

sentences.zh: 帝出宮，登煤山，望烽火徹天，歎息曰：「苦我民耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor left the palace, climbed Coal Hill, and gazing at signal fires blazing across the sky sighed: "My people suffer."
translations.idiomatic: He left the palace, climbed Coal Hill, saw beacon fires everywhere, and sighed: "My people—what they endure."

sentences.zh: 徘徊久之，歸乾清宮，令送太子及永王、定王于戚臣周奎、田弘遇第，劍擊長公主，趣皇后自盡。

translations.literal: He wandered long, then returned to the Palace of Heavenly Purity, sent the crown prince and Princes Yong and Ding to the houses of his in-laws Zhou Kui and Tian Hongyu, struck down the eldest princess with his sword, and urged the empress to take her own life.
translations.idiomatic: He wandered, then returned to Qianqing Palace, sent the crown prince and Princes Yong and Ding to Zhou Kui and Tian Hongyu, cut down the eldest princess, and ordered the empress to die.

sentences.zh: 十九日丁未，天未明，皇城不守，嗚鐘集百官，無至者。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth, dingwei, before dawn the inner city could not be held; the bell was rung to assemble the officials, but none came.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn on the nineteenth the inner city fell; the court bell rang, and no minister came.

sentences.zh: 乃復登煤山，書衣襟為遺詔，以帛自縊於山亭，帝遂崩。

translations.literal: He climbed Coal Hill again, wrote his testament on his robe, and hanged himself with silk in the hill pavilion; thus the emperor perished.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed Coal Hill again, wrote his last words on his robe, and hanged himself in the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 太監王承恩縊於側。

translations.literal: Eunuch Wang Chengen hanged himself at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Chengen hanged himself beside him.

sentences.zh: 自成毰笠縹衣，乘烏駁馬，入承天門。

translations.literal: Zicheng wore a straw hat and light silk robe and rode a piebald horse through the Gate of Accepting Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng entered through the Gate of Accepting Heaven in a straw hat and pale silk, riding a piebald horse.

sentences.zh: 偽丞相牛金星，尚書宋企郊、喻上猷，侍郎黎志升、張嶙然等騎而從。

translations.literal: The false Chancellor Niu Jinxing and Ministers Song Qijiao and Yu Shangyou, Vice Ministers Li Zhisheng and Zhang Linran, and others rode behind.
translations.idiomatic: Behind him rode the false chancellor Niu Jinxing, ministers Song Qijiao and Yu Shangyou, and vice ministers Li Zhisheng and Zhang Linran.

sentences.zh: 登皇極殿，據御座，下令大索帝后，期百官三日朝見。

translations.literal: He ascended the Hall of Supreme Harmony, took the imperial seat, and ordered a great search for the emperor and empress, fixing three days for the hundred officials to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: He took the throne in the Hall of Supreme Harmony and ordered the emperor and empress hunted down, giving officials three days to present themselves.

sentences.zh: 文臣自范景文、勳戚自劉文炳以下，殉節者四十餘人。

translations.literal: From civil officials such as Fan Jingwen to enfeoffed kin such as Liu Wenbing, more than forty died loyal.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty officials and nobles—from Fan Jingwen to Liu Wenbing—died refusing submission.

sentences.zh: 宮女魏氏投河，從者二百餘人。

translations.literal: Palace woman Wei threw herself into the river, and more than two hundred followed.
translations.idiomatic: Palace woman Wei drowned herself; over two hundred attendants followed.

sentences.zh: 象房象皆哀吼流淚。

translations.literal: The elephants in the elephant quarters all wailed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Court elephants trumpeted and wept.

sentences.zh: 太子投周奎家，不得入，二王亦不能匿，先後擁至，皆不屈，自成羈之宮中。

translations.literal: The crown prince fled to Zhou Kui's house but could not enter; the two princes likewise could not hide and were seized in turn; all refused to bow, and Zicheng held them in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was turned away at Zhou Kui's door; the two princes were captured; all refused to kneel, and Li Zicheng imprisoned them in the palace.

sentences.zh: 長公主絕而復蘇，舁至，令賊劉宗敏療治。

translations.literal: The eldest princess, having died and revived, was carried in; Zicheng ordered the rebel Liu Zongmin to treat her wounds.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest princess, cut down but still alive, was brought before Liu Zongmin for medical care.

sentences.zh: 已，乃知帝后崩，自成命以宮扉載出，盛柳棺，置東華門外，百姓過者皆掩泣。

translations.literal: Later, learning the emperor and empress were dead, Zicheng had them carried out on palace doors, placed in willow coffins, and set outside Donghua Gate; passersby all covered their faces and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the sovereigns were dead, he had their bodies borne out on palace doors in willow coffins at Donghua Gate; the people wept as they passed.

sentences.zh: 越三日己酉，味爽，成國公硃純臣、大學士魏藻德率文武百官入賀，皆素服坐殿前。

translations.literal: Three days later, on jiyou at dawn, Duke Zhu Chunchen and Grand Secretary Wei Zaode led the civil and military officials in congratulation, all in plain dress seated before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Duke Zhu Chunchen and Wei Zaode led the officials in congratulation, seated in mourning dress before the hall.

sentences.zh: 自成不出，群賊爭戲侮，為椎背、脫帽，或舉足加頸，相笑樂，百官懾伏不敢動。

translations.literal: Zicheng did not appear; the rebel host mocked them, pounding backs, snatching hats, some putting feet on their necks, laughing together, while the officials cowered and dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng stayed away while rebels jeered, beat them, pulled off hats, and trod on their necks; the officials lay still in terror.

sentences.zh: 太監王德化叱諸臣曰：「國亡君喪，若曹不思殯先帝，乃在此耶！」

translations.literal: Eunuch Wang Dehua rebuked the ministers: "The state is lost and the sovereign dead—will you not think of burying the late emperor, but sit here instead?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dehua cried out: "The dynasty is fallen—will you not bury your emperor, but sit here?"

sentences.zh: 因哭，內侍數十人皆哭，藻德等亦哭。

translations.literal: He wept; dozens of inner attendants wept, and Zaode and the others wept as well.
translations.idiomatic: He wept; inner eunuchs wept; Zaode and the court wept with them.

sentences.zh: 顧君恩以告自成，改殮帝后，用兗冕禕翟，加葦廠雲。

translations.literal: Gu Jun'en reported this to Zicheng; the emperor and empress were re-entombed in full regalia with a reed shed over the mound.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Jun'en told Li Zicheng; the bodies were reburied in imperial robes beneath a reed shelter.

sentences.zh: 大學士陳演勸進，不許。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Chen Yan urged him to take the throne; he would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan pressed him to ascend; he refused.

sentences.zh: 封太子為宋王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed the crown prince as Prince of Song.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was named Prince of Song.

sentences.zh: 放刑部、錦衣衛系囚。

translations.literal: He released prisoners held by the Ministry of Justice and the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners in the Ministry of Justice and the secret police were freed.

sentences.zh: 自成自居西安，建置官吏，至是益盡改官制。

translations.literal: Zicheng had governed from Xi'an with his own officials; now he overhauled the entire bureaucracy.
translations.idiomatic: Having ruled from Xi'an, he now remade every office in the capital.

sentences.zh: 六部曰六政府，司官曰從事，六科曰諫議，十三道曰直指使，翰林院曰弘文館，太僕寺曰驗馬寺，巡撫曰節度使，兵備曰防禦使，知府州縣曰尹、曰牧、曰令。

translations.literal: The Six Ministries became Six Governments; their chiefs were called Associates; the Six Offices became Remonstrance; the Thirteen Circuits became Direct-Pointing Commissioners; the Hanlin Academy became the Hongwen Hall; the Court of the Imperial Stud became the Horse-Inspection Temple; grand coordinators became Military Governors; circuit intendants became Defense Commissioners; prefects, magistrates, and county heads became Administrators, Pastors, and Magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Ministries became governments, censors remonstrance officers, circuits direct-pointing commissioners, the Hanlin the Hongwen Hall, the stud the horse-inspection bureau, and local titles were all renamed.

sentences.zh: 召見朝官，自成南響坐，金星、宗敏、企郊等左右雜坐，以次呼名，分三等授職。

translations.literal: Summoning court officials, Zicheng sat facing south; Jinxing, Zongmin, Qijiao, and others sat mixed to left and right; they were called by name and assigned posts in three grades.
translations.idiomatic: He received officials facing south, with Jinxing and Zongmin seated beside him, and assigned ranks in three tiers.

sentences.zh: 自四品以下少詹事梁紹陽、楊觀光等無不汙偽命，三品以上獨用故侍郎侯恂。

translations.literal: From fourth rank down, Junior Mentors Liang Shaoyang and Yang Guanguang and others all received false appointments; of third rank and above only the former Vice Minister Hou Xun was used.
translations.idiomatic: Every man from fourth rank down took a rebel post; only Hou Xun of third rank and above was retained from the old court.

sentences.zh: 其餘勳戚、文武諸臣奎、純臣、演、藻德等共八百餘人，送宗敏等營中，拷掠責賕賂，至灼肉折脛，備諸慘毒。

translations.literal: The rest—nobles and civil and military officials such as Kui, Chunchen, Yan, and Zaode, more than eight hundred in all—were sent to Zongmin's camp, tortured for bribes, flesh seared and shins broken, with every cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: More than eight hundred nobles and officials were handed to Zongmin for torture and extortion until flesh burned and bones snapped.

sentences.zh: 藻德遇馬世奇家人，泣曰：「吾不能為若主，今求死不得。」

translations.literal: Zaode met Ma Shiji's family and wept: "I could not be your master; now I cannot even die."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zaode wept to Ma Shiji's kin: "I failed you as patron—and now I cannot even die."

sentences.zh: 賊又編排甲，令五家養一賊，大縱淫掠，民不勝毒，縊死相望。

translations.literal: The rebels also organized households: every five families fed one rebel; rape and plunder ran wild; the people could not endure it, and suicides lined the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Five households were made to support one rebel; rape and looting were unchecked; corpses of the hanged filled the streets.

sentences.zh: 征諸勳戚大臣金，金足輒殺之。

translations.literal: Gold was levied from enfeoffed kin and great ministers; when the quota was met they were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles and ministers were squeezed for gold—and killed once they paid.

sentences.zh: 焚太廟神主，遷太祖主于帝王廟。

translations.literal: They burned the spirit tablets in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and moved Taizu's tablet to the Temple of Former Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral tablets were burned; Taizu's tablet was moved to the temple of former emperors.

sentences.zh: 時賊黨已陷保定，李建泰降，畿內府縣悉附。

translations.literal: By then rebel bands had taken Baoding; Li Jiantai surrendered, and prefectures and counties of the capital region all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Baoding had fallen; Li Jiantai surrendered; the capital districts submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 山東、河南遍設官吏，所至無違者。

translations.literal: In Shandong and Henan officials were installed everywhere; none resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong and Henan received rebel magistrates without a fight.

sentences.zh: 及淮，巡撫路振飛發兵拒之，乃去。

translations.literal: At the Huai River, Grand Coordinator Lu Zhenfei raised troops to block them, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhenfei barred the Huai with an army; the rebels turned back.

sentences.zh: 自成謂真得天命，金星率賊眾三表勸進，乃從之，令撰登極儀，諏吉日。

translations.literal: Zicheng believed he had truly received Heaven's mandate; Jinxing led the host in three memorials urging him to ascend, and he consented, ordering rites for enthronement and an auspicious day chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Heaven had chosen him, Li Zicheng let Jinxing press three times for enthronement, set the rites, and chose a lucky day.

sentences.zh: 及自成升御座，忽見白衣人長數丈，手劍怒視，座下龍爪鬣俱動，自成恐，亟下。

translations.literal: When he mounted the throne he suddenly saw a man in white several zhang tall, sword in hand, glaring in fury; the dragon claws on the seat stirred, and in terror he leapt down.
translations.idiomatic: As he took the throne a white figure many zhang high glared with a sword; the dragon claws on the seat seemed to move, and he fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 鑄金璽及永昌錢，皆不就。

translations.literal: Casting the golden seal and Yongchang coinage, neither would come right.
translations.idiomatic: The golden seal and Yongchang coins would not cast true.

sentences.zh: 聞山海關總兵吳三桂兵起，乃謀歸陝西。

translations.literal: Hearing that Wu Sangui, regional commander at Shanhai Pass, had raised troops, he planned to return to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that Wu Sangui had risen at Shanhai Pass; he prepared to retreat to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 初，三桂奉詔入援，至山海關，京師陷，猶豫不進。

translations.literal: At first Sangui, obeying the edict to relieve the capital, reached Shanhai Pass; when the capital fell he hesitated and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui had marched to relieve Beijing, halted at Shanhai Pass when the city fell, and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 自成劫其父襄，作書招之，三桂欲降。

translations.literal: Zicheng seized his father Xiang and sent a letter summoning him; Sangui was ready to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng captured Wu Xiang and summoned the son; Sangui was ready to submit.

sentences.zh: 至灤州，聞愛姬陳沅被劉宗敏掠去，憤甚，疾歸山海，襲破賊將。

translations.literal: At Luanzhou he learned his beloved Chen Yuan had been seized by Liu Zongmin; enraged, he raced back to Shanhai, surprised and broke the rebel general.
translations.idiomatic: At Luanzhou he learned Liu Zongmin had taken his concubine Chen Yuan; he wheeled back, smashed the rebel detachment, and broke for Shanhai.

sentences.zh: 自成怒，親部賊十余萬，執吳襄於軍，東攻山海關，以別將從一片石越關外。

translations.literal: Zicheng in fury personally led more than a hundred thousand rebels, holding Wu Xiang in the army, and attacked Shanhai Pass eastward, while another force crossed outside the pass through Yipianshi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng marched east with a hundred thousand men, Wu Xiang a hostage in camp, while a second column slipped past through Yipianshi.

sentences.zh: 三桂懼，乞降於我大清。

translations.literal: Sangui in fear begged surrender from our Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Wu Sangui turned to the Great Qing for aid.

sentences.zh: 四月二十二日，自成兵二十萬，陣於關內，自北山亙海。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of the fourth month, Zicheng drew up two hundred thousand men inside the pass, his line running from the northern hills to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second of the fourth month two hundred thousand rebels lined the pass from mountain to sea.

sentences.zh: 我兵對賊置陣，三桂居右翼末，悉銳卒搏戰，殺賊數千人，賊亦力鬥，圍開復合。

translations.literal: Our army faced the rebels in battle array; Sangui held the right wing's end with picked troops in fierce combat, killing several thousand rebels; the rebels fought hard, the encirclement opening and closing again.
translations.idiomatic: Qing forces formed battle lines; Sangui on the right wing cut down thousands; the rebel ring broke and closed again.

sentences.zh: 戰良久，我兵從三桂陣右突出，沖賊中堅，萬馬奔躍，飛矢雨墮，天大風，沙石飛走，擊賊如雹。

translations.literal: After long fighting our troops burst from the right of Sangui's formation, pierced the rebel center, ten thousand horses charging, arrows falling like rain; a great wind rose, sand and stone flew, and the rebels were struck as by hail.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qing cavalry burst from Sangui's right, shattered the rebel center under a storm of arrows and flying sand.

sentences.zh: 自成方挾太子登高岡觀戰，知為我兵，急策馬下岡走。

translations.literal: Zicheng, holding the crown prince on a high hill to watch the battle, knew it was our army and whipped his horse down the hill in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Watching from a hill with the crown prince as hostage, Li Zicheng saw the Qing banners and fled.

sentences.zh: 我兵追奔四十里，賊眾大潰，自相踐踏死者無算，僵屍遍野，溝水盡赤。

translations.literal: Our army pursued forty li; the rebel host collapsed in rout, trampling one another to death beyond count; corpses covered the fields and ditches ran red.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran forty li; rebels trampled one another dead; the fields were carpeted with bodies and the ditches ran red.

sentences.zh: 自成奔永平，我兵逐之。

translations.literal: Zicheng fled to Yongping; our army followed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng fled to Yongping with the Qing army at his heels.
