sentences.zh: 三桂先驅至永平，自成殺吳襄，奔還京師。

translations.literal: Sangui's vanguard reached Yongping; Zicheng killed Wu Xiang and fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui's van reached Yongping; Li Zicheng killed Wu Xiang and raced for Beijing.

sentences.zh: 時牛金星居守，諸降人往謁，執門生禮甚恭。

translations.literal: Niu Jinxing then held the capital; surrendered officials who came to call were received with the courtesy due a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Jinxing held Beijing; defecting officials were greeted with elaborate courtesy.

sentences.zh: 金星曰：「訛言方起，諸君宜簡出。」

translations.literal: Jinxing said: "Rumors are spreading; you gentlemen should keep a low profile."
translations.idiomatic: Jinxing warned: "Rumors fly—you should lie low."

sentences.zh: 由是降者始懼，多竄伏矣。

translations.literal: From this the surrendered began to fear and many went into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: The defectors grew afraid and vanished into hiding.

sentences.zh: 自成至，悉鎔所拷索金及宮中帑藏、器皿，鑄為餅，每餅千金，約數萬餅，騾車載歸西安。

translations.literal: When Zicheng arrived he melted all extorted gold and palace treasuries and vessels into ingots, each worth a thousand gold, numbering tens of thousands, loaded on mule carts for Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He melted extorted gold and palace treasure into thousand-tael cakes—tens of thousands of them—and sent them west on mule trains.

sentences.zh: 二十九日丙戌僭帝號于武英殿，追尊七代皆為帝后，立妻高氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth, bingxu, he usurped the imperial title in the Hall of Military Glory, posthumously ennobling seven generations as emperors and empresses, and installed his wife Gao as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth he declared himself emperor in the Hall of Military Glory, ennobled seven generations, and crowned Gao empress.

sentences.zh: 自成被冠冕，列仗受朝。

translations.literal: Zicheng donned the crown and robes and received obeisance amid ranked guards.
translations.idiomatic: He wore the imperial regalia and took homage under guard.

sentences.zh: 金星代行郊天禮。

translations.literal: Jinxing performed the suburban rites in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Jinxing conducted the heaven-worship rites for him.

sentences.zh: 是夕焚宮殿及九門城樓。

translations.literal: That night palaces and the nine gate towers were burned.
translations.idiomatic: That night palaces and gate towers burned.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，挾太子、二王西走，而使偽將軍左光先、谷可成殿。

translations.literal: At dawn he took the crown prince and the two princes west, leaving the false generals Zuo Guangxian and Gu Kecheng as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he fled west with the princes, leaving Zuo Guangxian and Gu Kecheng to cover the retreat.

sentences.zh: 五月二日，我大清兵入京師，下令安輯百姓，為帝后發喪，議諡號，遣將偕三桂追自成。

translations.literal: On the second day of the fifth month our Great Qing army entered the capital, ordered the people pacified, arranged funeral rites for the emperor and empress, debated posthumous titles, and sent generals with Sangui to pursue Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the second of the fifth month the Qing entered Beijing, pacified the people, buried the Ming sovereigns, and sent armies with Sangui after Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 時福王已監國南京，大學士史可法督師討賊。

translations.literal: By then the Prince of Fu had assumed regency at Nanjing; Grand Secretary Shi Kefa directed armies against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fu ruled at Nanjing; Shi Kefa marched against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 自成至定州，我兵追之，與戰，斬谷可成，左光先傷足，賊負而逃。

translations.literal: At Dingzhou our army overtook Zicheng and fought; Gu Kecheng was beheaded and Zuo Guangxian wounded in the foot; the rebels fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At Dingzhou Qing forces caught Li Zicheng, killed Gu Kecheng, wounded Zuo Guangxian, and drove the rebels west.

sentences.zh: 自成西走真定，益發眾來攻，我兵復擊之。

translations.literal: Zicheng fled west to Zhending and sent more troops to attack; our army struck again.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Zhending, gathered fresh troops, and was beaten again.

sentences.zh: 自成中流矢創甚，西逾故關，入山西。

translations.literal: Zicheng took an arrow wound and crossed the old pass west into Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded by an arrow, he crossed into Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 會我兵東返，自成乃鳩合潰散，走平陽。

translations.literal: When our army turned east, Zicheng gathered the scattered and fled to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army withdrew east; Li Zicheng rallied remnants and fled to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 李岩者，故勸自成以不殺收人心者也。

translations.literal: Li Yan was the man who had urged Zicheng to win hearts by sparing lives.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan was the adviser who had told Li Zicheng to win the people by restraint in killing.

sentences.zh: 及陷京師，保護懿安皇后令自盡。

translations.literal: When the capital fell he protected Empress Dowager Yi'an and saw that she took her own life.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of Beijing he shielded Empress Dowager Yi'an until she could die with dignity.

sentences.zh: 又獨于士大夫無所拷掠，金星等大忌之。

translations.literal: He alone did not extort the scholar-officials; Jinxing and the others greatly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: He alone spared the gentry from torture; Jinxing and his faction hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 定州之敗，河南州縣多反正，自成召諸將議，岩請率兵往。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Dingzhou many Henan prefectures and counties turned loyal again; Zicheng summoned his generals to council, and Yan asked to lead troops there.
translations.idiomatic: After Dingzhou, Henan cities rebelled against the rebels; Li Zicheng called a council, and Li Yan volunteered to recover the province.

sentences.zh: 金星陰告自成曰：「岩雄武有大略，非能久下人者。

translations.literal: Jinxing secretly told Zicheng: "Yan is bold and masterful, with great stratagems—not a man who can long serve under another.
translations.idiomatic: Jinxing whispered to Li Zicheng: "Li Yan is too bold and brilliant to remain a subordinate.

sentences.zh: 河南，岩故鄉，假以大兵，必不可制。

translations.literal: Henan is his homeland; if you lend him a great army, he cannot be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Henan is his home ground—give him an army and you will never control him.

sentences.zh: 十八子之讖，得非岩乎？」

translations.literal: The prophecy of the Eighteen Sons—could it not mean Yan?"
translations.idiomatic: The prophecy of the Eighteen Sons—is it not fulfilled in Li Yan?"

sentences.zh: 因譖其欲反。

translations.literal: He slandered him as plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He accused Li Yan of treason.

sentences.zh: 自成令金星與岩飲，殺之，賊眾俱解體。

translations.literal: Zicheng had Jinxing drink with Yan and killed him; the rebel host lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng had Jinxing toast Li Yan, then had him killed; the army lost its nerve.

sentences.zh: 自成歸西安，復遣賊陷漢中，降總兵趙光遠，進略保寧。

translations.literal: Zicheng returned to Xi'an and again sent rebels to take Hanzhong, subdue Regional Commander Zhao Guangyuan, and advance on Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Xi'an he sent columns to seize Hanzhong, win Zhao Guangyuan, and threaten Baoning.

sentences.zh: 時獻忠以兵拒之，乃還。

translations.literal: Xianzhong then barred his way with troops, and he turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong blocked him with an army, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 八月建祖禰廟成，將往祀，忽寒栗不能就禮。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, when the ancestral temple was completed and he was to sacrifice, he suddenly shivered with cold and could not perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, at the dedication of the ancestral temple, he shook with cold and could not complete the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 自成始以岩言，謬為仁義，及岩死，又屢敗，復強很自用，偽尚書張第元、耿始然皆以小忤死。

translations.literal: At first, on Yan's advice, he had pretended to benevolence; after Yan's death and repeated defeats he grew obstinate and arbitrary, and the false ministers Zhang Diyuan and Geng Shiran were both killed for small offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had played at mercy on Li Yan's advice; after Li Yan's death and repeated defeats he turned cruel and capricious, killing Zhang Diyuan and Geng Shiran for trifles.

sentences.zh: 制銅鏌，官吏坐賕，即鏌斬。

translations.literal: He fashioned a bronze execution blade; officials who took bribes were beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He had a bronze headsman's blade forged; any official caught in graft was cut down immediately.

sentences.zh: 民盜一雞者死。

translations.literal: A commoner who stole a chicken was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Stealing a chicken meant death.

sentences.zh: 西人大懼。

translations.literal: The people of the west were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Western Shaanxi lived in terror.

sentences.zh: 順治二年二月，我兵攻潼關，偽伯馬世耀以六十萬眾迎戰，敗死。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Shunzhi our army attacked Tong Pass; the false Earl Ma Shiyao met the fight with six hundred thousand men and was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Shunzhi 2 Qing forces stormed Tong Pass; Ma Shiyao met them with six hundred thousand men and died.

sentences.zh: 潼關破，自成遂棄西安，由龍駒寨走武岡，入襄陽，復走武昌。

translations.literal: Tong Pass fell; Zicheng abandoned Xi'an, fled through Longju Stockade to Wugang, entered Xiangyang, then fled again to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Pass lost, he abandoned Xi'an, fled through Longju to Wugang and Xiangyang, then on to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 我兵兩道追躡，連蹙之鄧州、承天、德安、武昌，窮追至賊老營，大破之者八。

translations.literal: Our army pursued on two roads, pressing him through Dengzhou, Chengtian, De'an, and Wuchang, and eight times smashed his old camps in desperate pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Two Qing columns harried him through Hubei, crushing his veteran camps eight times.

sentences.zh: 當是時，左良玉東下，武昌虛無人。

translations.literal: At that time Zuo Liangyu marched east and Wuchang stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu had marched east, leaving Wuchang undefended.

sentences.zh: 自成屯五十餘日，賊眾尚五十余萬，改江夏曰瑞符縣。

translations.literal: Zicheng camped more than fifty days; his host still numbered over five hundred thousand; he renamed Jiangxia Ruifu County.
translations.idiomatic: He lingered fifty days with half a million men and renamed Jiangxia Ruifu County.

sentences.zh: 尋為我兵所迫，部眾多降，或逃散。

translations.literal: Soon pressed by our army, many of his followers surrendered or scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by the Qing, his army melted away in surrenders and desertions.

sentences.zh: 自成走咸甯、蒲圻，至通城，竄於九宮山。

translations.literal: Zicheng fled to Xianning and Puqi, reached Tongcheng, and hid on Jiugong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He fled through Xianning and Puqi to Tongcheng and hid on Jiugong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，自成留李過守寨，自率二十騎略食山中，為村民所困、不能脫，遂縊死。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Zicheng left Li Guo to hold the camp and himself led twenty horsemen to forage in the hills; villagers trapped him and he could not escape, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he left Li Guo in camp and rode out with twenty men to forage; peasants cornered him, and he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 或曰村民方築堡，見賊少，爭前擊之，人馬俱陷泥淖中，自成腦中鉏死。

translations.literal: Some say villagers were building a stockade, saw few rebels, rushed to attack, and both man and horse sank in the mire; Zicheng was killed by a hoe blow to the head.
translations.idiomatic: Others say villagers building a fort overwhelmed his tiny party in the mud and brained him with a hoe.

sentences.zh: 剝其衣，得龍衣金印，眇一目，村民乃大驚，謂為自成也。

translations.literal: Stripping his clothes they found dragon robes and a golden seal; one eye was blind; the villagers were greatly alarmed, believing it was Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Stripping the corpse they found imperial robes, a golden seal, and one blind eye—the peasants knew it was Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 時我兵遣識自成者驗其屍，朽莫辨。

translations.literal: Our army sent men who had known Zicheng to identify the corpse, but it had rotted beyond recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Qing agents who had known him could not identify the rotted body.

sentences.zh: 獲自成兩從父偽趙侯、偽襄南侯及自成妻妾二人，金印一。

translations.literal: They captured Zicheng's two cousins, the false Marquis of Zhao and false Marquis of Xiangnan, and two of his wives, with one golden seal.
translations.idiomatic: They seized two of his cousins, two wives, and a golden seal.

sentences.zh: 又獲偽汝侯劉宗敏、偽總兵左光先、偽軍師宋獻策。

translations.literal: They also captured the false Marquis of Ru Liu Zongmin, the false Regional Commander Zuo Guangxian, and the false strategist Song Xiance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongmin, Zuo Guangxian, and Song Xiance were taken alive.

sentences.zh: 於是斬自成從父及宗敏於軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zicheng's cousins and Zongmin were beheaded in camp.
translations.idiomatic: His cousins and Liu Zongmin were executed in camp.

sentences.zh: 牛金星、宋企郊等皆遁亡。

translations.literal: Niu Jinxing, Song Qijiao, and the others all fled and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Jinxing, Song Qijiao, and the rest escaped.

sentences.zh: 自成兄子過改名錦，偕諸賊帥奉高氏降于總督何騰蛟。

translations.literal: Zicheng's nephew Guo changed his name to Jin and, with other rebel chiefs, presented Gao in surrender to Grand Coordinator He Tengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Li Guo took the name Jin and, with other chiefs, surrendered Gao to He Tengjiao.

sentences.zh: 時唐王立於閩，賜錦名赤心，封高氏忠義夫人，號其軍曰忠貞營，隸騰蛟麾下。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Tang ruled in Fujian, Jin was granted the name Chixin, Gao was enfeoffed as Lady of Loyal Righteousness, and their army was called the Loyal-Faithful Battalion under Tengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tang named him Chixin, ennobled Gao as Lady of Loyal Righteousness, and enrolled the Loyal-Faithful Battalion under Tengjiao.

sentences.zh: 永明王時，赤心封興國侯，尋死。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Yongming, Chixin was enfeoffed Marquis of Xingguo and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Yongming he became Marquis of Xingguo and soon died.

sentences.zh: 張獻忠

translations.literal: Zhang Xianzhong
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong

sentences.zh: 張獻忠者，延安衛柳樹澗人也，與李自成同歲生。

translations.literal: Zhang Xianzhong was a man of Liushujian in Yan'an Guard, born in the same year as Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong came from Liushujian in Yan'an Guard and was Li Zicheng's age.

sentences.zh: 長隸延綏鎮為軍，犯法當斬，主將陳洪范奇其狀貌，為請于總兵官王威釋之，乃逃去。

translations.literal: Growing up he served as a soldier under Yan'an Command; having broken the law and been condemned to death, Commander Chen Hongfan was struck by his appearance and begged Regional Commander Wang Wei to release him, whereupon he fled.
translations.idiomatic: As a soldier under Yan'an he faced execution; Chen Hongfan, struck by his looks, persuaded Wang Wei to spare him, and he fled.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，陝西賊大起，王嘉胤據府穀，陷河曲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen banditry rose across Shaanxi; Wang Jiayin seized Fugu and took Hequ.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 3 rebellion swept Shaanxi; Wang Jiayin seized Fugu and Hequ.

sentences.zh: 獻忠以米脂十八寨應之，自稱八大王。

translations.literal: Xianzhong answered from the Eighteen Stockades of Mizhi and styled himself the Eight Great King.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong rose from Mizhi's Eighteen Stockades as the Eight Great King.

sentences.zh: 明年，嘉胤死，其党王自用復聚眾三十六營，獻忠及高迎祥、羅汝才、馬守應等皆為之渠。

translations.literal: The next year Jiayin died; his follower Wang Ziyong again gathered thirty-six camps; Xianzhong, Gao Yingxiang, Luo Ruocai, Ma Shouying, and others all became chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayin died the next year; Wang Ziyong rallied thirty-six camps, and Xianzhong, Gao Yingxiang, Luo Ruocai, and Ma Shouying became chiefs.

sentences.zh: 其冬，洪承疇為總督，獻忠及汝才皆就撫。

translations.literal: That winter Hong Chengchou became grand coordinator; Xianzhong and Ruocai both submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Hong Chengchou took command; Xianzhong and Ruocai briefly submitted.

sentences.zh: 已而叛入山西，偕群賊焚掠。

translations.literal: Soon they rebelled again, entered Shanxi, and with the rebel host burned and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: They soon rebelled again, crossed into Shanxi, and burned with the host.

sentences.zh: 尋擾河北，又偕渡河。

translations.literal: They then harried Hebei and again crossed the river with the host.
translations.idiomatic: They ravaged Hebei and crossed the Yellow River again.

sentences.zh: 自是，陝西、河南、湖廣、四川，江北數千里地，皆被蹂躪。

translations.literal: From this time Shaanxi, Henan, Huguang, Sichuan, and the country north of the Yangtze for several thousand li were trampled.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi, Henan, Huguang, Sichuan, and the land north of the Yangtze for thousands of li were laid waste.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，賊渠率眾無專主，遇官軍，人自為鬥，勝則爭進，敗則竄山谷不相顧。

translations.literal: At this time rebel chiefs led their followers without a single supreme leader; meeting government troops each fought on his own; if victorious they vied to advance, if defeated they fled into the hills and did not look after one another.
translations.idiomatic: No single chief commanded the host; each band fought alone, advancing in victory and scattering in defeat without mutual aid.

sentences.zh: 官軍遇賊追殺，亦不知所逐何賊也。

translations.literal: When government troops pursued and killed bandits, they did not know which band they were chasing.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial pursuers rarely knew which rebel band they were fighting.

sentences.zh: 賊或分或合，東西奔突，勢日強盛。

translations.literal: The bandits split and merged, rushing east and west, their power growing daily.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels split and reunited, surging east and west, growing stronger by the day.

sentences.zh: 八年，十三家會滎陽，議敵官軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Thirteen Families met at Xingyang to plan against government troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Thirteen Families met at Xingyang to plot against the Ming.

sentences.zh: 守應欲北渡，獻忠嗤之，守應怒，李自成為解，乃定議。

translations.literal: Shouying wished to cross north; Xianzhong mocked him; Shouying grew angry, and Li Zicheng mediated, and the plan was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shouying wanted to cross north; Xianzhong ridiculed him; Zicheng patched the quarrel and they agreed.

sentences.zh: 獻忠始與高迎祥並起作賊，自成乃迎祥偏裨，不敢與獻忠並。

translations.literal: At first Xianzhong and Gao Yingxiang had risen together as bandits; Zicheng was only Yingxiang's lieutenant and did not dare rank himself with Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong and Gao Yingxiang had been equals; Li Zicheng was only Yingxiang's lieutenant and dared not rival Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 及是遂相頡頏，與俱東掠，連破河南、江北諸縣，焚皇陵。

translations.literal: Now they matched one another and together raided east, taking in succession counties of Henan and north of the Yangtze, and burned the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Now he stood as Zicheng's equal; together they ravaged Henan and the north, and burned the imperial mausoleums.

sentences.zh: 已而迎祥、自成西去。

translations.literal: Soon Yingxiang and Zicheng went west.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiang and Zicheng then turned west.

sentences.zh: 獻忠獨東，圍廬州、舒城，俱不下。

translations.literal: Xianzhong alone went east, besieged Luzhou and Shucheng, and could not take either.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong marched east alone, failed before Luzhou and Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 攻桐城，陷廬江，屠巢、無為、潛山、太湖、宿松諸城，應天巡撫張國維禦之。

translations.literal: He attacked Tongcheng, took Lujiang, and massacred the cities of Chao, Wuwei, Qianshan, Taihu, and Susong; Grand Coordinator of Nanjing Zhang Guowei opposed him.
translations.idiomatic: He took Lujiang, slaughtered Chao, Wuwei, Qianshan, Taihu, and Susong, and met Zhang Guowei of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 獻忠從英、霍遁，道麻城，合守應等入關，會迎祥於鳳翔。

translations.literal: Xianzhong fled from Ying and Huo by way of Macheng, joined Shouying and others in entering the pass, and met Yingxiang at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped from Ying and Huo through Macheng, entered the pass with Shouying, and joined Yingxiang at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 已，復出商、洛，屯靈寶，以待迎祥。

translations.literal: Soon he came out again through Shang and Luo, encamped at Lingbao, and waited for Yingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He emerged again through Shang and Luo, camped at Lingbao, and waited for Yingxiang.

sentences.zh: 迎祥至，則合兵復東。

translations.literal: When Yingxiang arrived they united their armies and again went east.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiang came; they united and marched east again.

sentences.zh: 總兵官左良玉、祖寬擊之，獻忠與迎祥分道走。

translations.literal: Regional Commanders Zuo Liangyu and Zu Kuan attacked them; Xianzhong and Yingxiang split and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu and Zu Kuan attacked; Xianzhong and Yingxiang split and fled.

sentences.zh: 寬追獻忠，戰於嵩縣及九皋山，三戰皆克，俘斬甚眾。

translations.literal: Kuan pursued Xianzhong and fought at Song County and Jiugao Mountain; three battles were won, with many captured and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Kuan pursued Xianzhong, fought at Song and Jiugao Mountain, and won three victories with heavy slaughter.

sentences.zh: 獻忠恚，再合迎祥眾還戰，復大敗。

translations.literal: Xianzhong in rage united with Yingxiang's host and fought again, and suffered another great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Xianzhong reunited with Yingxiang and was crushed again.

sentences.zh: 迎祥尋與自成入陝西，而守應、汝才諸賊，各盤踞鄖陽、商、洛山中，不能救，獻忠亦遁山中。

translations.literal: Yingxiang soon entered Shaanxi with Zicheng, while Shouying, Ruocai, and other bandits each held the mountains of Yunyang, Shang, and Luo and could not rescue him; Xianzhong also fled into the hills.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiang and Zicheng entered Shaanxi; other chiefs held the Yunyang mountains and could not help; Xianzhong fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，總督盧象升去，苗胙土巡撫湖廣，不習兵。

translations.literal: The next autumn Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng departed; Miao Zhengtu became grand coordinator of Huguang and did not know warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Next autumn Lu Xiangsheng left; Miao Zhengtu, new governor of Huguang, knew nothing of war.

sentences.zh: 於是獻忠自均州，守應自新野，蠍子塊自唐縣，並犯襄陽，眾二余萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xianzhong came from Junzhou, Shouying from Xinye, and Xiezi Kuai from Tang County, and together attacked Xiangyang with more than twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong came from Junzhou, Shouying from Xinye, Xiezi Kuai from Tang—they stormed Xiangyang with over twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 總兵秦翼明兵寡不能禦，湖廣震動。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Qin Yiming had too few troops to resist; Huguang was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yiming could not hold them; Huguang trembled.

sentences.zh: 獻忠糾汝才、守應及闖塌天諸賊，順流東下，與江北賊賀一龍、賀錦等合，烽火達淮、揚。

translations.literal: Xianzhong rallied Ruocai, Shouying, and Chuangtian and other bandits, went downstream east, and joined north-of-the-Yangtze rebels He Yilong and He Jin; beacon fires reached Huai and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Ruocai, Shouying, and Chuangtian, swept downriver, united with He Yilong and He Jin, and alarm fires reached the Huai.

sentences.zh: 南京兵部尚書范景文、操江都御史黃道直、總兵官楊禦蕃分汛固守，安池道副使史可法親率兵當賊沖。

translations.literal: Minister of War at Nanjing Fan Jingwen, River-Patrol Censor-in-Chief Huang Daozhi, and Regional Commander Yang Yufan divided forces to hold fast; Anqing Circuit Vice Commissioner Shi Kefa personally led troops against the rebel van.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jingwen, Huang Daozhi, and Yang Yufan held Nanjing's approaches while Shi Kefa met the rebel spearhead at Anqing.

sentences.zh: 賊從間道犯安慶，連營百里，巡撫國維告警。

translations.literal: The bandits by a bypath attacked Anqing; their camps stretched a hundred li; Grand Coordinator Guowei sounded the alarm.
translations.idiomatic: They struck Anqing by a side road in camps a hundred li long; Guowei called for aid.

sentences.zh: 詔左良玉、馬爌、劉良佐合兵援之，遂大破賊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zuo Liangyu, Ma Guang, and Liu Liangzuo to unite and relieve the city, and they inflicted a great defeat on the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu, Ma Guang, and Liu Liangzuo were ordered to relieve Anqing and shattered the rebel army.

sentences.zh: 賊走潛山之天王古寨，國維檄良玉搜山，良玉不應，尋北去。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to the King-of-Heaven Ancient Stockade in Qianshan; Guowei ordered Liangzuo to search the mountains, but Liangzuo did not respond and soon marched north.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels fled to Qianshan's King-of-Heaven stockade; Guowei ordered Liu Liangzuo to hunt them, but he marched north instead.

sentences.zh: 賊乃復出太湖，連蘄、黃，敗官軍於酆家店，殺參將程龍、陳于王等四十餘人。

translations.literal: The bandits again came out of Taihu, took in succession Qi and Huang, and defeated government troops at Fengjia Store, killing Assistant Regional Commanders Cheng Long, Chen Yuwang, and more than forty others.
translations.idiomatic: They burst from Taihu, overran Qi and Huang, and at Fengjia Store killed Cheng Long, Chen Yuwang, and forty officers.

sentences.zh: 會總兵官牟文綬偕良佐來援，復破賊。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Mou Wensui came with Liangzuo to relieve them and again defeated the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Wensui and Liu Liangzuo arrived and beat them again.

sentences.zh: 賊皆遁，獻忠入湖廣。

translations.literal: The bandits all fled; Xianzhong entered Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels scattered; Xianzhong withdrew into Huguang.

sentences.zh: 是時，河南、湖廣賊十五家，惟獻忠最狡黠驍勍，次則汝才。

translations.literal: At this time among the fifteen bandit hosts of Henan and Huguang, Xianzhong was the most cunning and fierce, Ruocai second.
translations.idiomatic: Of fifteen rebel hosts in Henan and Huguang, Xianzhong was fiercest and most cunning, Ruocai next.

sentences.zh: 獻忠嘗偽為官兵，欲給宛城，良玉適至，獻忠倉皇走，前鋒羅岱射之中額，良玉馬追及，刃拂獻忠面，馬馳以免。

translations.literal: Xianzhong once disguised himself as government troops to deceive Wancheng; Liangyu happened to arrive and Xianzhong fled in panic; his vanguard Luo Dai shot him in the forehead; Liangyu on horseback overtook him and a blade swept Xianzhong's face as his horse galloped free.
translations.idiomatic: He once dressed as Ming troops to take Wancheng; Zuo Liangyu arrived; Luo Dai put an arrow in his forehead; Liangyu's blade scarred his face as he escaped.

sentences.zh: 會熊文燦為總理，刊檄撫賊。

translations.literal: Then Xiong Wencan became supreme commander and issued proclamations to pacify the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Wencan became supreme pacifier and issued surrender proclamations.

sentences.zh: 闖塌天者，本名劉國能，與獻忠有郤，詣文燦降。

translations.literal: Chuangtian, whose original name was Liu Guoneng, had a feud with Xianzhong and came to Wencan to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chuangtian—Liu Guoneng—hated Xianzhong and surrendered to Wencan.

sentences.zh: 獻忠創甚，不能戰，大恐。

translations.literal: Xianzhong was badly wounded and could not fight, and was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Badly wounded, Xianzhong could not fight and was terrified.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，偵知陳洪范隸文燦麾下為總兵，大喜，因遣間齎重幣獻洪範曰：「獻忠蒙公大恩，得不死，公豈忘之邪？

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year, learning that Chen Hongfan served under Wencan as regional commander, he was overjoyed and sent an agent with heavy gifts to Hongfan, saying: "Xianzhong owes his life to your great grace—would you forget?
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year he learned Chen Hongfan served under Wencan and sent gifts with a message: "You spared my life—have you forgotten?

sentences.zh: 願率所部降以自效。」

translations.literal: I wish to lead my followers in surrender to repay the debt."
translations.idiomatic: I will lead my men to surrender and serve you."

sentences.zh: 洪範亦喜，為告文燦，受其降。

translations.literal: Hongfan was pleased and told Wencan, who accepted the surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan rejoiced, told Wencan, and surrender was accepted.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史林銘球、分巡道王瑞栴與良玉謀，俟獻忠至執之，文燦不可。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Lin Mingqiu and Circuit Intendant Wang Ruizhi with Liangyu plotted to seize Xianzhong when he arrived; Wencan would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Mingqiu and Wang Ruizhi plotted with Liangyu to arrest him on arrival; Wencan refused.

sentences.zh: 獻忠遂據穀城，請十萬人餉，文燦不敢決。

translations.literal: Xianzhong then occupied Gucheng and asked for rations for a hundred thousand men; Wencan dared not decide.
translations.idiomatic: He occupied Gucheng and demanded rations for a hundred thousand men; Wencan hesitated.

sentences.zh: 時群賊皆聚南陽，屠掠旁州縣。

translations.literal: At that time all the bandits gathered at Nanyang, slaughtering and plundering the neighboring prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: All rebel hosts gathered at Nanyang, ravaging the surrounding counties.

sentences.zh: 文燦赴裕州，益大發檄撫賊。

translations.literal: Wencan went to Yuzhou and issued proclamations on an even greater scale to pacify the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan went to Yuzhou and redoubled the surrender appeals.

sentences.zh: 汝才以戰敗乞降於太和山監軍太監李繼改。

translations.literal: Ruocai, having been defeated in battle, begged surrender from Supervising Eunuch Li Jigai at Taihe Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Ruocai, beaten in battle, surrendered to the eunuch Li Jigai at Taihe Mountain.

sentences.zh: 明年，射塌天、混十萬、過天星、關索、王光恩等十三家渠帥，先後俱降。

translations.literal: The next year the thirteen chieftains—Shetian, Hunshiwan, Guotianxing, Guansuo, Wang Guangen, and others—surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The next year thirteen chiefs—Shetian, Hunshiwan, Guotianxing, and the rest—surrendered in turn.

sentences.zh: 陝西總督洪承疇、巡撫孫傳庭復大破李自成，自成竄崤、函山中，朝廷皆謂賊撲剪殆盡。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou and Grand Coordinator Sun Chuanting again inflicted a great defeat on Li Zicheng; Zicheng fled into the Xiao and Han mountains, and the court believed the bandits were nearly exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou and Sun Chuanting crushed Li Zicheng in the Xiao-Han mountains; the court thought the rebellion nearly ended.

sentences.zh: 獻忠在穀城，訓卒治甲仗，言者頗疑其欲反。

translations.literal: Xianzhong was at Gucheng, drilling troops and repairing arms and armor; many spoke of his intent to rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: At Gucheng he drilled troops and forged arms; many suspected he would rebel again.

sentences.zh: 帝方信兵部尚書楊嗣昌言，謂文燦能辦賊，不復憂也。

translations.literal: The emperor then trusted Minister of War Yang Sichang, believing Wencan could handle the bandits, and no longer worried.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted Yang Sichang and believed Wencan had the rebels in hand.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，獻忠叛，殺知縣阮之鈿，隳穀城，陷房縣，合汝才兵，殺知縣郝景春。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer Xianzhong rebelled, killed Magistrate Ruan Zhitong, destroyed Gucheng, took Fang County, united with Ruocai's troops, and killed Magistrate Hao Jingchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he rebelled, killed Ruan Zhitong, destroyed Gucheng, took Fang County with Ruocai, and killed Hao Jingchun.

sentences.zh: 十三家降賊一時並叛，惟王光恩不從。

translations.literal: The thirteen surrendered hosts all rebelled at once; only Wang Guangen did not join.
translations.idiomatic: All thirteen surrendered bands rose again; only Wang Guangen held back.

sentences.zh: 獻忠去房縣，左良玉追擊之，羅岱為前鋒，至羅犬英山，岱中伏死，良玉大敗。

translations.literal: Xianzhong left Fang County; Zuo Liangyu pursued; Luo Dai led the van to Luoying Mountain in Luoxian; Dai fell into an ambush and died; Liangyu suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Fang County he was pursued by Zuo Liangyu; Luo Dai was ambushed and killed at Luoying Mountain; Liangyu was routed.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌已拜大學士，乃自請督師，帝大悅。

translations.literal: Sichang had already become grand secretary and now asked to take command in person; the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang, now grand secretary, volunteered to command; the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 十月朔，嗣昌至襄陽，集諸將議進兵。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month Sichang reached Xiangyang and assembled the generals to plan the advance.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the tenth month he reached Xiangyang and convened the generals.

sentences.zh: 時群賊大掠，賀一龍、賀錦犯隨、應、麻、黃，與官軍相持。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits plundered on a great scale; He Yilong and He Jin attacked Sui, Ying, Ma, and Huang and locked in stalemate with government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels ravaged everywhere; He Yilong and He Jin held Sui, Ying, Ma, and Huang against the Ming.

sentences.zh: 汝才及過天星竄伏漳、房、興、遠，獻忠踞湖廣、四川界，將西犯。

translations.literal: Ruocai and Guotianxing hid in Zhang, Fang, Xing, and Yuan; Xianzhong held the Huguang–Sichuan border and was about to invade west.
translations.idiomatic: Ruocai and Guotianxing lurked in the mountains; Xianzhong held the Huguang–Sichuan frontier and prepared to strike west.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌視東略稍緩，乃宿輜重襄陽，浚濠築城甚固，令良玉專力剿獻忠。

translations.literal: Sichang thought the eastern front could wait; he stored baggage at Xiangyang, dug moats and built walls very solidly, and ordered Liangyu to concentrate on exterminating Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang judged the east secondary, fortified Xiangyang, and ordered Liangyu to focus solely on Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 十三年閏正月，良玉擊賊枸坪關，獻忠遁，追至瑪瑙山。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month of the thirteenth year Liangyu attacked the bandits at Goupíng Pass; Xianzhong fled and was pursued to Manáo Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of the thirteenth year Liangyu drove him from Goupíng Pass to Manáo Mountain.

sentences.zh: 賊據山拒敵，良玉先登，賀人龍、李國奇夾擊，大敗之，斬首千三百餘級，擒獻忠妻妾。

translations.literal: The bandits held the mountain and resisted; Liangyu climbed first; He Renlong and Li Guoqi struck from both sides and inflicted a great defeat, beheading more than thirteen hundred; Xianzhong's wives were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held the heights; Liangyu led the climb; He Renlong and Li Guoqi flanked them; thirteen hundred heads fell and Xianzhong's wives were taken.

sentences.zh: 湖廣將張應元、汪之鳳追敗之水右壩。

translations.literal: Huguang generals Zhang Yingyuan and Wang Zhifeng pursued and defeated them at Shuiyouba.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yingyuan and Wang Zhifeng beat them again at Shuiyouba.

sentences.zh: 川將張令、方國安又邀擊於岔溪。

translations.literal: Sichuan generals Zhang Ling and Fang Guo'an intercepted them at Chaxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ling and Fang Guo'an ambushed them at Chaxi.

sentences.zh: 獻忠奔柯家坪，張令逐北深入，被圍，應元、之鳳援之，復破賊。

translations.literal: Xianzhong fled to Kejiaping; Zhang Ling pursued deep north and was surrounded; Yingyuan and Zhifeng relieved him and again defeated the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong fled to Kejiaping; Zhang Ling pursued too far and was surrounded until Yingyuan and Zhifeng rescued him and won again.

sentences.zh: 獻忠率千餘騎竄興、歸山中，勢大蹙。

translations.literal: Xianzhong led more than a thousand horsemen into the mountains of Xing and Gui; his power was greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: With a thousand horsemen he hid in the Xing-Gui mountains, his power broken.

sentences.zh: 初，良玉之進兵也，與嗣昌議不合。

translations.literal: At first, when Liangyu advanced, he and Sichang disagreed on strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu and Sichang had quarreled over strategy from the first.

sentences.zh: 獻忠遣間說良玉，良玉乃圍而弗攻。

translations.literal: Xianzhong sent agents to persuade Liangyu, and Liangyu encircled but did not attack.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong's agents bought Liangyu, who surrounded him but would not close in.

sentences.zh: 獻忠因得與山民市鹽芻米酷，收潰散，掩旗息鼓，益西走白羊山。

translations.literal: Xianzhong thus was able to trade salt, fodder, rice, and vinegar with the mountain people, gather the scattered, lower banners and silence drums, and press further west to Baiyang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He traded salt, grain, and vinegar with hill folk, regathered stragglers, marched silently, and slipped west to Baiyang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 時汝才及過天星從寧昌窺大昌、巫山，欲渡江，為官兵所扼。

translations.literal: At that time Luo Rucai and Guo Tianxing, from Ningchang, were scouting toward Dachang and Wushan, intending to cross the river, but were blocked by government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Rucai and Guo Tianxing had slipped out of Ningchang to probe Dachang and Wushan and cross the Yangtze, but government forces barred the way.

sentences.zh: 獻忠至，遂與之合。

translations.literal: When Xianzhong arrived, he joined them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong came up and the bands united.

sentences.zh: 獻忠雖累敗，氣益盛，立馬江岸，有不前赴者，輒戮之。

translations.literal: Though repeatedly defeated, Xianzhong's spirit only grew fiercer; he stood his horse on the riverbank and executed any who hesitated to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat after defeat only stoked Zhang Xianzhong's fury: on the riverbank he would cut down any man who hung back.

sentences.zh: 賊爭死鬥，官軍退走。

translations.literal: The bandits fought desperately; the government army fell back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fought as if glad to die, and the government lines broke.

sentences.zh: 賊畢渡，屯萬頃山，歸、巫大震。

translations.literal: The bandits crossed in full force and encamped on Mount Wanqing; Guizhou and Wushan were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Once every man was across, they camped on Mount Wanqing, and the regions of Guizhou and Wushan trembled.

sentences.zh: 已而汝才、過天星犯開縣不利，汝才東走，過天星復軼開縣而西。

translations.literal: Before long Luo Rucai and Guo Tianxing attacked Kaizhou without success; Rucai went east while Guo Tianxing again slipped past Kaizhou westward.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Rucai and Guo Tianxing struck Kaizhou and failed; Rucai veered east, Guo Tianxing slipped west of Kaizhou once more.

sentences.zh: 諸將往復追逐，獻忠乃悉眾攻楚兵於土地嶺，副將汪之鳳戰死。

translations.literal: Generals chased them back and forth; Xianzhong then hurled his entire force against Chu troops at Tudi Ridge, and Vice Commander Wang Zhifeng died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: While commanders wheeled and pursued, Xianzhong threw his whole host at Chu troops on Tudi Ridge; Vice Commander Wang Zhifeng fell.

sentences.zh: 遂陷大昌，進屯開縣，張令戰死，石砫女土司秦良玉亦敗。

translations.literal: He then took Dachang, advanced to encamp at Kaizhou—Zhang Ling fell in battle, and the female Tusi Qin Liangyu of Shizhu was also defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Dachang, pushed on to Kaizhou—Zhang Ling died fighting—and even Qin Liangyu, the woman Tusi of Shizhu, was beaten.

sentences.zh: 汝才復自東至，與獻忠轉趨達州。

translations.literal: Rucai came again from the east and, with Xianzhong, turned toward Dazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai returned from the east; he and Xianzhong swung toward Dazhou.

sentences.zh: 川撫邵捷春退扼涪江。

translations.literal: Sichuan Governor Shao Jiechun retreated to hold the Fu River.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan governor Shao Jiechun fell back to block the Fu River.

sentences.zh: 賊北陷劍州，將入漢中。

translations.literal: The bandits took Jianzhou in the north and were about to enter Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took Jianzhou northward and aimed for Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 總兵官趙光遠、賀人龍守陽平、百丈險。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Zhao Guangyuan and He Renlong held the Yangping and Baizhang passes.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Zhao Guangyuan and He Renlong guarded Yangping and the Baizhang narrows.

sentences.zh: 賊不得過，乃復走巴西。

translations.literal: Unable to pass, the bandits turned back into Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked, they doubled back into Baxi.

sentences.zh: 涪江師潰，捷春論死。

translations.literal: The Fu River army collapsed; Jiechun was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu River line collapsed; Jiechun was condemned to die.

sentences.zh: 獻忠屠綿州，越成都，陷滬州，北渡隱永川，走漢川、德陽，入巴州。

translations.literal: Xianzhong slaughtered Mianzhou, passed Chengdu, took Luzhou, crossed north into Yongchuan, and fled through Hannan and Deyang into Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong sacked Mianzhou, swept past Chengdu, seized Luzhou, forded north into Yongchuan, and fled through Hannan and Deyang into Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 又自巴走達州，復至開縣。

translations.literal: From Ba he went to Dazhou again, then returned to Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: From Ba he doubled to Dazhou, then came back to Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，嗣昌聞賊入川，進駐重慶。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sichang heard the bandits had entered Sichuan, he advanced to station at Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, hearing the rebels had entered Sichuan, Yang Sichang moved his headquarters to Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 監軍萬元吉曰：「賊或東突，不可無備，宜分中軍間道出梓潼，扼歸路。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wan Yuanji said: "The bandits may burst eastward—we cannot be unprepared; detach a central force by a side route through Zitong to cut off their line of retreat."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wan Yuanji urged: "They may bolt east—we must be ready. Send a central column by a hidden road through Zitong to sever their retreat."

sentences.zh: 嗣昌不聽，擬令諸將盡赴滬州追賊。

translations.literal: Sichang would not listen and planned to order all generals to Luzhou to pursue the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang refused and ordered every general to Luzhou in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，總兵猛如虎、參將劉士傑追之開縣之黃陵城，賊還戰，官軍大敗，士傑及遊擊郭開等皆死。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year, Commander Meng Ruhu and Deputy Liu Shijie pursued them to Huanglingcheng in Kaizhou; the bandits turned to fight and the government army was utterly defeated—Shijie and Guerrilla Commander Guo Kai and others all perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year, Meng Ruhu and Liu Shijie chased them to Huanglingcheng in Kaizhou; the rebels wheeled and shattered the government host—Shijie, Guerrilla Commander Guo Kai, and many more died.

sentences.zh: 獻忠果東出，令汝才拒鄖撫袁繼鹹兵，自率輕騎，一日夜馳三百里，殺督師使者于道，取軍符，紿陷襄陽城。

translations.literal: Xianzhong did burst east: he ordered Rucai to hold off Yuan Jixian's Yun troops, while he himself led light cavalry three hundred li in a day and night, killed the Grand Secretary's messenger on the road, seized the military tallies, and tricked his way into Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong did break east: Rucai held Yuan Jixian's Yun force at bay while he rode light three hundred li in a day and a night, slew the Grand Secretary's courier, seized the tallies, and duped his way into Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 獻忠縛襄王翊銘置堂下，屬之酒曰：「我欲借王頭，使楊嗣昌以陷籓誅，王其努力盡此酒。」

translations.literal: Xianzhong bound Prince Xiang Yi Ming at the hall and set wine before him, saying: "I mean to borrow your highness's head so that Yang Sichang may be executed for allowing an imperial prince to fall—drink this wine with all your might."
translations.idiomatic: He bound Prince Xiang, Yi Ming, set wine before him in the hall, and said: "I need your highness's head so Sichang may be put to death for losing a prince—drain this cup."

sentences.zh: 遂殺之，並殺鄖襄道張克儉、推官鄺曰廣，復得其所失妻妾。

translations.literal: He then killed him, together with Xiangyang Circuit Intendant Zhang Kejian and Assistant Magistrate Kuang Yueguang, and recovered the wives and concubines he had lost.
translations.idiomatic: Then he killed the prince, Xiangyang intendant Zhang Kejian, and assistant magistrate Kuang Yueguang, and took back the wives and concubines he had lost.

sentences.zh: 又去，陷樊城、當陽、郟。

translations.literal: He left again and took Fancheng, Dangyang, and Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on, seizing Fancheng, Dangyang, and Ye.

sentences.zh: 合汝才入光州，殘商城、羅山、息縣、信陽、固始。

translations.literal: Joining Rucai he entered Guangzhou and ravaged Shangcheng, Luoshan, Xixian, Xinyang, and Gushi.
translations.idiomatic: With Rucai he entered Guangzhou and laid waste to Shangcheng, Luoshan, Xixian, Xinyang, and Gushi.

sentences.zh: 分軍犯茶山、應城，陷隨州。

translations.literal: He sent detachments against Chashan and Yingcheng and took Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent columns against Chashan and Yingcheng and seized Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 偽張良玉幟，入泌陽。

translations.literal: Flying Zhang Liangyu's banners, he entered Biyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under false banners of Zhang Liangyu he entered Biyang.

sentences.zh: 再攻應山，不克，去。

translations.literal: He attacked Yingshan again but could not take it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Yingshan again, failed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 攻鄖陽，守將王光恩力戰，始解。

translations.literal: He attacked Yunyang; Garrison Commander Wang Guang'en fought fiercely until the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: At Yunyang, garrison commander Wang Guang'en fought so hard the siege broke.

sentences.zh: 又拔鄖西，群盜附者萬計，遂東略地。

translations.literal: He also took the west of Yun, and bandits flocking to him numbered in the tens of thousands; he then marched east to seize territory.
translations.idiomatic: He seized western Yun as well; tens of thousands of outlaws rallied to him, and he turned east to carve out ground.

sentences.zh: 獻忠自瑪瑙山之敗，心畏良玉，及屢勝，有驕色。

translations.literal: Since defeat at Mount Agate, Xianzhong had feared Liangyu; after many victories his manner grew arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Since Agate Mountain he had feared Liangyu; now, after repeated wins, pride overtook him.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，良玉追擊之信陽，大破之，降賊眾數萬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, Liangyu pursued him to Xinyang and routed him utterly, and tens of thousands of bandits surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Liangyu ran him down at Xinyang and broke him utterly; tens of thousands surrendered.

sentences.zh: 獻忠傷股，乘夜東奔，良玉急追之。

translations.literal: Xianzhong was wounded in the thigh, fled east by night, and Liangyu pressed close behind.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong took an arrow in the thigh and fled east by night; Liangyu clung to his heels.

sentences.zh: 會大雨，江溢道絕，官軍不能進，獻忠走免。

translations.literal: Heavy rain fell, rivers overflowed and roads were cut; the government army could not advance, and Xianzhong escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Rain flooded the rivers and severed the roads; the government host could not follow, and Xianzhong slipped away.

sentences.zh: 已，復出商城，將向英山，又為副將王允成所破，眾道散且盡，從騎止數十。

translations.literal: Later he emerged from Shangcheng again, intending to move on Yingshan, but was beaten again by Deputy Wang Yuncheng; his forces scattered almost entirely, and only several dozen horsemen remained at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Later he broke from Shangcheng toward Yingshan, was shattered again by deputy Wang Yuncheng, and his host melted away until only a few dozen riders remained.

sentences.zh: 時汝才已先與自成合，獻忠遂投自成。

translations.literal: By then Rucai had already joined Zicheng first; Xianzhong therefore threw in his lot with Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai had already thrown in with Zicheng; Xianzhong now cast his lot with him too.

sentences.zh: 自成以部曲遇之，不從。

translations.literal: Zicheng treated him as a subordinate officer; he would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng treated him as a subordinate; he refused.

sentences.zh: 自成欲殺之，汝才諫曰：「留之使擾漢南，分官軍兵力。」

translations.literal: Zicheng wished to kill him; Rucai remonstrated: "Keep him alive to harass southern Han and divide the government army's strength."
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng meant to kill him. Rucai pleaded: "Keep him to harry southern Han and split the government forces."

sentences.zh: 乃陰與獻忠五百騎，使遁去。

translations.literal: He then secretly gave Xianzhong five hundred horsemen and let him slip away.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he gave Xianzhong five hundred horse and let him escape.

sentences.zh: 道糾土賊一斗穀、瓦罐子等，眾復盛，然猶佯推自成。

translations.literal: On the road he gathered local bandits such as Yidougu and Waguanzi; his following swelled again, yet he still pretended to defer to Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he gathered hill bandits like Yidougu and Waguanzi; his ranks swelled again, yet he still feigned deference to Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，賊營革、左二賀陷含、巢、潛諸縣，欲西合獻忠，以湖廣官兵沮不得達。

translations.literal: Earlier, the rebel chiefs Ge and Zuo Erhe had taken Han, Chao, and Qian and wished to join Xianzhong in the west, but Huguang troops blocked the route.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the chiefs Ge and Zuo Erhe had seized Han, Chao, and Qian and meant to join Xianzhong in the west, but Huguang troops barred the way.

sentences.zh: 及汴圍急，督師丁啟睿及左良玉皆往援汴，獻忠乘間陷亳州，入英、霍山中，與革、左、二賀相見，皆大喜。

translations.literal: When the siege of Bian grew urgent, Grand Secretary Ding Qirui and Zuo Liangyu both went to relieve Bian; Xianzhong seized the interval to take Bozhou and enter the Ying and Huo mountains, where he met Ge, Zuo, and Erhe—all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian was hard pressed, Ding Qirui and Zuo Liangyu hurried to its relief; Xianzhong seized the gap, took Bozhou, and entered the Ying and Huo hills to meet Ge, Zuo, and Erhe—great was their joy.

sentences.zh: 明年合攻，陷舒城、六安，掠民益軍。

translations.literal: The next year they joined in attack, took Shucheng and Lu'an, and pressed the people into service.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they struck together, took Shucheng and Lu'an, and drove the people into the ranks.

sentences.zh: 陷廬州，知府鄭履祥死。

translations.literal: They took Luzhou; Prefect Zheng Luxiang died.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Luzhou; prefect Zheng Luxiang died.

sentences.zh: 陷無為、廬江，習水師於巢湖。

translations.literal: They took Wuwei and Lujiang and drilled a navy on Chaohu Lake.
translations.idiomatic: They took Wuwei and Lujiang and trained a fleet on Chaohu.

sentences.zh: 太監盧九德以總兵官黃得功、劉良佐之兵戰於夾山，敗績，江南大震。

translations.literal: Eunuch Lu Jiude fought with commanders Huang Degong and Liu Liangzuo at Jiashan and was defeated; Jiangnan was convulsed.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Lu Jiude met Huang Degong and Liu Liangzuo at Jiashan and was beaten; all Jiangnan shook.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽總督高鬥光、安慶巡撫鄭二陽逮治，詔起馬士英代鬥光。

translations.literal: Fengyang Governor Gao Douguang and Anqing Governor Zheng Eryang were arrested and tried; the court recalled Ma Shiying to replace Douguang.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang governor Gao Douguang and Anqing governor Zheng Eryang were seized and tried; Ma Shiying was summoned to replace Douguang.

sentences.zh: 是秋，得功、良佐大破賊於潛山，獻忠腹心婦豎盡走蘄水，革、左二賀北投自成。

translations.literal: That autumn, Degong and Liangzuo routed the bandits at Qianshan; Xianzhong's inner circle of women and boys all fled to Qishui, and Ge, Zuo, and Erhe went north to Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Degong and Liangzuo crushed the rebels at Qianshan; Xianzhong's women and boys fled to Qishui, and Ge, Zuo, and Erhe went north to Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 已，獻忠復襲陷太湖。

translations.literal: Before long Xianzhong again stormed and took Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xianzhong stormed Taihu again.

sentences.zh: 會良玉避自成東下，盡撤湖廣兵自從。

translations.literal: Liangyu, evading Zicheng's eastward drive, withdrew all Huguang troops to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu, sidestepping Zicheng's eastward march, pulled every Huguang soldier after him.

sentences.zh: 獻忠聞之，又襲陷黃梅。

translations.literal: On hearing this, Xianzhong again stormed Huangmei.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of it, Xianzhong struck Huangmei once more.

sentences.zh: 十六年春，連陷廣濟、蘄州、蘄水。

translations.literal: In spring of the sixteenth year he took Guangji, Qizhou, and Qishui in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixteenth year he seized Guangji, Qizhou, and Qishui in turn.

sentences.zh: 入黃州，黃民盡逃，乃驅婦女鏟城，尋殺之以填塹。

translations.literal: Entering Huangzhou, the people fled entirely; he drove women to dig the ramparts, then killed them to fill the moats.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangzhou the people had all fled; he forced women to dig the walls, then slew them to fill the ditches.

sentences.zh: 麻城人湯志者，大姓奴也，殺諸生六十人，以城降賊。

translations.literal: Tang Zhi of Macheng, a bondsman of a great clan, killed sixty licentiates and surrendered the city to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhi of Macheng—a great family's bondsman—killed sixty students and opened the city to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 獻中改麻城為州。

translations.literal: Xianzhong renamed Macheng a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong made Macheng a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又西陷漢陽，全軍從鴨蛋洲渡，陷武昌，執楚王華奎，籠而沈諸江，盡殺楚宗室。

translations.literal: He went west and took Hanyang; the whole army crossed from Yadanzhou and took Wuchang, seized Prince Chu Hua Kui, caged him, and sank him in the river; he killed every member of the Chu imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: He drove west, seized Hanyang, and the whole host crossed from Yadanzhou to take Wuchang. He seized Prince Chu Hua Kui, caged him, and sank him in the river, and slaughtered the entire Chu imperial house.

sentences.zh: 錄男子二十以下、十五以上為兵，餘皆殺之。

translations.literal: Males twenty and under and fifteen and over were enrolled as soldiers; the rest were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Boys from fifteen to twenty were pressed into the ranks; all others were killed.

sentences.zh: 由鸚鵡洲至道士洑，浮胔蔽江，逾月人脂厚累寸，魚鱉不可食。

translations.literal: From Parrot Isle to Daoshifu, corpses choked the river; for more than a month human fat lay inches thick and fish and turtles were unfit to eat.
translations.idiomatic: From Parrot Isle to Daoshifu the dead clogged the river; for a month human grease lay inches deep, and fish and turtles could not be eaten.

sentences.zh: 獻忠遂僭號，改武昌曰天授府，江夏曰上江縣。

translations.literal: Xianzhong then usurped the title, renaming Wuchang Heavenly Bestowed Prefecture and Jiangxia Shangjiang County.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong then took the throne, renaming Wuchang Heavenly Bestowed Prefecture and Jiangxia Shangjiang County.

sentences.zh: 據楚王第，鑄西王之寶，偽設尚書、都督、巡撫等官，開科取士。

translations.literal: He occupied the Prince of Chu's mansion, cast the seal of Western King, and falsely appointed ministers, grand marshals, governors, and the like, and held the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the Chu palace, cast the Western King's seal, set up false ministers, grand marshals, and governors, and held examinations.

sentences.zh: 以興國州柯、陳兩姓土官悍勇，招降之。

translations.literal: Because the native officers of the Ke and Chen clans of Xingguo prefecture were fierce, he summoned them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Ke and Chen native officers of Xingguo were fierce fighters; he called them to submit.

sentences.zh: 題詩黃鶴樓。

translations.literal: He inscribed a poem on the Yellow Crane Tower.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a poem on the Yellow Crane Tower.

sentences.zh: 下令發楚邸金振饑民。

translations.literal: He ordered the treasure stored in the Chu palace opened to relieve starving people.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Chu palace treasuries opened to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 蘄、黃等二十一州縣悉附。

translations.literal: Twenty-one prefectures and counties including Qi and Huang all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one prefectures and counties, Qi and Huang among them, submitted.

sentences.zh: 時李自成在襄陽，聞之忌且怒，貽書譙責。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zicheng was at Xiangyang; on hearing this he was jealous and enraged and sent a letter of reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng was at Xiangyang; hearing of it he burned with envy and sent a scolding letter.

sentences.zh: 左良玉兵復西上，偽官吏多被擒殺。

translations.literal: Zuo Liangyu's troops advanced west again; many false officials were captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu's army marched west again; false officials were seized and killed in droves.

sentences.zh: 獻忠懼，乃悉眾趨岳州、長沙。

translations.literal: Xianzhong grew afraid and marched his whole force toward Yuezhou and Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid, Xianzhong drove his whole host toward Yuezhou and Changsha.

sentences.zh: 於是監軍道王瓆、沔陽知州章曠、武昌生員程天一、白雲寨長易道三皆起兵討賊，蘄、黃、漢陽三府皆反正。

translations.literal: Then Military Inspector Wang Zhi, Mianyang Magistrate Zhang Kuang, Wuchang student Cheng Tianyi, and White Cloud Stockade chief Yi Daosan all raised troops against the bandits; Qishui, Huang, and Hanyang prefectures all returned to the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Then military inspector Wang Zhi, Mianyang magistrate Zhang Kuang, Wuchang student Cheng Tianyi, and White Cloud stockade chief Yi Daosan all rose against the rebels; Qishui, Huang, and Hanyang turned back to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 獻忠遂陷咸甯、蒲圻，逼岳州。

translations.literal: Xianzhong then took Xianning and Puci and pressed on Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong seized Xianning and Puci and closed on Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 沅撫李乾德、總兵孔希貴等據城陵磯拒戰，三戰三克，殲其前部。

translations.literal: Hunan Governor Li Qiande and Commander Kong Xigui held Chenglingji and fought them off; three battles, three victories, destroying his vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan governor Li Qiande and commander Kong Xigui held Chenglingji and beat them back three times, destroying his van.

sentences.zh: 獻忠怒，百道並進，乾德等不支，皆走，岳州陷。

translations.literal: Xianzhong raged and advanced on a hundred fronts; Qiande and the others could not hold; they all fled and Yuezhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong raged and pressed on a hundred roads; Qiande could not stand and fled—Yuezhou fell.

sentences.zh: 獻忠欲渡洞庭湖，卜於神，不吉，投珓而訽。

translations.literal: Xianzhong wished to cross Dongting Lake; he divined before the god—ill omens—and cursed as he cast the blocks.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to cross Dongting and divined to the god; the omens were bad, and he cursed as he cast the lots.

sentences.zh: 將渡，風大作，獻忠怒，連巨舟千艘，載婦女焚之，水光夜如晝。

translations.literal: When he was about to cross, a great wind rose; enraged, he chained a thousand great boats laden with women and burned them; the water glowed at night like day.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to cross, a gale rose. In fury he chained a thousand great boats full of women and burned them; the lake blazed through the night like noon.

sentences.zh: 騎而逼長沙，巡按劉熙祚奉吉王、惠王走衡州，總兵尹先民降，長沙陷。

translations.literal: He rode hard against Changsha; Censor Liu Xizuo escorted the Ji and Hui princes to Hengzhou; Commander Yin Xianmin surrendered and Changsha fell.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped on Changsha. Censor Liu Xizuo bore the Ji and Hui princes to Hengzhou; commander Yin Xianmin surrendered, and Changsha fell.

sentences.zh: 尋破衡州，吉王、惠王、桂王俱走永州。

translations.literal: Soon he took Hengzhou; the Ji, Hui, and Gui princes all fled to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took Hengzhou; the Ji, Hui, and Gui princes fled to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 乃拆桂府材，載至長沙，造偽殿，而自追三王於永。

translations.literal: He stripped timber from the Gui prince's mansion, shipped it to Changsha to build a false palace, and himself pursued the three princes toward Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He tore down the Gui palace for timber, rafted it to Changsha to build a false hall, and himself chased the three princes toward Yong.

sentences.zh: 熙祚命中軍護三王入廣西，身入永死守，城陷見殺。

translations.literal: Xizuo ordered the central army to conduct the three princes into Guangxi; he entered Yong to hold it to the death, and when the city fell he was slain.
translations.idiomatic: Xizuo sent the central army to escort the three princes into Guangxi; he entered Yong to die defending it and was killed when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 又陷寶慶、常德，發故督師楊嗣昌祖墓，斬其屍見血。

translations.literal: He also took Shaoyang and Changde, opened the ancestral tomb of the late Grand Secretary Yang Sichang, and severed the corpse until it bled.
translations.idiomatic: He took Shaoyang and Changde, opened Grand Secretary Yang Sichang's tomb, and hacked the corpse until blood ran.

sentences.zh: 攻道州，守備沈至緒戰歿，其女再戰，奪父屍還，城獲全。

translations.literal: He attacked Daozhou; Garrison Commander Shen Zhixu died in battle; his daughter fought twice more, recovered her father's body, and the city was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: At Daozhou garrison commander Shen Zhixu fell; his daughter fought twice more, bore her father's body back, and the city held.

sentences.zh: 遂東犯江西，陷吉安、袁州、建昌、撫州、永新、安福、萬載、南豐諸府縣。

translations.literal: He then invaded Jiangxi eastward, taking Ji'an, Yuanzhou, Jianchang, Fuzhou, Yongxin, Anfu, Wanzai, Nanfeng, and other prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He turned east into Jiangxi, seizing Ji'an, Yuanzhou, Jianchang, Fuzhou, Yongxin, Anfu, Wanzai, Nanfeng, and more.

sentences.zh: 廣東大震，南、韶屬城官民盡逃。

translations.literal: Guangdong was shaken; cities of Nan and Shao saw officials and people flee entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong shook; in Nan and Shao officials and people fled to the last man.

sentences.zh: 賊有獻計取吳、越者，獻忠憚良玉在，不聽，決策入川中。

translations.literal: Someone offered a plan to seize Wu and Yue; Xianzhong, fearing Liangyu, would not heed it and decided to enter the Sichuan basin.
translations.idiomatic: One man urged him to take Wu and Yue; fearing Liangyu, Xianzhong would not listen and chose to enter Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十七年春陷夔州，至萬縣，水漲，留屯三月。

translations.literal: In spring of the seventeenth year he took Kuizhou, reached Wanxian; the water rose and he camped three months.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year he took Kuizhou and reached Wanxian; floods held him there three months.

sentences.zh: 已，破涪州，敗守道劉麟長、總兵曾英兵。

translations.literal: Before long he took Fuzhou, defeating Circuit Defender Liu Linchang and Commander Zeng Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took Fuzhou, beating circuit defender Liu Linchang and commander Zeng Ying.

sentences.zh: 進陷佛圖關。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Fotuguan.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on and seized Fotuguan.

sentences.zh: 破重慶，瑞王常浩遇害。

translations.literal: He took Chongqing; Prince Rui Chang Hao perished.
translations.idiomatic: He took Chongqing; Prince Rui Chang Hao died.

sentences.zh: 是日，天無雲而雷，賊有震者。

translations.literal: That day thunder rolled though the sky was cloudless; some bandits were struck.
translations.idiomatic: That day thunder pealed under a clear sky; some rebels were struck dead.

sentences.zh: 獻忠怒，發巨砲與天角。

translations.literal: Xianzhong raged and fired great cannon at Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong raged and turned great guns on the sky.

sentences.zh: 遂進陷成都，蜀王至澍率妃、夫人以下投于井，巡撫龍文光被殺。

translations.literal: He then advanced and took Chengdu; Prince Shu Zhi Shu led consorts and ladies below to cast themselves into a well; Governor Long Wenguang was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Chengdu. Prince Shu Zhi Shu led consorts and ladies into a well; governor Long Wenguang was slain.

sentences.zh: 是時我大清兵已定京師，李自成遁歸西安。

translations.literal: By then our Great Qing army had secured the capital; Li Zicheng had fled back to Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Great Qing had taken the capital; Li Zicheng had fled to Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 南京諸臣尊立福王，命故大學士王應熊督川、湖軍事，兵力弱，不能討賊。

translations.literal: The ministers at Nanjing enthroned the Prince of Fu and ordered former Grand Secretary Wang Yingxiong to direct Sichuan-Huguang military affairs, but his forces were weak and could not suppress the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing ministers enthroned the Prince of Fu and set former grand secretary Wang Yingxiong over Sichuan and Huguang, but his forces were too weak to crush the rebels.

sentences.zh: 獻忠遂僭號大西國王，改元大順，冬十一月庚寅，即偽位，以蜀王府為宮，名成都曰西京。

translations.literal: Xianzhong then usurped the title King of the Great Western State, changed the era name to Dashun; in the eleventh month, on gengyin day, he ascended the false throne, made the Shu princely mansion his palace, and renamed Chengdu Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong declared himself king of the Great Western State, took the era name Dashun, and in the eleventh month on the day gengyin mounted the false throne, made the Shu palace his hall, and called Chengdu Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 用汪兆麟為左丞相，嚴錫命為右丞相。

translations.literal: He appointed Wang Zhaolin Left Chancellor and Yan Timing Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He made Wang Zhaolin left chancellor and Yan Timing right chancellor.

sentences.zh: 設六部五軍都督府等官，王國麟、江鼎鎮、龔完敬等為尚書。

translations.literal: He established six ministries, a grand marshal's headquarters, and the like; Wang Guolin, Jiang Dingzhen, Gong Wanjing, and others became ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He set up six ministries and a grand marshal's office; Wang Guolin, Jiang Dingzhen, Gong Wanjing, and others became ministers.

sentences.zh: 養子孫可望、艾能奇、劉文秀、李定國等皆為將軍，賜姓張氏，分徇諸府州縣，悉陷之。

translations.literal: Adopted sons Sun Kewang, Ai Nengqi, Liu Wenxiu, Li Dingguo, and others were all made generals, given the surname Zhang, and sent to overrun prefectures and counties—all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Adopted sons Sun Kewang, Ai Nengqi, Liu Wenxiu, and Li Dingguo were made generals, given the surname Zhang, and sent to overrun the provinces—all fell.

sentences.zh: 保甯、順慶先已降自成，置官吏，獻忠悉逐去。

translations.literal: Baoning and Shunqing had already surrendered to Zicheng and received officials; Xianzhong drove them all out.
translations.idiomatic: Baoning and Shunqing had already submitted to Zicheng and taken his officials; Xianzhong expelled them all.

sentences.zh: 自成發兵攻，不克，遂據有全蜀。

translations.literal: Zicheng sent troops to attack but could not prevail; Xianzhong thus held all of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng sent troops but could not break him; Xianzhong held all Shu.

sentences.zh: 惟遵義一郡及黎州土司馬金堅不下。

translations.literal: Only Zunyi prefecture and the native officer of Lizhou, Ma Jin, held out and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zunyi and Lizhou native officer Ma Jin held out and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 獻忠黃面長身虎頷，人號黃虎。

translations.literal: Xianzhong had a sallow face, tall frame, and tiger jaw; men called him Yellow Tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong was sallow, long of body, tiger-jawed; men called him Yellow Tiger.

sentences.zh: 性狡譎，嗜殺，一日不殺人，輒悒悒不樂。

translations.literal: By nature cunning and treacherous, addicted to killing—if he did not kill someone in a day, he grew sulky and joyless.
translations.idiomatic: Cunning and murderous by nature—if he killed no one in a day, he grew dark and restless.

sentences.zh: 詭開科取士，集于青羊宮，盡殺之，筆墨成丘塚。

translations.literal: He falsely announced the civil examinations and assembled candidates at Qingyang Palace, then killed them all; brushes and ink formed hillocks like burial mounds.
translations.idiomatic: He lured scholars to examinations at Qingyang Palace and slaughtered them all; pens and ink piled like graves.

sentences.zh: 坑成都民於中園。

translations.literal: He buried the people of Chengdu alive in the central park.
translations.idiomatic: He buried the people of Chengdu alive in the central park.

sentences.zh: 殺各衛籍軍九十八萬。

translations.literal: He killed ninety-eight myriad registered troops of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: He killed nine hundred eighty thousand registered guard troops.

sentences.zh: 又遣四將軍分屠各府縣，名草殺。

translations.literal: He sent four generals to massacre each prefecture and county in turn—called "grass slaughter."
translations.idiomatic: He sent four generals to massacre every prefecture and county—a slaughter called "mowing the grass."

sentences.zh: 偽官朝會拜伏，呼獒數十下殿，獒所嗅者，引出斬之，名天殺。

translations.literal: At false court levees, officials kowtowed; he released dozens of mastiffs down the hall, and whom the dogs scented was led out and beheaded—called "heaven's slaughter."
translations.idiomatic: At false court audiences, officials kowtowed; he loosed mastiffs down the hall, and whom the dogs sniffed was dragged out and killed—"heaven's slaughter."

sentences.zh: 又創生剝皮法，皮未去而先絕者，刑者抵死。

translations.literal: He also devised live-flaying; if the skin was not yet removed when the victim died, the executioner was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: He invented flaying alive; if the skin was not off before the victim died, the flayer was executed.

sentences.zh: 將卒以殺人多少敘功次，共殺男女六萬萬有奇。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers were ranked by how many they killed; men and women slain numbered more than six hundred thousand odd.
translations.idiomatic: Officers were promoted by the body count; men and women killed exceeded six hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 賊將有不忍至縊死者。

translations.literal: Some bandit generals could not bear it and hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Some rebel generals could not bear it and hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 偽都督張君用、王明等數十人，皆坐殺人少，剝皮死，並屠其家。

translations.literal: False grand marshals Zhang Junyong, Wang Ming, and several tens of others were all flayed alive for killing too few, and their families were slaughtered too.
translations.idiomatic: False grand marshals Zhang Junyong, Wang Ming, and dozens more were flayed for killing too few, and their families were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 脅川中士大夫使受偽職，敘州布政使尹伸、廣元給事中吳宇英不屈死。

translations.literal: He coerced Sichuan scholar-officials into taking false office; Pacification Commissioner Yin Shen of Yizhou and Supervising Secretary Wu Yuying of Guangyuan died refusing.
translations.idiomatic: He forced Sichuan gentry into office; pacification commissioner Yin Shen of Yizhou and supervising secretary Wu Yuying of Guangyuan died refusing.

sentences.zh: 諸受職者，後尋亦皆見殺。

translations.literal: Those who did accept office were later hunted down and killed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Those who took office were hunted down and killed in turn.

sentences.zh: 其慘虐無人理，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: His atrocities defied human reckoning and cannot all be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: His cruelties passed human telling and cannot all be written.

sentences.zh: 又用法移錦江，涸而闕之，深數丈，埋金寶億萬計，然後決堤放流，名水藏，曰：「無為後人有也。」

translations.literal: He also diverted the Jin River, drained it, and dug it several fathoms deep, burying treasure beyond counting in hundred-millions, then breached the dike to let the water flow back—called "water burial," saying: "Let there be nothing left for those who come after."
translations.idiomatic: He dammed the Jin River, drained it, and dug it deep, burying treasure beyond count, then broke the dike to flood it back—"water burial," he said: "Let nothing remain for those who come after."

sentences.zh: 當是時，曾英、李占春、于大海、王祥、楊展、曹勳等議兵並起，故獻忠誅殺益毒。

translations.literal: At that time Zeng Ying, Li Zhanchun, Yu Dahai, Wang Xiang, Yang Zhan, Cao Xun, and others mustered troops together, so Xianzhong's slaughter grew even more venomous.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zeng Ying, Li Zhanchun, Yu Dahai, Wang Xiang, Yang Zhan, Cao Xun, and others raised arms, and Xianzhong's killing grew fouler still.

sentences.zh: 川中民盡，乃謀窺西安。

translations.literal: When the people of Sichuan were exhausted, he turned to covet Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan was emptied of people, he cast his eye on Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，獻忠盡焚成都宮殿廬舍，夷其城，率眾出川北，又欲盡殺川兵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, Xianzhong burned every palace and dwelling in Chengdu, razed the city, and led his host north out of Sichuan; he again intended to massacre all Sichuan troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3, Xianzhong burned Chengdu's palaces and houses, leveled the city, and marched north out of Sichuan; he meant again to slaughter every Sichuan soldier.

sentences.zh: 偽將劉進忠故統川兵，聞之，率一軍逃。

translations.literal: The false general Liu Jinzhong had formerly commanded Sichuan troops; hearing this, he fled with an army.
translations.idiomatic: False general Liu Jinzhong had once led Sichuan troops; hearing this, he deserted with his command.

sentences.zh: 會我大清兵至漢中，進忠來奔，乞為鄉導。

translations.literal: When our Great Qing army reached Hanzhong, Jinzhong came over and begged to serve as guide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Qing reached Hanzhong, Jinzhong came in and offered to guide them.

sentences.zh: 至鹽亭界，大霧。

translations.literal: At the Yanting border, a great fog.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yanting border, fog swallowed the land.

sentences.zh: 獻忠曉行，猝遇我兵於鳳凰坡，中矢墜馬，蒲伏積薪下。

translations.literal: Xianzhong marched at dawn, suddenly met our army at Fenghuang Slope, was struck by an arrow and fell from his horse, and crawled under a pile of firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong marched at dawn, met our troops at Fenghuang Slope, took an arrow, fell from his horse, and crawled under a stack of firewood.

sentences.zh: 於是我兵擒獻忠出，斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon our army dragged Xianzhong out and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Our troops dragged him out and struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 川中自遭獻忠亂，列城內雜樹成拱，狗食人肉若猛獸虎豹，齧人死輒棄去，不盡食也。

translations.literal: After Xianzhong's devastation in Sichuan, trees within the walled cities grew as thick as arms; dogs ate human flesh like tigers and leopards—when they had gnawed a man dead they cast the corpse aside without finishing it.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianzhong's ravaging of Sichuan, trees in the cities grew wrist-thick; dogs ate men like tigers, and when a man was dead they left the corpse half eaten.

sentences.zh: 民逃深山中，草衣不食久，遍體皆生毛。

translations.literal: People fled deep into the mountains, wearing grass and eating nothing for so long that hair grew over their whole bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors hid deep in the hills, clothed in grass, starved so long that hair covered their bodies.

sentences.zh: 獻忠既誅，賊黨可望、能奇、文秀、定國等潰入川南，殺曾英、李乾德等，後皆降于永明王。

translations.literal: After Xianzhong was executed, his followers Kewang, Nengqi, Wenxiu, Dingguo, and the rest scattered into southern Sichuan, killed Zeng Ying, Li Qiande, and others, and later all surrendered to the Prince of Yongming.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianzhong's death, Kewang, Nengqi, Wenxiu, Dingguo, and the rest broke into southern Sichuan, killed Zeng Ying and Li Qiande, and later surrendered to the Prince of Yongming.
